### Turra Coo

The **Turra Coo** ([Doric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doric_dialect_%28Scotland%29) for "the Turriff Cow") was a white [Ayrshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrshire_cattle)-[Shorthorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shorthorn) cross [dairy cow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dairy_cow) which lived near the [Aberdeenshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeenshire) town of [Turriff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turriff) in north-east Scotland in the early twentieth century. The cow became famous following a dispute between her owner, supported by local people, against the government over [taxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax) and compulsory [national insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_insurance).

#### Background

Under the [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_%28UK%29) government of the 1910s, the [Chancellor of the Exchequer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_of_the_Exchequer) [David Lloyd George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lloyd_George) introduced a scheme whereby [National Insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Insurance) contributions (by employer) became compulsory for all workers between the ages of 16 and 70. This was enacted via the [National Insurance Act 1911](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Insurance_Act_1911), and caused outrage among the farmers local to Turriff, who claimed that their contributions were too high; and that, as they were rarely able to be off work due to illness like industrial workers, it was unfair for them to have to pay for a service they were unlikely to use.[^2336]

In Turriff, popular protests were held in the Johnston and Paterson Mart, and Lendrum farmer Robert Paterson refused to stamp the insurance cards of his employees. Paterson was charged under the National Insurance Act and sentenced to pay a fine of £15 plus the arrears of national insurance contributions. Paterson paid the fine, but refused to make up the arrears, resulting in orders on 13 November 1913 for Turriff's [Sheriff Officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheriff_Officer) George Keith to seize property to the value of £7 (equivalent to £698.35 in 2025) from Paterson's farm. However, this was more difficult than it seemed as officers could not move property without local assistance, and the locals refused to help in protest.

#### The cow

Sheriff Officer George Keith [poinded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poinding) the only piece of property which was easily mobile: Paterson's white milk cow, which was set to be sold in Turriff on 9 December, the delay being due to the fact that both of Turriff's agricultural marts supported Paterson and refused to handle the sale, requiring a special licence to be granted for a public sale and an auctioneer to be brought in from elsewhere.

On the appointed day, the cow was taken from Paterson's farm and led to Turriff on foot. The denizens of Turriff found the cow tied in the village square, decorated in ribbons and painted with the words 'Lendrum to [Leeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_symbols_of_Wales)' in reference to Lloyd George's [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales) origin, and representing the Sheriff Officer's and government's victory over the hostile farmers. The cow was put up for [auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auction). The response was a near [riot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot), and a 100-strong mob proceeded to pelt the sheriff officers with rotten fruit and [soot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soot). Amidst the melee, the cow herself escaped from her handler and ran away, later being found in a nearby barn. Eight farm workers, including Paterson, were subsequently put on trial in Aberdeen for disorderly conduct but all were acquitted, having received verdicts of "[not proven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_proven)".

The cow was eventually taken to [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen) where it was sold to a farmer, Alexander Craig, for £7, but Bryony Miller, a local girl and wife of the Patersons' farmhand John Miller, with his help, rallied the local community together to buy back the cow for Lendrum. The presentation of the cow back to the Patersons on 20 January 1914 was a major public event; it was estimated that more than 3,000 people turned out to see the cow paraded in triumph through Turriff, adorned with ribbons and garlands of dried flowers, painted with the slogan "Free!! Divn't ye wish that ye were me" and accompanied by a band playing "[See the Conquering Hero Comes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judas_Maccabaeus_%28Handel%29)". The cow returned to the Patersons' farm at Lendrum, where she died six years later and was buried in a corner of the farmland.

#### The cow in film

A film was made of the cow. This was shown at both The Gaiety and Coliseum cinemas in Aberdeen in February 1914. These were operated by [William Dove Paterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Dove_Paterson) "who took the film to Turriff for a special show in aid of the Parish Church renovation scheme, and to the Victoria Hall, Ellon, where great cheers and applause greeted the appearance on screen of several well-known farmers."[^2337]

#### Sculpture and commemoration

The case became a *[cause celebre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cause_celebre)* at the time and numerous souvenir items were produced featuring likenesses of the Coo and frequently adorned with the slogan "Lendrum to Leeks".

The foghorn of [Girdle Ness Lighthouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girdle_Ness_Lighthouse) was nicknamed the 'Torry Coo', as an allusion to the cow, and the horn's cow-like bellow.

On 31 October 1971, a roadside monument was unveiled at Lendrum, with a plaque featuring a silhouette of a cow's head and the words "The Famous 'Turra Coo' incident took place in 1913 when Robert Paterson headed resistance to injustice to farm workers in the insurance act."

On 20 November 2010, a sculpture of the Turra Coo by David Blyth, Charles Engebretsen and Ginny Hutchinson was unveiled in Turriff town centre, at the junction of the two major shopping streets, a spot now known locally as "Coo Corner".[^2338] The sculpture was based on a stuffed cow known as "Alese" and bearing a strong resemblance to photographs of the original Turra Coo. Alese herself is on display at the Aberdeenshire Farming Museum in [Mintlaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mintlaw).

The centenary was officially marked in Turriff on 16 November 2013, with various events revolving around a dramatic re-enactment of the story.[^2339]

In 2014, the town's [Highland League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Football_League) football club, [Turriff United F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turriff_United_F.C.), adopted a mascot based on the Turra Coo (though unlike the original, the mascot is usually referred to as male).

### Diving horse

A **diving horse** is an attraction that was popular in North America from the mid-1880s[^2340] till the mid-20th century and occasionally thereafter, in which a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) would be dropped headfirst into a pool of water, sometimes from as high as 60 feet.[^2341]

#### History

[William "Doc" Carver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Frank_Carver) "invented" horse-diving exhibitions. Allegedly, in 1881 Carver was crossing a bridge over [Platte River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platte_River) ([Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska)) when it partially collapsed. His horse fell in divelike manner into the waters below, inspiring Carver to develop the diving horse act. He trained various animals and went on tour. His son, Al Floyd Carver, constructed the ramp and tower, and Lorena Carver was the first rider. [Sonora Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonora_Webster_Carver) joined the show in 1924 and later married Al Floyd Carver. The show became a permanent fixture at [Atlantic City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City)'s popular venue [Steel Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_Pier). There, Sonora, Al and Lorena continued the show following his death.

In 1931, Sonora and her horse Red Lips lost their balance on the platform. Sonora survived the fall, but was permanently blinded by [detached retinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_detachment) in both eyes as a result of keeping her eyes open. She continued horse-diving until 1942 and later wrote a memoir, published as *[A Girl and Five Brave Horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Girl_and_Five_Brave_Horses)*. A film loosely based on her life, *[Wild Hearts Can't Be Broken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Hearts_Can't_Be_Broken)*, was released in 1991.[^2342]

In [Lake George, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_George_%28town%29,_New_York), the [Magic Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Forest) theme park hosted a diving horse feature beginning in 1977, originally featuring a horse named Rex, later replaced by a [gelding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelding) named Lightning. The manager stated, "There is no rider, no prods, no electrical jolts, and no trap doors."[^2343] The theme park was purchased in 2018[^2344] and re-opened as Lake George Expedition Park, without horse diving.

#### Animal welfare

A horse-diving show was an in-residence act held at New Jersey's [Steel Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_Pier). Pressure from [animal-rights activists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_rights_movement) and declining demand led to the act being shuttered in the 1970s. Although there was a brief resumption of the act at the pier in 1993, it was again shut down amid opposition.[^2340][^2345] The horses sometimes dived four times a day, seven days a week.[^2341] An attempt in 2012 to revive the shows at Steel Pier was halted when animal-welfare advocates petitioned the owners not to hold the shows. [Wayne Pacelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Pacelle), then president of the [Humane Society of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humane_Society_of_the_United_States) stated: "This is a merciful end to a colossally stupid idea."[^2346]

#### Loading of the pier

Atlantic City's Steel Pier was also used to mount a measuring device ([tide gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tide_gauge)) to monitor changes in the sea level of the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean). However, changes in sea level at the pier turned out to have been caused by the weight of the crowds gathered to watch the diving horses. Measurements from 1929 to 1978 indicated [sea level rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise) - when the crowds were regular and caused the pier to settle slightly in the soft, sandy bottom - except during the horse-jumping hiatus from 1945 to 1953 when the lack of regular crowds allowed the pier to rise slightly.[^2347]

### Rhinogradentia

**Rhinogradentia** is a fictitious [order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_%28biology%29) of [extinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction) [shrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrew)-like [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal) invented by German [zoologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoologist) [Gerolf Steiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerolf_Steiner). Members of the order, known as **rhinogrades** or **snouters**, are characterized by a [nose-like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nose) feature called a "nasorium", which evolved to fulfill a wide variety of functions in different species. Steiner also created a fictional persona, [naturalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalist) Harald Stümpke, who is credited as author of the 1961 book *Bau und Leben der Rhinogradentia* (translated into English in 1967 as *The Snouters: Form and Life of the Rhinogrades*). According to Steiner, it is the only remaining record of the animals, which were wiped out, along with all the world's Rhinogradentia researchers, when the small Pacific [archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago) they inhabited sank into the ocean due to nearby atomic bomb testing.

Successfully mimicking a genuine scientific work, Rhinogradentia has appeared in several publications without any note of its fictitious nature, sometimes in connection with [April Fools' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_Fools'_Day).

#### Background

Rhinogradentia, their island home of Hy-yi-yi, zoologist Harald Stümpke, and a host of other people, places, and documents are fictional creations of [Gerolf Steiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerolf_Steiner) (1908-2009), a German zoologist. Steiner is best known for his fictional work as Stümpke, but he was an accomplished zoologist in his own right. He held a professorship at the [University of Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Heidelberg) and later the [Technical University of Karlsruhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_University_of_Karlsruhe), where he occupied the department chair from 1962 to 1973.[^2348]

Steiner was also interested in illustration, and in 1945 drew a picture for one of his students as thanks for some food. He took inspiration from a short [nonsense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonsense) poem by [Christian Morgenstern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Morgenstern), *[The Nasobame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nasobame)* (*Das Nasobēm*) about an animal that walked using its nose. He took to the drawing, made a copy for himself, and later incorporated the creatures into his teaching.[^2349] According to [Bud Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Webster), Steiner's motivation for writing a book about them was instructional, to illustrate "how animals evolve in isolation", but Joe Cain speculates that the success of the joke may have led to a teaching and writing career based on that rather than the other way around.[^2350][^2349]

#### Harald Stümpke's account

Steiner's fictional author, credited as "quondam curator of the Museum of the Darwin Institute of Hy-yi-yi, Mairuwili", provides a very detailed account of the order and individual species, written in a dry, scholarly tone.[^2351] Michael Ohl wrote that the book is written "in truly amusing attention to detail and using what is immediately recognizable as a practiced scientific patois".[^2352] The evidently expert voice of the author, his competent writing, and apparent familiarity with conventions of academic literature set the work apart as a rare example at the intersection of fiction and scholarship.[^2353] Steiner credits himself by name as illustrator of the book, and explains how that role led him to possess the only remaining record of Rhinogradentia.[^2354]

##### Discovery and study at Hy-yi-yi

According to Stümpke, Rhinogradentia were native to Hy-yi-yi, a small [Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean) [archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago) comprising eighteen islands: Annoorussawubbissy, Awkoavussa, Hiddudify, Koavussa, Lowlukha, Lownunnoia, Mara, Miroovilly, Mittuddinna, Naty, Nawissy, Noorubbissy, Osovitissy, Ownavussa, Owsuddowsa, Shanelukha, Towteng-Awko, and Vinsy. The islands occupied 1,690 km² (650 sq mi) and the archipelago's highest peak, 2,230 m (7,320 ft), was on its main island, Hiddudify (Hy-dud-dye-fee).[^2354]

The first description of Hy-yi-yi published in Europe was that of Einar Pettersson-Skämtkvist, a Swedish explorer who arrived in Hiddudify by chance in 1941, after escaping from a Japanese [prisoner-of-war camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner-of-war_camp).[^2354][^2353][^2355] Each of the islands was home to distinctive fauna, dominated by Rhinogradentia, the only mammals other than humans and one species of shrew. In the time after the war, a number of scientists took interest in the rhinogrades and began formal research into their physiology, morphology, behaviors, and evolution.[^2355]

In the late 1950s, nearby [nuclear weapons testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_testing) by the [United States military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_military) accidentally caused all of the islands of Hy-yi-yi to sink into the ocean, destroying all traces of the rhinogrades and their unique [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem). Also killed were all the world's Rhinogradentia researchers, who were attending a conference on Hy-yi-yi at the time.[^2354][^2353] The book's epilogue, credited to Steiner in his capacity as the book's illustrator, explains that Stümpke had sent the book's materials to Steiner to serve as the basis for illustrations in preparation for publication. Following the disaster, it is the only remaining record of the subjects it describes.[^2351]

##### Biological characteristics and behavior

Rhinogrades are [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal) characterized by a nose-like feature called a "nasorium", the form and function of which vary significantly between species.[^2351][^2354] According to Stümpke, the order's remarkable variety was the natural outcome of [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) acting over millions of years in the remote Hy-yi-yi islands. All the 14 [families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_%28taxonomy%29) and 189 known snouter [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) descended from a small [shrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrew)-like animal, which gradually evolved and diversified to fill most of the [ecological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) niches in the archipelago, from tiny worm-like beings to large herbivores and predators.[^2351]

Many rhinogrades used their nose for locomotion, for example the "snout leapers" like *Hopsorrhinus aureus*, whose nasorium was used for jumping, or the "earwings" like *Otopteryx*, which flew backwards by flapping its ears and used its nose as a [rudder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudder).[^2349] Some species used their nasorium for catching food, for example by using it to [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing) or to attract and trap insects.[^2356] Other species included the fierce *Tyrannonasus imperator* and the shaggy *Mammontops*.[^2357][^2358][^2359][^2360]

Pettersson-Skämtkvist's early descriptions of the animals he encountered on Hy-yi-yi led zoologists to name them after the title creature in Christian Morgenstern's *The Nasobame*.[^2352] In the poem, which exists outside of this fictional universe and also served as an inspiration for Steiner, the Nasobame is seen "striding on its noses" (*auf seinen Nasen schreitet*).[^2356][^2361]

##### Genera

Stümpke's book classifies 138 species of rhinograde in the following fictitious [genera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus):[^2354][^2362]

- *Archirrhinos*
- *Cephalanthus*
- *Columnifax*
- *Corbulonasus*
- *Dulcicauda*
- *Eledonopsis*
- *Emunctator*
- *Enterorrhinus*
- *Hexanthus*
- *Holorrhinus*
- *Hopsorrhinus*
- *Larvanasus*
- *Liliopsis*
- *Mammontops*
- *Mercatorrhinus*
- *Nasobema*
- *Nasolimaceus*
- *Nudirhinus*
- *Orchidiopsis*
- *Otopteryx*
- *Phyllohopla*
- *Ranunculonasus*
- *Remanonasus*
- *Rhinochilopus*
- *Rhinolimacius*
- *Rhinosiphonia*
- *Rhinostentor*
- *Rhinotaenia*
- *Rhinotalpa*
- *Rhizoidonasus*
- *Stella*
- *Tyrannonasus*

The names generally refer to particular forms or functions of the nasorium of animals in that genus, typically providing vernacular names for clarity.[^2352]

#### Publication history

Steiner's books as Stümpke have been translated into other languages, sometimes crediting other names based on the country of publication. "Harald Stümpke", "Massimo Pandolfi", "Hararuto Shutyunpuke", and "Karl D. S. Geeste" are pseudonyms. Translator names are real.

#### Legacy

Rhinogradentia is considered one of the best known biological [hoaxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoax) and [scientific jokes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody_science) and Steiner's pseudonymous works on the subject continue to be reprinted and translated.[^2363][^2364][^2365][^2349] The first edition did not explicitly state that it was a hoax.

Following the publication of the French translation, [George Gaylord Simpson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gaylord_Simpson) wrote a seemingly serious review which extended the hoax in a 1963 issue of the journal *[Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_%28journal%29)*, taking issue with the way Stümpke named the animals as "criminal violations of the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature". Simpson also noted that Stümpke neglected to include an unrelated mathematical concept, a "rotated matrix".[^2352]

Since the book's original publication several scientists and publishers have written about Rhinogradentia as though Steiner's account were true, though it is unclear how many of those who continued and popularized the joke did so intentionally. Wulf Ankle wrote that the order "is not a poetic invention, but has really lived".[^2356] Rolf Siewing's *Zoology Primer* lists them as an order of mammal, noting that their existence is doubted.[^2352] [Erich von Holst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_von_Holst) celebrated the discovery of "a completely new animal world".[^2356] Timothy E. Lawlor's widely read textbook *Handbook to the Orders and Families of Living Mammals* includes an entry for Rhinogradentia that does not acknowledge its fictional nature.[^2363][^2366][^2367] The East German *Liberal-Demokratische Zeitung* took note of the nuclear demise of the rhinogrades, writing that they would still be alive "had we, the peaceable powers, managed in time to implement widespread disarmament and prohibit the production and testing of nuclear weapons."[^2352]

Prior to the publication of Leigh Chadwick's English translation, an abbreviated version ran in the April 1967 edition of *[Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_History_%28magazine%29)*, a magazine published by the [American Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Museum_of_Natural_History). It comprised material from the book's introduction, first chapter, selected descriptions of genera, and the epilogue, and was presented as the lead story, without qualification, by the normally serious publication.[^2360][^2368] The following month, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times)* ran a story about the snouters on the front page, based on the *Natural History* article. According to the magazine's editorial director, they had "received more than 100 letters and telegraphs about the snouters, most of them from people who forgot that the article was published on April Fool's Day."[^2360] *Natural History* printed several letters to the editor in its June-July issue, and conveyed to the *Times* the content of several more, ranging from skeptical to fascinated and continuations of the joke.[^2360][^2368] One reader, entomologist [Alice Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Gray), expressed thanks for the article, which enabled her family to identify an animal-shaped metal bracelet from the South Pacific as having been modeled after a "Hoop Snouter", and included a drawing to preserve the record because, she said, it had been melted down with some toy soldiers and a spoon by a young cousin with a new casting set.[^2360][^2368]

Decades later, papers are still published purporting to continue Stümpke's research or otherwise paying homage to Steiner's hoax. In a 2004 paper in the *Russian Journal of Marine Biology*, authors Kashkina & Bukashkina claim to have discovered two new marine genera: *Dendronasus* and an as yet unnamed parasitic taxon.[^2369][^2370] The Max Planck Institute for Limnology announced a new species discovered in the [Großer Plöner See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gro%C3%9Fer_Pl%C3%B6ner_See).[^2352] On [April Fools' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_Fools'_Day) in 2012, the [National Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Natural_History_%28France%29) in France announced the discovery of a wood-eating [termite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Termite)-like genus, *Nasoperferator*, with a rotating nose resembling a [drill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drill).[^2371][^2372]

Rhinogradentia has been included in a number of museum exhibitions and collections. The National Museum of Natural History's *Nasoperferator* announcement was accompanied by a two-month exhibit honoring the animals, featuring purported stuffed specimens in its gallery of extinct species.[^2373] Mock [taxidermies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxidermy) of rhinogrades have also been included in an exhibit at the [Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mus%C3%A9e_d'ethnographie_de_Neuch%C3%A2tel),[^2374] and in the permanent collections of the [Musée zoologique de la ville de Strasbourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mus%C3%A9e_zoologique_de_la_ville_de_Strasbourg) and the [Salzburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salzburg) [Haus der Natur](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haus%20der%20Natur%20Salzburg).[^2375][^2376][^2349]

Three real species have been named after Steiner and Stümpke: *Rhinogradentia steineri*, a [snout moth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyralidae),[^2377] *[Hyorhinomys stuempkei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyorhinomys_stuempkei)*, a shrew rat also known as the Sulawesi snouter,[^2378][^2379] and *[Tateomys rhinogradoides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tateomys_rhinogradoides)*, the Tate's shrew rat.[^2380]

### Fungie

**Fungie** (/ˈfʌŋɡi/), also known as the **Dingle Dolphin**,[^2381] was a male [common bottlenose dolphin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_bottlenose_dolphin). He became separated from other wild dolphins and lived in very close contact with the people of [Dingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingle) on the southwest coast of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland).[^2382][^2383]

Wild bottlenose dolphins are estimated to have a median lifespan between 8.3 and 17.4 years, while one has been observed to live for at least 67 years.[^2384] Fungie was first seen in Dingle harbour in 1983 and continued to seek out human contact over the following 37 years. Therefore, Fungie was fully grown and likely already in his middle or even old age at the time of his disappearance in October 2020.[^2385] By 2019, it was estimated that he was at least 40 years of age and [Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records) declared him to be the oldest solitary wild dolphin in the world.[^2386][^2387] His long life led to rumours that the original Fungie had died and been replaced with a lookalike to avoid damage to tourism. However, this idea was dismissed by locals, who pointed out that a dolphin introduced to the harbour would simply leave, as it would not be possible to train a newly introduced dolphin to stay within it.[^2388][^2389]

Fungie was known to interact playfully with swimmers, surfers, kayakers, and divers in the water. There were no recorded cases of Fungie being aggressive towards humans. Although it is normal for social animals such as dolphins to live in close contact with each other, it is still a rare occurrence for them to seek out human contact, and Fungie is the first recorded occurrence of a dolphin interacting positively with humans in the wild in Ireland. Fungie had been frequently observed eating [garfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garfish), prey not previously known to be eaten by dolphins.[^2390]

In 2020, there was concern for his welfare after he had gone missing for several days, having last been seen on 13 October.[^2391] Marine experts have declared that he either moved on to new waters or simply died, and reported sightings by the general public after 15 October were dismissed as "well-intentioned, but incorrect".[^2392]

### Mayor Max II

**Maximus Mighty-Dog Mueller II** (May 6, 2013 - July 30, 2022) was a [Golden Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Retriever) dog who served as the second unofficial mayor of Idyllwild, part of the [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place) of [Idyllwild-Pine Cove, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idyllwild%E2%80%93Pine_Cove,_California). His deputy mayors, Mitzi and Mikey, were his cousins.[^2393] After his death Mayor Max II was succeeded by his cousin Max III, who was sworn in on December 10, 2022.[^2394]

#### Mayoralty

In 2012, the non-profit organization Idyllwild Animal Rescue Friends (ARF) hosted an "election" for mayor of Idyllwild (which, as part of an unincorporated community, has no local government) as part of a fundraising event for the organization. Fourteen dogs and two cats ran, and Max, a [Golden Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Retriever), was elected as Idyllwild's first mayor. On April 2, 2013, Mayor Max died, and Maximus Mighty-Dog Mueller II, another Golden Retriever, arrived in Idyllwild on July 21 to complete the remainder of the term.[^2395] In March 2014, as the end of Max's term approached, ARF solicited the town's interest in holding another election. The people overwhelmingly pled for Mayor Max's continuation in perpetuity.[^2396][^2394]

Mayor Max was recognized by the [County of Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Riverside), California.[^2397] The mayor's duties included visiting with locals and out-of-town visitors, attending business grand openings and other town functions, participating in the town's two annual parades, and promoting Idyllwild.[^2398] Max's popularity had spread the world over, and he has represented the town through appearances on news programs, talk shows, advertisements, billboards, and a game show.[^2399]

#### Death

Mayor Max was hospitalized and died in Temecula, California on July 30, 2022. He was succeeded by [Mayor Max III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_Max_III), who formally took office on December 10, 2022.[^2400][^2401]

### Stubbs (cat)

**Stubbs** (April 12, 1997 - July 21, 2017) was a [cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat) who was the honorary [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor) of [Talkeetna, Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkeetna,_Alaska), from July 18, 1997, until his death in 2017. Stubbs was described as a [tourist attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourist_attraction), having been flooded with cards and letters, and drawing 30 to 40 tourists each day who hoped to meet the mayor of [Talkeetna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkeetna,_Alaska). His position was honorary, as the town is only a [historic district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_districts_in_the_United_States). Every afternoon, Stubbs went to a nearby restaurant and drank water mixed with [catnip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catnip) out of a wine or margarita glass. Stubbs died in 2017 at the age of 20.

#### Early life

Stubbs was born on April 12, 1997, in [Talkeetna, Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkeetna,_Alaska).[^2402] Later in 1997, Lauri Stec, manager of Nagley's General Store, found Stubbs in a box full of kittens in her parking lot.[^2403] The owners were giving the kittens away; Stec chose "Stubbs" because he did not have a tail.[^2404]

#### Political career

Stubbs became the mayor of [Talkeetna, Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkeetna,_Alaska) on July 18, 1997.[^2405] Stubbs was widely described as having been elected after a [write-in campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Write-in_candidate) by voters who opposed the human candidates,[^2406] but [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR) pointed out that this could not have happened because "the tiny town has no real mayor, so there was no election."[^2407] Nagley's General Store was used as Stubbs's "mayoral office" during his tenure.[^2404]

Stubbs was featured in an effort to protest the [2014 United States Senate election in Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_United_States_Senate_election_in_Alaska) when people urged voters to write Stubbs in on the ballot.[^2408] Stubbs was featured in a video criticizing both the Democratic and Republican candidates for Senate.[^2408] One opinion writer for the *[Alaska Dispatch News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Dispatch_News)* insisted that the whole story was false, and that Talkeetna did not have a cat mayor.[^2409]

##### As a tourist attraction

Stubbs was described as a [tourist attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourist_attraction),[^2410] having been flooded with cards and letters, and drawing 30 to 40 tourists each day (most of whom were en route to other Alaska destinations, such as [Denali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denali))[^2411] who hoped to meet the mayor of [Talkeetna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkeetna,_Alaska). His position was honorary, as the town is only a [historic district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_districts_in_the_United_States).[^2412] Every afternoon, Stubbs went to a nearby restaurant and drank water mixed with [catnip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catnip) out of a wine[^2404][^2413] or margarita glass.[^2414]

##### Attacks

On August 31, 2013, Stubbs was attacked by a dog.[^2403][^2415] He was placed under heavy sedation at a veterinary hospital 70 miles (110 km) away in [Wasilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasilla,_Alaska), having suffered a punctured lung, a fractured sternum, and a deep cut in his side.[^2403][^2416] A [crowd-funding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowd-funding) page was set up to help pay his veterinary bills.[^2417] Stubbs remained in the veterinary hospital for nine days before returning to the upstairs room of the general store.[^2418] As a result, he was discouraged from roaming. Donations toward his care were received from around the world; the surplus was given to an animal shelter and to the local veterinary clinic.[^2413]

Other incidents included Stubbs being shot by teenagers with [BB guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BB_gun), falling into a restaurant's deep fryer (which was switched off and cold at the time), and hitching a ride to the outskirts of Talkeetna on a garbage truck.[^2418]

#### Later life and death

In 2015, Stubbs was growing older and thus slowed down his public presence.[^2419] He died on July 21, 2017.[^2402][^2420] His owners said that "He was a trooper until the end of his life."[^2419] Stubbs's owners have suggested that another family cat, Denali, may assume Talkeetna's "mayoralty".[^2421]

### Aptostichus barackobamai

***Aptostichus barackobamai*** (also known as the **Barack Obama trapdoor spider**) is a large [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of [trapdoor spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapdoor_spider) in the [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_%28taxonomy%29) [Euctenizidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euctenizidae) named after the [44th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Presidents_of_the_United_States) President of the United States, [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama). The species was first reported by [Jason Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bond) of [Auburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University) in December 2012 as one of 33 new species of the [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) *[Aptostichus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aptostichus)*. The species is endemic throughout northern California, forming burrows out of silk, dirt, and sand, from which it attacks prey. This spider is identified by its dark red to red-brown coloration with a stripped or chevron patterned abdomen. Breeding occurs during the winter and females tend to be larger than their male counterparts. *A. barackobamai* is part of the larger *Aptostichus icenoglei* [species complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_complex), and is a close relative to *Aptostichus icenoglei* and *Aptostichus isabella*.

#### Taxonomy

*Aptostichus barackobamai* is a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) of [trapdoor spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_trapdoor_spiders) within the [Euctenizidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euctenizidae) family.[^2422] The species was first [described](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_description) by [Jason Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bond), director of the [Auburn University Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University), in December 2012. The [specific name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specific_name_%28zoology%29), *barackobamai*, is in honor of former United States president [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama). *A. barackobamai* was one of 33 new species of the [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) *[Aptostichus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aptostichus)* described in Bond's paper, many of which are named after famous individuals.[^2423][^2424] *Aptostichus barackobamai* is one of many [species named after Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_things_named_after_Barack_Obama), and is also known as the Barack Obama trapdoor spider.[^2423][^2424][^2425]

##### Species group and evolution

*Aptostichus barackobamai*, *Aptostichus icenoglei,* and *Aptostichus isabella* are all members of the *Aptostichus icenoglei* [species complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_complex). *A barackobamai* was likely the first member of this species group to diverge following the uplift of the [Transverse Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_Ranges) in California approximately 5 million years ago, isolating the ancestral species and prevented any further [gene flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_flow). Despite this, all three species demonstrate [niche conservatism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_niche_conservatism) between each other, particularly in their [habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) preferences. The following [cladogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cladogram) shows the [phylogenetic position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogeny) of *A. barackobamai* among the members of the *Aptostichus icenoglei* species complex based upon [ancestral reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancestral_reconstruction), along with an assessment of 403 [loci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_%28genetics%29):[^2426][^2427]

|     | Aptostichus barackobamai Aptostichus isabella Aptostichus icenoglei |
|-----|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

#### Description

*Aptostichus barackobamai* is a species of large, [sexually dimorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_dimorphism) spiders. Males' legs, [carapaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carapace), and [chelicerae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelicerae) are a dark red color. Their [abdomen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen) is a red-brown with [mottled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mottle) stripes running [dorsally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location). The [cephalothorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalothorax)'s carapace is 5.94 centimetres (2.34 in) long and 5.06 centimetres (1.99 in) wide. Their cephalothorax is covered in white [setae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seta), has short black bristles along the outside edges, and the topside of the cephalothorax is smooth. The foveal groove is narrow, deep, and slightly curved forward. Their eyes are slightly raised relative to the head. The posterior sternal sigilla are moderately sized, non-contiguous, and positioned close to the margin. The anterior sigilla are smaller, oval, and also close to the margins. The chelicerae consist of a row of six [denticles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denticle_%28tooth_feature%29), and the palpal endites have one cuspule along its edge. The rastellum (a rake-like burrowing part of the jaw) is made up of 6 spines. The abdomen is covered in thick and fine black setae. The legs are covered heavily in [scopulae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scopulae). The [pedipalp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedipalp) is slender and lacking in spines. The [palpal bulb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palpal_bulb) is broad at its base, spineless, and tapers to a sharp point.[^2423]

Females differ from the males in that their carapace, legs, and chelicerae tend to be a red-brown color and their abdomen has a mottled [chevron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevron_%28insignia%29) pattern. Females tend to be larger, their cephalothorax's carapace is 8 centimetres (3.1 in) long and 6.88 centimetres (2.71 in) wide. Their cephalothorax is covered with both black and white intermingled setae but the outside edges lack setae. Their chelicerae consist of eight teeth and the palpal endites have twelve cuspules. The rastellium has 7 short spines all in a row that extend out and upwards. The female's anterior legs are more slender than their posterior pair. Their [spermathecal bulbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatheca) form a long, curved stalk.[^2423]

*Aptostichus barackobamai* can be differentiated from other *Aptostichus* species by the male's spination pattern, which is offset proximally. Additionally, the male metatarsal mating [apophysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms) is a triangular shape. Females have a spermathecal bulb located along the medial auxiliary segment, unlike other members of the genus. *Aptostichus isabella* is the closest in appearance to *A. barackobamai* but have a rectangular mating apophysis instead.[^2423]

##### Behavior

*A. barackobamai* burrows underground for shelter, making waterproof 'trapdoor' structures out of soil, sand, and webbing. From these burrows, the spider will strike at [prey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predation), a common behavior among [trapdoor spiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_trapdoor_spiders).[^2427][^2424][^2425] [Breeding season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonal_breeder) occurs during the winter months. Spiders may go longer periods of time without feeding to better [camouflage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camouflage) themselves.[^2428]

#### Distribution

*Aptostichus barackobamai* is a species [endemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism) to California,[^2429] and has been observed at several locations in the northern part of the state. Originally, the species was believed to be isolated to the locality of [Hopland, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopland,_California), due to its apparent rarity, but specimen have since been found throughout [north-central California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_California). Particular locations where populations are known to exist are [Mendocino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendocino_County,_California), [Napa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County,_California), [Shasta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shasta_County,_California), [Sutter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutter_County,_California), and [Tehama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehama_County,_California) counties. Geographically, these include the [Mayacamas Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayacamas_Mountains), the [Sutter Buttes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutter_Buttes), parts of the [California Floristic Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Floristic_Province), and the northernmost ridges of the Central Valley. While no specimen have been found yet to corroborate a wider distribution, predictions by Jason Bond estimate that the species likely inhabits the majority of the Central Valley and its eastern mountain ranges.[^2423]

*A. barackobamai's* habitat consists of mixed [redwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequoioideae) and [coniferous forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conifer).[^2423] Their [microhabitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat) is mainly shady, north-facing slopes.[^2427]

##### Conservation status

Due to the wide range and abundance of *A. barackobamai*'s population, the species is not considered to be [threatened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threatened_species), overall. Jason Bond, during his initial description of the species, postulated that some isolated populations (such as those local to the Sutter Buttes) may be threatened.[^2423]

### Mini (frog)

***Mini*** is a [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of tiny [microhylid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microhylid) frogs that are [endemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemic) to southeastern [Madagascar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madagascar) where they live among [leaf litter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_litter) in lowland forests. The three species and the genus itself were first [scientifically described](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientifically_described) in 2019 by [Mark Scherz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Scherz). Although not yet rated by the [IUCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IUCN), they have very small ranges and it has been recommended that two qualify as [critically endangered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critically_endangered) and *M. ature* as [data deficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_deficient).[^2430][^2431]

At about 8-11.5 mm (0.31-0.45 in) in [snout-vent length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snout%E2%80%93vent_length), *M. mum* and *M. scule* are two of the world's [smallest frogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallest_organisms), and the larger *M. ature* is only c. 15 mm (0.6 in).[^2430][^2431][^2432][^2433] They were formerly confused with *[Stumpffia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stumpffia)*, another genus of tiny frogs from Madagascar. All are well-[camouflaged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camouflage) brown frogs.[^2430]

#### Species

The genus name is derived from English prefix "mini-", denoting a small version of an object. All the binomials names are examples of [wordplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_play) as they sound like words for small in English. There are currently 3 species:[^2430]

- *[Mini ature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_ature)* Scherz *et al.*, 2019
- *[Mini mum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_mum)* Scherz *et al.*, 2019
- *[Mini scule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini_scule)* Scherz *et al.*, 2019

#### Description

Diminutive terrestrial frogs (adult SVL 8.2-14.9 mm) with divided [vomers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vomer), [procoelous vertebral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procoelous_Vertebrae) column, divided sphenethmoids, and genetic affinities. Skin smooth to slightly granular, occasionally iridescent. A lateral colour border is present but varies in intensity among species. Highly reduced fingers and toes, fusion or loss of carpal 2, and paedomorphic skull morphology: laterally displaced narrow nasals, teeth absent from vomer, in some species present on the maxilla and premaxilla, otic capsule sometimes dorsally ossified, brain case comprising most of the skull's length and width.[^2430]

#### Distribution and habitation

The genus *Mini* is endemic to low-elevation habitats (0-350 m a. s. l.) of southeastern Madagascar.[^2430]

### Zyzyxia

***Zyzyxia*** is a genus of tropical shrubs in the family [Asteraceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteraceae) native to Central America.[^2434][^2435] There is only one known species, ***Zyzyxia lundellii***.[^2436][^2437]

#### Description and distribution

*Zyzyxia* is a shrub that grows to 3 meters tall. Its leaves are covered in very rough [hairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trichome). The ray and disc [petals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petal) are both yellow, and the fruits are brown.

All known collections of *Zyzyxia* come from [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala) and [Belize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belize). There, the shrubs grow in dry tropical forests of [pine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine) or ericaceous [scrub forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrubland).[^2438]

#### Naming

Around 1990, John L. Strother was revising the six [North American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America) [genera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of the subtribe Ecliptinae in the sunflower family ([Asteraceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteraceae)) for publication in *[Systematic Botany Monographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematic_Botany)*. He carefully examined species in the genus *[Wedelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedelia)*, and decided that "something was looking odd and different" in some of the specimens. For one, the [achenes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achene) ([fruits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit)) did not have a thin winged membrane around the edge as other species in the genus were supposed to have. Strother decided that the plant was actually a new and previously unnamed [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus) of plant.

By this time, the lengthy [monograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monograph) he had written was in the final stages of proofing for publication. His editor insisted that the genera be treated alphabetically, and to insert a new genus in the middle of his 100-page treatment would mean numerous changes to the format and layout of the article. The only way the editor would accept the new genus was if it were placed alphabetically after the last genus in the article, *[Zexmenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zexmenia)*. This would put it nearly at the end of the article, and minimize the changes needed for publication.

Knowing this, Strother decided he might as well make the genus the last one likely ever to exist in any list, and named the plant *Zyzyxia*.[^2434]

[^2434]: Strother, John L. (1991). Taxonomy of *Complaya, Elaphandra, Iogeton, Jefea, Wamalchitamia, Wedelia, Zexmenia*, and *Zyzyxia* (Compositae - Heliantheae - Ecliptinae). Systematic Botany Monographs 33: 91-93. ISBN 0-912861-33-9.

### Tree of Knowledge (Australia)

The **Tree of Knowledge** was a heritage-listed tree in Oak Street, [Barcaldine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcaldine,_Queensland), [Barcaldine Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcaldine_Region), [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland), Australia, that was poisoned and killed in 2006. It was a 200-year-old *[Corymbia aparrerinja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corymbia_aparrerinja)* ghost gum.[^2439] It was added to the [Queensland Heritage Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Heritage_Register) on 21 October 1992.[^2440]

The town was the headquarters of the [1891 Australian shearers' strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1891_Australian_shearers'_strike) and the tree was the site of the 1892 reading of the Labour Party manifesto leading to the formation of the [Australian Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party) (ALP).[^2441]

#### History

The Tree of Knowledge was a [ghost gum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_gum) located in front of the [Barcaldine railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcaldine_railway_station,_Queensland) under which the workers of the 1891 Shearer's Strike met. An icon of the Labor Party and Trades Unions, it symbolises the foundation of the organised representation of labour in Queensland.[^2440]

Barcaldine sprang up in 1886 as the terminus of the [Central Western railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Western_railway_line,_Queensland). The area was already settled by [pastoralists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoral_farming) and had previously been centred on [Blackall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackall,_Queensland). Large sheep stations were like small townships with their own working facilities, stores, worker's accommodation and tradesmen such as blacksmiths. The owners and managers of these stations had considerable power to dictate terms to an itinerant workforce of [sheep shearers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep_shearer) recruited for the shearing season. Poor working conditions, low pay and the threat of competition from cheap foreign labour caused discontent within the industry.[^2440]

Barcaldine was a natural focus for the development of unionism. As the railhead, the town drew many seasonal and casual workers. Besides shearers and hands there were navvies who had worked on the construction of the railway and carriers who had found their work reduced by it. Difficulties in finding work and financial hardship helped to build a sense of mateship and mutual support amongst sections of them. In 1887, the Central Queensland Carriers Union was formed, and discussions leading up to this are said to have been held under the gum tree which provided shade where carriers waited at the front of the railway station. At the same time, the [Queensland Shearers' Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Shearers_Union) was formed at Blackall. Within a year, it had 1,300 members, indicating a perceived need for collective bargaining to obtain fair pay and working conditions. In 1888, the Central Queensland Labourers' Union was formed at Barcaldine. These three unions were the driving force behind the strike of 1891.[^2440]

In [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane), the [Trades and Labour Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trades_and_Labour_Council_of_Queensland) was formed in 1885 and in 1889 became the Australian Labour Federation. At Barcaldine in the same year the Pastoral Employers' Association was founded in response and moved to reduce pay rates. Many workers now joined the unions, pushing membership of the Shearers Union over 3000 and the Labourer's Union to 2,250. Only severe wet weather in 1890 delayed a confrontation. By January 1891 union representatives had gathered at Barcaldine for meetings and pastoralists were pressing shearers to sign freedom of contract forms. A [strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_action) was called and employers began to import non-union labour from the south. Strikers, some of whom were armed, gathered at Barcaldine and set up a camp at Lagoon Creek and other places around the town.[^2442][^2440]

The [Queensland Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Government) dispatched police and soldiers to the area and the strikers responded by [drilling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_parade) and staging [torchlight processions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torchlight_procession) in the town. As the non-union labour, police, and soldiers usually arrived by rail, strikers would rally outside the railway station to block their arrival and protest. Consequently, the tree in front of the station, the Tree of Knowledge, was the location of many meetings and a focus for protest.[^2442] In March 1891, the situation escalated as carriers and railway workers [went out in sympathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solidarity_action) and military reinforcements arrived. Barcaldine became the focus of the whole country's interest and armed conflict was expected. However, heavy rain which limited movement and the arrest of leaders slowed momentum and strikers began to disperse. On 15 June, the strike was officially called off. It had failed, but was to have far-reaching effects. In 1892, at the foot of the tree, the Manifesto of the Queensland Labour Party dated 9 September 1892 was read out, leading to the formation of the Labor Party in Queensland.[^2440][^2443] The manifesto is considered one of the foundation documents of the current [Australian Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party)[^2444] and is now held by the [State Library of Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Library_of_Queensland).[^2445] In 2008, the manifesto was added to UNESCO's [Memory of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_of_the_World_Programme) Australian Register and in 2009, the document was added to UNESCO's Memory of the World International Register.[^2446]

Because the area beneath the Tree of Knowledge was the scene of actions and decisions which had a profound effect on the future of labour and politics in Australia, it has become an icon of the Labor Party and Trades Unions. It is also important to the people of Barcaldine as a symbol of the town's identity and historical importance. This is reflected by the name chosen for the commemoration committee formed in 1987, the Tree of Knowledge Development Committee, and by the care given to the tree. In 1990, it was discovered that the tree was infested by termites and other insects and had severe health problems. Treatment by a tree surgeon, pest control and flushing of the root system with thousands of litres of water gave the tree a new lease of life. This treatment was completed in late 1993.[^2440]

In 1991, there were major celebrations at Barcaldine to mark the centenary of the Shearers' Strike. In preparation for this, the area around the tree was landscaped and a memorial to the strikers erected within the enclosure.[^2440]

In 2006, the tree was poisoned with [glyphosate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyphosate) (a main ingredient in the [herbicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbicide) [RoundUp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RoundUp)). An [arborist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arborist) declared the tree dead on 3 October 2006. The ALP offered a reward of A\$10,000 for any information that would help identify those responsible. The remains of the tree were removed on 29 July 2007. According to a Queensland Government release,[^2447] the tree's wood underwent preservation with the remains of the tree - 7 metres (23 ft) tall and 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) across - being transferred to a special preservation facility.

Several cuttings propagated from the tree before its death are now growing in Barcaldine. In 2008, the tree was successfully [cloned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloning) in by workers at the former [Queensland Department of Primary Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Department_of_Primary_Industries).[^2448] A clone of the tree has also been planted at the Ecosciences Precinct in Brisbane.[^2449]

A new memorial on the site of the remains of the original tree (costing about A\$5M) was officially opened on 2 May 2009.[^2450] The memorial designed by Brian Hooper Architect & m3architecture (architects in association), won The Lachlan Macquarie Award for Heritage Architecture and a National Commendation for Public Architecture at the 2010 National Architecture Awards of the [Australian Institute of Architects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Institute_of_Architects).[^2451]

In 2009, as part of the [Q150](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q150) celebrations, the Tree of Knowledge was also announced as one of the [Q150 Icons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q150_Icons) of Queensland for its role as a "location".[^2452]

On 19 April 2011 Prime Minister [Julia Gillard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Gillard) joined ACT Chief Minister [Jon Stanhope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stanhope) at the [National Arboretum Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Arboretum_Canberra) in a ceremonial planting of a tree grown from an original cutting of the Tree of Knowledge.[^2453][^2454]

#### Description

The Tree of Knowledge is a ghost gum (*[Corymbia aparrerinja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corymbia_aparrerinja)*[^2455]) situated outside the railway station in the main street of Barcaldine. Early photographs show a wider canopy than existed at the time of the tree's demise. At the foot of the tree is a plaque which says:

> This plaque commemorates the loyalty, courage, and sacrifice in 1891 of the stalwart men and women of the west from whom, beneath this tree, emerged Australia's labour and political movement.[^2440]

The Tree of Knowledge is protected by a modern metal fence and the area surrounding it is bordered by a low rail composed of evenly spaced lengths of log and is landscaped with flowering shrubs. This area also contains a flagpole and a bronze and granite monument symbolising shear blades which was erected in 1991 to commemorate the centenary of the Shearer's Strike.[^2440]

#### Heritage listing

Tree of Knowledge was listed on the [Queensland Heritage Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Heritage_Register) on 21 October 1992 having satisfied the following criteria.[^2440]

**The place is important in demonstrating the evolution or pattern of Queensland's history.**

The Tree of Knowledge was a key site during the Shearer's Strike in 1891, a confrontation between capital and labour that was a major event in Queensland's history. The strike was a watershed in the development of the labour movement and the formation of the Australian Labor Party.[^2440]

**The place has a strong or special association with a particular community or cultural group for social, cultural or spiritual reasons.**

The Tree of Knowledge is closely linked with the cultural identity of Barcaldine and has a strong association with its people.[^2440]

**The place has a special association with the life or work of a particular person, group or organisation of importance in Queensland's history.**

The Tree of Knowledge has a special association with the history of the Australian Labor Party and with the Trades Union movement in Queensland.[^2440]

### Concealing objects in a book

There are many real and fictitious occurrences of **concealing objects in a book**. Items can be concealed in [books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book) in a number of ways. Small items such as a photograph or a note can be hidden in between the pages of the book. Thicker items can be hidden by removing the interior portion of some or all of the pages, creating a **book [safe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe)** or **hollowed-out book**. Book safes are easy for their owners to recognise, but they do not stand out to a thief or other intruder.

Another type of concealment is the hiding of messages in the text or on a book's pages by printing in code - a form of [steganography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steganography). For example, letters could be underlined on sequential pages, with the letters spelling out a message or code. There are a number of actual and fictional examples of items or messages having been concealed in a book.

Illicit chemicals may be smuggled by soaking individual pages with them.

Books are used as a [concealment device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concealment_device) in part because they are readily available and inconspicuous in many settings.

#### Methods of concealment

##### Hollow book safes

Book safes (also known as dummy books or faux books) are designed to imitate a real book by appearance to deceive people, some books may be whole with empty pages, others may be hollow or in other cases, there may be a whole panel carved with spines which are then painted to look like books, titles of some books may also be fictitious.

Prices can vary based on the cost of materials, additional features, and resources used to create the functionality and aesthetics of the hollow book. The main functional purpose aims for the containment of valuables, memorable items, or contraband within the cloak of an ordinary book. Thus maintaining privacy and security from unwanted intrusions and/or theft.

The scale of gadgetry used to create the seal of a hollow book's closing properties have ranged from simple to complex. Simple elastic bands, interlocking rope, and other common book closing techniques are used. Other times, hidden magnets do the task as well as the unusual use of complex locking mechanisms that require a lock and key combinations have also been used to keep a book closed.

Material choices used in the creation of the hollow book's body are usually actual books. However, other plastic, metal, cardboard, or paper materials have also been used to either simulate a real book, or to be used as extra features.

Many book safes are handmade. Structures made from real books are sealed and pressed before hollowing the inside pages with a sharp cutting utility. Sealing the back and allowing the front cover to act as a door that can be opened and shut. While other hollow books are made from cardboard cigar boxes, simulating a book on the outside.

There are many reasons to have dummy books on display such as; to allude visitors of the vast wealth of information in their possession and to inflate the owner's appearance of wealth, to conceal something,[^2456] for shop displays or for decorative purposes.

#### Choice of book

In fictional uses of book safes, the title or subject of the book can be symbolic or related to the nature of the object, e.g., hidden money in a copy of *[The Wealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wealth_of_Nations)*. There are a number of cases from films and television series where an item is hidden in the [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible).

In early 19th century at [Gwrych Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwrych_Castle), [North Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Wales), [Lloyd Hesketh Bamford-Hesketh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Hesketh_Bamford-Hesketh) was known for his vast collection of books at his library, however, at the later part of that same century, the public became aware that parts of his library was a fabrication, dummy books were built and then locked behind glass doors to stop people from trying to access them, from this a proverb was born, "Like Hesky's library, all outside".[^2457][^2458]

#### Actual or purported examples

##### Objects

- Recording artist Ugly Husbands released a full-length cassette in a limited edition of 50, each in a different book-safe, on Roll Over Rover Records.[^2459]
- Hollowed-out books have been used to smuggle items into [prisons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisons), such as tools to aid a [prison escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_escape) or [contraband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contraband) such as drugs or weapons.[^2460]
- Small [bombs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomb) can be hidden inside books, with a trigger that operates when book is opened. In 1980, [United Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines) president Percy Wood was injured by the explosion of a [pipe bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipe_bomb) hidden inside a book that he received in the mail.[^2461]
- A man in [Redding, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redding,_California) was arrested after taking photographs of a young girl with a camera hidden inside a book.[^2462]
- In 2005, antiques thieves attempted to use a hollowed-out book to take a precious lead weight out of Israel.[^2463]
- Guards at the Washington County Jail in [Fayetteville, Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayetteville,_Arkansas) seized a book that had been marked with what appeared to be stains from a leaking yellow felt pen, but tested positive for [methamphetamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methamphetamine).[^2464]
- [Ilya Lichtenstein and Heather Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bitfinex_hack) used two hollowed-out books to conceal items in their attempts to launder \$4.5 billion in stolen cryptocurrency in 2019.[^2465]
- In 1996, [Ricardo Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Lopez) fabricated a hollowed-out book to house a sophisticated acid dispersal device, designed to look inconspicuous and infiltrate the postal system to injure [bjork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bjork). The package was intercepted at a post office in London by the Metropolitan Police after the famous Ricardo Lopez tapes were discovered by the Hollywood Police Department.

#### Fictional occurrences

##### Television

- In the series *[Blackadder the Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackadder_the_Third)*, the opening titles feature [Edmund Blackadder Esq.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Blackadder) removing a romance novel (featuring the titles of the episode and accompanying cover art) from a hollowed-out book featuring the title *Blackadder the Third*.
- In the series *[Prison Break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_Break)*, the main character, [Michael Scofield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scofield), hides a screw in a Bible, which he uses to break out of prison.
- In the *[Lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_%282004_TV_series%29)* episode "[What Kate Did](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kate_Did)", one of the characters finds some [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographic_film) in a Bible.
- In *[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Simpsons)* episode "[Co-Dependents' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-Dependents'_Day)", Homer conceals alcohol in a Bible whilst visiting Marge in rehab, having framed her in a drunk-driving incident to avoid another DUI. He later discovers, to his horror and after promising to cut down on his drinking, that his hollowed-out Bible has been replaced with an intact copy.
- In the *[House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_%28TV_series%29)* episode "Finding Judas", the title character conceals a bottle of [Vicodin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicodin) in a textbook on [lupus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupus_erythematosus).
- In the *[King of the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Hill)* episode "Full Metal Dust Jacket," [Dale Gribble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Gribble) attempts to buy a book for the purpose of hiding a [firearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firearm) in it.
- In the series *[Pretty Little Liars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Little_Liars)*, character, [Spencer Hastings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Hastings), finds four small tapes concealed in a book.

##### Film

- [Red Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Grant), one of the villains in the 1963 [James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond) film *[From Russia with Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/From_Russia_with_Love_%28film%29)* has a gun hidden in a copy of *[War and Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_and_Peace)*.
- A nail trimmer is concealed in a Bible by inmate [Frank Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Morris_%28prisoner%29) in the 1979 film *[Escape from Alcatraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape_from_Alcatraz_%28film%29)*.
- In the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) mini-series *[Smiley's People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiley's_People_%28TV_series%29)*, [George Smiley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Smiley) hides a negative photograph of Kirov and Leipzig in an antique edition on loan from a friend upon Oliver Lacon's intrusion into his study. When Lacon's interest in the book becomes untenable, Smiley remarks that the edition is worth half the national budget and could he leave it alone, thus preserving the cover for the interleaved exposure.
- In the 1993 [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company) film *[The Three Musketeers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Three_Musketeers_%281993_film%29)*, [Aramis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aramis) pulls a pistol from a hollowed out bible to save [d'Artagnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Batz_de_Castelmore_d'Artagnan) from the executioners' axe.
- In the 1994 film *[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shawshank_Redemption)*, one of the characters hides a [rock hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geologist's_hammer) inside a Bible. The first page to be cut into bears the title "[Exodus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Exodus)". The line "Salvation lies within" is also repeated more than once.
- In the 1997 Disney film *[Jungle 2 Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_2_Jungle)*, an item is hidden in the Bible.
- In the 1997 film *[The Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_%281997_film%29)*, Nicholas takes a gun from a hollowed-out copy of *[To Kill a Mockingbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To_Kill_a_Mockingbird)*.
- In the 1999 film *[The Matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix)*, [Neo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo_%28The_Matrix%29) hides several [computer disks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_disk) in a copy of [Jean Baudrillard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Baudrillard)'s *[Simulacra and Simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulacra_and_Simulation)*.
- In the 1999 [short film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_subject) *[Me and the Big Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_and_the_Big_Guy)*, Citizen 43275-B hides a handwritten 'Guide to Revolution', pen, and pair of glasses in a Re-Education Manual, having intentionally irritated [Big Brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Brother_%28Nineteen_Eighty-Four%29) to the extent that he no longer wants to surveil him in order to continue writing it in private.
- In the 2001 film *Lara Croft: Tomb Raider*, [Lara Croft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lara_Croft) finds a hidden note from her father bound behind a book jacket.
- In the 2004 film *[Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_&_Kumar_Go_to_White_Castle)*, Kumar hides his stash of marijuana in his medical book.
- In the 2004 film *[National Treasure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Treasure_%28film%29)*, Benjamin Gates's father keeps money in a copy of *[Common Sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Sense_%28pamphlet%29)*.
- In the 2006 film *[V for Vendetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V_for_Vendetta_%28film%29)*, Bishop Anthony James Lilliman hides a gun in a copy of the Bible.
- In the 2007 film *[The Invisible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Invisible_%282007_film%29)*, the protagonist hides money he has earned selling essays in a hollowed-out copy of *[Catch-22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catch-22)*.
- In the 2019 film *El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie*, [Todd Alquist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Alquist) initially hides money he earned from manufacturing meth in hollowed-out encyclopedias. After his cleaner uncovers this system, Alquist kills her and begins hiding money in his fridge.

##### Fiction writing

- *[Explorers on the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explorers_on_the_Moon)*, one of *[The Adventures of Tintin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Tintin)*, features a book hollowed out to hold alcohol.
- In [Robert Ludlum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ludlum)'s book *[The Janson Directive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Janson_Directive)*, Paul Janson's old mentor Angus Fielding, don of [Trinity College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_College,_Cambridge), pulls a .22 Webley [Pistol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pistol) out of the 1759 edition of [Samuel Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Johnson)'s *[A Dictionary of the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Dictionary_of_the_English_Language) A-G* (the A standing for ammunition and the G for guns).
- In the novel *[Interstellar Pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstellar_Pig)*, Barney hides the Piggy in a hollowed-out high-school yearbook.
- In the manga series *[Cardcaptor Sakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardcaptor_Sakura)* and *Cardcaptor Sakura: Clear Card*, the Clow/Sakura Book is a book safe containing the magical cards of [Clow Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clow_Reed) and [Sakura Kinomoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakura_Kinomoto).
- In the novel *[John Dies at the End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dies_at_the_End)*, David keeps a gun in a hollowed-out copy of the [Qur'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qur'an).
- In the novel *[The Testaments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Testaments)* by [Margaret Atwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Atwood), Lydia uses a hollowed-out copy of *[Apologia Pro Vita Sua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apologia_Pro_Vita_Sua)* to hide an illicit manuscript that will later be known as the *Ardua Hall Holograph*. In the manuscript, Lydia details her induction as a Founding Aunt of Gilead, the endemic corruption and hypocrisy of the Commanders of the Faith, and her covert efforts to deliver justice within the Gileadian system and assist the Mayday Resistance.

##### Games

- In the 2001 [adventure game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_game) *Alfred Hitchcock Presents: The Final Cut*, the player must cut open a book with a knife to discover a key.[^2466]
- In the horror game *[Resident Evil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resident_Evil_%281996_video_game%29)*, players can obtain a book with a medal hidden inside.
- In the video game *Hitman: Blood Money*, the player can conceal a bomb in a hollow Bible.
- In the Nintendo DS game *[Another Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Code)*, a key is found inside a hollow book.
- In the PC and [NES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NES) game *[Shadowgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadowgate)*, a key is found in a hollowed out book. The player must learn to open the book without removing it to avoid triggering a trap that will drop them into a pit.

#### Related concepts

- Often in popular fiction, a switch to open a [secret passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_passage) is disguised as a book on a [bookshelf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookshelf).
