### Once Upon a Time in Shaolin

***Once Upon a Time in Shaolin*** is the seventh studio album by the American [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop) group [Wu-Tang Clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu-Tang_Clan). It was recorded in secret and features the entire Wu-Tang Clan, plus the rapper [Redman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redman_%28rapper%29), the [Wu-Tang Killa Beez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu-Tang_Killa_Beez), [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona) players, the actress [Carice van Houten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carice_van_Houten) and the singer [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher).

Feeling the value of music had been cheapened by the internet, the producers [Cilvaringz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilvaringz) and [RZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RZA) created only one copy, with no ability to [download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download) or [stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media) it. In 2015, [Martin Shkreli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Shkreli), the CEO of [Turing Pharmaceuticals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Pharmaceuticals), bought it at auction for \$1.5 million. In 2018, following Shkreli's conviction for [securities fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_fraud), a federal court seized assets belonging to him, including *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin*. In 2021, the [US Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Department_of_Justice) sold it to a corporate entity for more than \$2 million, who sold to the [non-fungible token](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token) collectors PleasrDAO for \$4 million.

A legal agreement stipulates that the album cannot be commercially exploited until 2103, although it can be played at listening parties. The first public exhibition began in June 2024 at the [Museum of Old and New Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Old_and_New_Art) in [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart), Tasmania. That month, Shkreli livestreamed it on [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_%28social_media_app%29), triggering a lawsuit from PleasrDAO. PleasrDAO also began selling partial ownership of the album as an [NFT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFT), with each purchase accelerating the release by 88 seconds.

Many fans reacted negatively to the news of the single-copy album. Critics who have heard *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* in whole or part responded positively. *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone)* said it had the potential to become Wu-Tang Clan's most popular album in decades, [*Complex*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_%28magazine%29) likened it to early Wu-Tang albums and *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian)* praised the single-copy concept as a "work of art". In 2015, the *[Guinness Book of Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_Book_of_Records)* certified *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* as the most valuable album in the world.

#### Recording

Wu-Tang Clan began working on *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* in the late 2000s.[^3822] It took about six years to complete. It was recorded in secret, mostly in [Staten Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island), New York, and produced in [Marrakesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakesh), Morocco.[^3823][^3824] It features the entire Wu-Tang Clan, plus the rapper [Redman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redman_%28rapper%29), the [Wu-Tang Killa Beez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu-Tang_Killa_Beez), [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona) football players, the actress [Carice van Houten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carice_van_Houten)[^3825] and two appearances from the singer and actress [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher).[^3826][^3827] The Wu-Tang rapper [Method Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Method_Man) said the members were not told they were working on a Wu-Tang album, and that they were uncomfortable with the single-copy concept after it was announced.[^3828]

#### Release

Inspired by musical [patronage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patronage) during the [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance),[^3829] the Wu-Tang producer [Cilvaringz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilvaringz) decided to create *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* as an [art object](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_object).[^3826] Feeling the value of music had been cheapened by [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming) and [online piracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_piracy), he and the Wu-Tang producer [RZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RZA) hoped to return it to the value of [fine art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_art).[^3823] They wrote on their website:[^3826]

> The music industry is in crisis. The intrinsic value of music has been reduced to zero. Contemporary art is worth millions by virtue of its exclusivity ... By adopting a 400 year old Renaissance-style approach to music, offering it as a commissioned commodity and allowing it to take a similar trajectory from creation to exhibition to sale ... we hope to inspire and intensify urgent debates about the future of music.

Wu-Tang deleted the [master files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_recordings).[^3824] A single copy, on two CDs, is held in a silver jewel-encrusted box with a wax Wu-Tang Clan seal and leather-bound liner notes.[^3827][^3824] On March 3, 2015, the box was detained at [JFK Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JFK_Airport) for three hours while border control determined its contents.[^3830] That month, Wu-Tang Clan exhibited the album to a crowd of about 150 art collectors, dealers and critics in [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens), New York.[^3827] Attendees were searched for recording devices.[^3827] About 13 minutes of the album were played to the audience.[^3827]

##### Purchase by Martin Shkreli (2015)

*Once Upon A Time In Shaolin* was auctioned through [Paddle8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddle8) in 2015,[^3831] which had previously sold works by artists including [Jeff Koons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Koons), [Julian Schnabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Schnabel) and [Damien Hirst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Hirst).[^3823] Legal agreements stipulated that it could not be commercially exploited for 88 years, although it could be released free or played at listening parties.[^3832] According to RZA, the number eight was symbolic as there were eight original members of Wu-Tang Clan, the numbers of the year 2015 add up to eight, Paddle8 has eight in its name, and a rotated eight forms the [symbol for infinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbol_for_infinity), used on their second album, *[Wu-Tang Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu-Tang_Forever)* (1997).[^3833] The auction gained significant attention. An unfounded rumor spread online that the purchase agreement stipulated that members of Wu-Tang Clan, or the actor [Bill Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Murray), would be allowed one attempt at stealing the record back in a heist.[^3834]

The winning bid was accepted on May 3, 2015, followed by months of legal diligence.[^3835] The sale was completed on August 26 to a private individual for an unspecified amount.[^3823] On December 9, *[Bloomberg Businessweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_Businessweek)* identified the buyer as the [Turing Pharmaceuticals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_Pharmaceuticals) CEO [Martin Shkreli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Shkreli), who had paid \$2 million.[^3836][^3837] RZA said the sale was agreed before Shkreli's controversial price hike of the anti-infective agent [Daraprim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraprim). According to RZA, after learning the buyer's identity, Cilvaringz and Wu-Tang Clan donated a "significant portion" of the proceeds to charity.[^3838] The *[Guinness Book of Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_Book_of_Records)* certified *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* as the most valuable album in the world, surpassing records by [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley) and [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles).[^3839]

In January 2016, Shkreli told [*Vice*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_%28magazine%29) that he had considered destroying the album or "installing it in some remote place so that people have to make a spiritual quest to listen".[^3840] He promised to release it free if [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump) won the [2016 US presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_US_presidential_election). In November, after Trump was elected, Shkreli streamed excerpts online.[^3841] In February 2016, the artist Jason Koza sued RZA, Cilvaringz, Paddle8 and Shkreli in the [U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._District_Court_for_the_Southern_District_of_New_York), alleging they used his artwork on the album without permission.[^3842][^3843] Koza withdrew the case that May.[^3844]

In September 2017,[^3845] Shkreli attempted to sell *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* on the online auction site [eBay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBay), with the winning bid passing \$1m. He was incarcerated on unrelated fraud counts before the sale could be completed.[^3846] RZA disapproved of the sale, saying: "I think he could have got more than what he paid. I was actually impressed that within eight days he got up to \$1m in bidding ... If it had been left a bit longer, no telling how far it would have gone."[^3847] RZA hoped to buy it himself, but was contractually unable.[^3848]

##### Purchase by PleasrDAO (2018-2021)

In March 2018, following Shkreli's conviction for [securities fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_fraud), a federal court seized assets belonging to him worth \$7.36m, including *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin*.[^3849] On July 27, 2021, Jacquelyn M. Kasulis, acting [United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Attorney_for_the_Eastern_District_of_New_York), announced that the [US Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Department_of_Justice) had sold the album in connection with the approximately \$7.4 million forfeiture judgment entered against Shkreli at his March 2018 sentencing.[^3850] It was purchased for \$2,238,482.30 by WTC Endeavours Limited, a corporate entity created in Hong Kong for the purchase.[^3851]

In September 2021, the album was sold for \$4 million to PleasrDAO, a group that purchases [non-fungible tokens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token) (NFTs) that honor "anti-establishment rebels". PleasrDAO had previously purchased NFTs related to the American whistleblower [Edward Snowden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden) and the Russian punk band [Pussy Riot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pussy_Riot).[^3822] PleasrDAO described the purchase as the "ultimate protest against middlemen and rent seekers of musicians and artists" and described Shkreli as "the ultimate internet villain".[^3852] It hoped to make the album more widely available, but is bound by the restrictions forbidding its release to the public, and suggested it could be played at listening parties or exhibitions.[^3822]

##### Public exhibition and NFTs (2024)

On June 9, 2024, Shkreli livestreamed *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* to an audience of approximately 5,000 via the social network [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_%28Twitter%29). It was the first time it had been made available for public listening. PleasrDAO sued Shkreli for playing it without permission, arguing that he had diminished its value.[^3853] Judge [Pamela K. Chen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_K._Chen) issued a temporary [restraining order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restraining_order) blocking Shkreli from disseminating the album.[^3854] On 27 August, a New York federal judge ordered Shkreli to surrender his copies.[^3855]

The first official exhibition of *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* began on June 15, 2024, at the [Museum of Old and New Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Old_and_New_Art) in [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart), Tasmania.[^3824][^3856] Attendees signed a waiver promising not to record it, binding until 2103, and were played a 30-minute mix created by Cilvaringz for the exhibition.[^3857] That month, PleasrDAO began selling partial ownership of the album as an NFT for one dollar. Each purchase accelerates the release date by 88 seconds and gives the purchaser a five-minute [sampler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampler_album).[^3857][^3858]

In September 2025, Chen refused to dismiss PleasrDAO's lawsuit against Shkreli, ruling that he had potentially violated federal protections for [trade secrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_secrets) by retaining copies of the album. Chen wrote that "the secret and exclusive nature of the album is a large part of its intrinsic value".[^3859] In January 2026, Shkreli [counter-sued](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-sued) RZA and Cilvaringz, saying they had improperly sold the album copyrights to PleasrDAO. Chen rejected the move, saying counterclaims can only be asserted against an opposing party (PleasrDAO).[^3860]

#### Music

Reporting from the exhibition in Queens, [*Complex*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_%28magazine%29) described *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* as "rich, layered, and sonically bombastic", with a "rugged, hard-hitting sound" reminiscent of early Wu-Tang Clan albums. It begins with "ominous, foreboding" sounds of rain and thunder, before the rapper [Raekwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raekwon) begins the first verse. Other sounds include fire sirens, crowd applause, and a marching drum beat. [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher) appears twice, as singer and actress, and closes the record with the "belted" words "Wu-Tang baby, they rock the world".[^3840]

#### Response

The *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone)* critic Christopher Weingarten wrote that, based on the 13 minutes played in Queens, *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* had the potential to become Wu-Tang Clan's most popular album since 1997. He likened it to the [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2) album *[All That You Can't Leave Behind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_That_You_Can't_Leave_Behind)* (2000) and the [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica) album *[Death Magnetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_Magnetic)* (2008), and said it "hearkened back to the RZA's glory days" of the mid-1990s.[^3861]

Shkreli played the album during his interview with the *Vice* writer Allie Conti, who said: "From what I heard, it was definitely better than their last album, although I wouldn't say it's worth \$2 million necessarily."[^3840] After attending the Tasmania exhibition, the *Guardian* writer Sian Cain wrote that the album was "not as thrillingly in your face" as the 1993 debut *[Enter the Wu-Tang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enter_the_Wu-Tang)*, but was "easily as good" as *Wu-Tang Forever* (1997), with a more polished sound than both. She concluded: "So as Wu-Tang Clan music goes, it's good. But as a work of art, *Once Upon a Time in Shaolin* is truly great."[^3857]

Many fans reacted negatively to the news of the single-copy album. Method Man supported the concept, but spoke out against the 88-year commercial ban, blaming RZA and Cilvaringz. He said: "Fuck that album ... When music can't be music and y'all turning it into something else, fuck that. Give it to the people, if they want to hear the shit, let them have it. Give it away free." RZA replied that the ban was necessary to maintain the integrity of the album as a work of art and to deflect notions of a [publicity stunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publicity_stunt).[^3862][^3833] Method Man heard the album for the first time in October 2026 during a listening party for the podcast *[Pablo Torre Finds Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Torre_Finds_Out)*. He felt Cilvaringz was emulating RZA's sound too closely and some points were overlong, but concluded: "I do not hate this album ... That album ain't as bad as I expected it to be."[^3863]

In August 2020, it was announced that [Paul Downs Colaizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Downs_Colaizzo) was set to direct a film for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix) based on the story of the album, produced by [Plan B Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_B_Entertainment).[^3864] A documentary, *[The Disciple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Disciple_%282026_film%29)*, directed by [Joanna Natasegera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Natasegara), premiered at the [2026 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Sundance_Film_Festival) and is scheduled for release on Netflix in October 2026.[^3865]

### Backstroke of the West

***Star War: The Third Gathers - The Backstroke of the West***,[^3867] more commonly known as ***Backstroke of the West***, is a 2005 Chinese [bootleg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bootleg_recording) DVD of the film *Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith* that became an [internet meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme) for its poor [machine-translated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation) English subtitles. The bootleg first gained attention in June 2005 shortly after its release, when American blogger Jeremy Winterson purchased a copy at a [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai) market and shared [screenshots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenshot) on his personal blog.

The [literal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literal_translation) machine translation from Chinese to English resulted in bizarre mistranslations, most notably renaming [Anakin Skywalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anakin_Skywalker) to "Allah Gold", [Obi-Wan Kenobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obi-Wan_Kenobi) to "Ratio Tile", and the [Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedi) to "Hopeless Situation Warriors". Additionally, the resulting subtitles introduce random profanity and instances of [Chinglish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinglish). A full-length English [fandub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fandub) of the film was produced for [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube).

The bootleg is most famous for its translation of [Darth Vader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darth_Vader)'s climactic scream of "Nooooooo!", which was rendered in the subtitles as "Do not want". Following the fandub's wider circulation in early 2017, the bootleg received renewed attention from [entertainment journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_journalism), several of whom praised the quality of the voice acting and its unintentional comedic reworking of the film.

#### History

##### Origin

On June 7, 2005, Jeremy Winterson wrote about his experience seeing *Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith* at a local theater with a friend who was visiting for business the past weekend. Winterson considered the film as superior to the first two films in the [*Star Wars* prequel trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_prequel_trilogy) and a fitting conclusion to the saga, while noting it was in the middle position in the chronology of the series.[^3868]

The following day, Winterson encountered a DVD seller and decided to purchase a [bootleg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bootleg_recording) DVD of *Revenge of the Sith* as part of a batch from a local [street vendor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_%28trade%29) along his commute.[^3869][^3870][^3871] He wrote that the seller had assured him of the DVD's quality, which was priced at 7 RMB.[^3872][^3868]

At the time, Winterson lived in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai), China, as an [expat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expat) for work in 2005.[^3869][^3870][^3871] Having shelved the DVD shortly after purchase, he later credited his sister with rediscovering it and sparking his interest.[^3873] Winterson stated he purchased the DVD at [Xiangyang Market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangyang_Market),[^3874] an [open-air market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-air_market) in Shanghai known as a major hub for [pirated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_infringement) and [counterfeit goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterfeit_consumer_good).[^3875] The following year, in 2006, the market was permanently closed as part of a crackdown to improve the city's image.[^3876]

Following positive feedback from friends and family on Winterson's blog post about the bootleg, one of his friends shared it through a work [mailing list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailing_list), after which it became popular enough that Winterson's [domain provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name_registrar) temporarily suspended his blog for [exceeding its bandwidth limits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_traffic).[^3877][^3878][^3879] Winterson's blog post was briefly mentioned in an official *starwars.com* blog post on June 17, 2005.[^3880]

##### Translation errors

Winterson theorized the film's [subtitles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtitles) were first transcribed by hand into Chinese and then [machine-translated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation) back into English.[^3881][^3882] The machine translation often ignored structural differences between English and Chinese and produced [literal translations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literal_translation) of [Chinese characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_characters).[^3883][^3884]

Notable character and faction name changes include:

- [Anakin Skywalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anakin_Skywalker) was translated to "Allah Gold".[^3885]
- [Obi-Wan Kenobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obi-Wan_Kenobi) was translated to "Ratio Tile".[^3886]
- [Chancellor Palpatine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_Palpatine) was translated to "Speaker D".[^3887]
- The [Jedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedi) were translated to "Hopeless Situation Warriors".[^3888]
- The [Jedi Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedi_High_Council) was translated to the "[Presbyterian Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterian_Church)" or "Hopeless Situation Presbyterians".[^3889][^3890]

#### Reception and legacy

A full-length [fandub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fandub) of the film was produced by the [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube) channel TheThirdGathers; the dub was later reposted, in full, by YouTube channel GratefulDeadpool on February 14, 2016.[^3891][^3892][^3893] The English fandub received wider attention from [entertainment journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_journalism) in January 2017, with some viewing it as an unintentional and comedic improvement over the original film. *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter)* called the redub a "fan-made masterpiece" that did "the unthinkable" by making the film "cool",[^3894] while *[Uproxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uproxx)* declared it a "vastly superior movie".[^3895] *[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_A.V._Club)* described the "legendarily bad Chinese dub" as the "best version of the *Star Wars* prequels," writing that it made the film "watchable by making \[it\] even less sensible".[^3896]

*[SlashFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SlashFilm)* described the machine-translated script as a "beautiful monstrosity" and "kind of magical", declaring it "the only version of this movie I ever want to watch".[^3897] Noting its unintentional comedy and the mixed reception of the [prequel trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prequel_trilogy) films, *[Nerdist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerdist)* stated it allowed fans to enjoy the film as a "bizarre, sometimes incoherent comedy,"[^3898] and *[Gizmodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gizmodo)* declared it "gloriousness defined" and "basically the greatest thing on Earth."[^3899] Several journalists further noted the quality of the fandub cast's voice acting.[^3900][^3901]

Journalists highlighted specific bizarre mistranslations, such as [General Grievous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Grievous) commanding troops to "batter to death them",[^3902] and random use of the word "[fuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuck)" and other profanity, which *[Inverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_%28website%29)* stated made the otherwise "squeaky-clean" film "weird and enjoyable".[^3903] The bootleg is best known for the mistranslation of [Darth Vader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darth_Vader)'s climactic scream of "Nooooooo!", into "Do not want", upon learning about the death of his wife, [Padmé Amidala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padm%C3%A9_Amidala).[^3904][^3905][^3906] *Inverse* attributed this to the lack of "an equivalent word for 'no'" in Chinese, with the machine translation instead using the "negative tense of a verb" based on the scene's context.[^3907]

### The Extraordinary Adventures of Mr. West in the Land of the Bolsheviks

***The Extraordinary Adventures of Mr. West in the Land of the Bolsheviks*** ([Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language): Необычайные приключения мистера Веста в стране Большевиков, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Russian): *Neobychainye priklyucheniya mistera Vesta v strane bolshevikov*) is a 1924 Soviet silent [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film) film directed by [Lev Kuleshov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lev_Kuleshov). Kuleshov considered the film a "verification" of his theories around [editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_editing) and [montage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montage_%28filmmaking%29), and he drew inspiration from [American cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States), which he found more engaging than Russian cinema.

The film follows J. S. West and Cowboy Jeddy, two Americans who visit the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union) after the [Russian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Revolution). West is wealthy but naive, and he expects the country to be barbaric. A Soviet gang leader exploits West's fears by staging a fake arrest and trial, then offers to "rescue" him in exchange for money. When West is actually rescued by the Soviet police, he realizes his expectations and stereotypes were wrong and celebrates the country.

Upon its initial release, the film garnered popularity among Soviet audiences; however, Soviet critics criticized its emphasis on American themes and its lack of political engagement. Despite its initial popularity, the film was censored two years after its release. Today, critics and historians often consider *Mr. West* the beginning of a "golden age" of Soviet cinema. The movie satirizes American perceptions of the Soviet Union.

#### Plot

J. S. West, director of the [YMCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YMCA), plans to visit the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union). His wife reads magazine articles that portray Russians as barbarians, and asks him to bring Cowboy Jeddy as a bodyguard. When West and Jeddy arrive in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow), a thief steals one of their suitcases and brings it to a gang leader named Zhban. Realizing that West is wealthy and distrusts Russians, Zhban concocts a plan to scam him.

West and Jeddy hire a taxi, but Jeddy gets separated and forgets the car's license plate. Frustrated and concerned for West's safety, he hijacks a carriage. When the police try to arrest him, Jeddy escapes by fleeing along rooftops, then unexpectedly reunites with Ellie, a woman he once saved from being mugged in the United States. Ellie vouches for his character, explaining that he falsely believed Russians were savages, and convinces the police to let him free.

Zhban returns West's suitcase, claiming he recovered it from a barbarian, and invites West to stay with him for safety. He gives West a fake tour of Moscow, which purportedly shows that the [Moscow State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_State_University) and [Bolshoi Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolshoi_Theatre) have been destroyed. One of Zhban's gang members, the Countess, tries to seduce West. Zhban hires another group of criminals to dress as exaggerated Russian stereotypes, kidnap West and the Countess, stage a show trial, and sentence them to death. Zhban then "rescues" West and the Countess in exchange for West's money.

Zhban's scheme is interrupted by the police, who arrive with Jeddy and Ellie. The police give West a real tour of Moscow, showing him the still-standing University and Theatre and a military parade. Impressed, West sends home a telegram asking his wife to burn the magazines and hang up a picture of [Vladimir Lenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Lenin).

#### Cast

- [Porfiri Podobed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porfiri_Podobed) as J. S. West
- [Boris Barnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Barnet) as Cowboy Jeddy
- [Aleksandra Khokhlova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandra_Khokhlova) as The Countess
- [Vsevolod Pudovkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vsevolod_Pudovkin) as Zhban
- [Sergey Komarov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Komarov_%28actor%29) as The One-Eyed Man
- [Leonid Obolensky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Obolensky) as The Dandy
- Valia Lopatina as Ellie

#### Background

*The Extraordinary Adventures of Mr. West in the Land of the Bolsheviks* was produced and set in the aftermath of the [Russian Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Revolution). Led by Vladimir Lenin, the [Bolsheviks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsheviks) overthrew the Russian government, [executed the Tsar and his family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_the_Romanov_family), fought [a civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Civil_War), and established the [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism) Soviet Union.[^3908] Western countries largely condemned the revolution's violence; the United States would not [diplomatically recognize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_recognition) the Soviet Union until 1933.[^3909]

Lenin nationalized the country's film industry in 1919, but his 1921 [New Economic Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Economic_Policy) required it to fund itself. The state paid for new Soviet cinema with profits from imported American films. These imported films were extremely popular, leading [Lev Kuleshov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lev_Kuleshov) to coin the term *amerikanshchina* (*American[-itis](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-itis)*).[^3910]

Many Russian filmmakers left after the revolution, but Kuleshov stayed and worked to develop a new Soviet cinema.[^3909] He organized a workshop called the Kuleshov Collective to develop a new approach to filmmaking.[^3911] His approach was informed by film shortages. The workshop staged theatrical "films without film", using curtains and lighting to represent cuts and close-ups[^3912] and a "spacial metric grid" to visualize the hypothetical movie screen.[^3913] He developed a preference for short shots over long shots to avoid mistakes.[^3914] Kuleshov believed editing distinguished film from theater, and considered [montage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montage_%28filmmaking%29) as fundamental to cinema as [harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony) is to music.[^3915] He rejected [Konstantin Stanislavski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantin_Stanislavski)'s [acting method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanislavski's_system), which focused on psychology and emotion. Instead, Kuleshov wanted his actors to emphasize precise, legible movements.[^3916] He found Hollywood action and [slapstick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick) more engaging than the work of Russian directors like [Aleksandr Khanzhonkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandr_Khanzhonkov), and felt cinema should be efficient and industrial to help its audience embrace modernity.[^3917]

#### Production

In 1924, the Kuleshov Collective released *The Extraordinary Adventures of Mr West in the Land of the Bolsheviks* as its first feature. Kuleshov himself directed the film, and his students, including [Boris Barnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Barnet) and [Vsevolod Pudovkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vsevolod_Pudovkin), played the lead roles.[^3918] The movie was filmed from 15 December 1923 to 7 April 1924.[^3919]

[Nikolai Aseyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Aseyev_%28writer%29) wrote an initial script for the film, but Kuleshov and Pudovkin extensively rewrote it.[^3909] Kuleshov later said they kept only the characters' names.[^3920] The plot may have been influenced by a 1923 story in [Krokodil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krokodil) called "The Adventures of Mr. Stupidhead in Russia", which also featured a foreigner who believes Russia is barbaric; when Mr. Stupidhead instead sees a functional society, he assumes it's a facade.[^3921] The film's working title was *How Will This End?*[^3922] Its ultimate title alludes to adventure stories like *[The Legend of the Glorious Adventures of Tyl Ulenspiegel in the Land of Flanders and Elsewhere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Thyl_Ulenspiegel_and_Lamme_Goedzak)*.[^3909]

Kuleshov and his actors choreographed scenes and rehearsed using stopwatches and [metronomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metronome) to avoid wasting film.[^3912][^3923] In one scene, Boris Barnet fell while traversing a tightrope, claiming that Kuleshov left him hanging for a half hour while criticizing his insufficient training.[^3919]

#### Style

*The Extraordinary Adventures of Mr. West in the Land of the Bolsheviks* is a satirical comedy.[^3911] Kuleshov considered the film a "verification" of his approach to montage and production, and Rimgaila Salys describes it as a "compendium" of his cinematic ideas. The film includes chases and stunts inspired by popular American cinema, rapid editing, [slow motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_motion), flashbacks, and re-contextualized documentary footage.[^3917] Kuleshov includes visual jokes (such as Zhban getting hit with a [žban](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%D0%B6%D0%B1%D0%B0%D0%BD)), parodies of religious icons, and references to films like *[Neighbors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbors_%281920_film%29)*, *[The Cabinet of Dr Caligari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cabinet_of_Dr_Caligari)*, and *[Dr Mabuse the Gambler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr_Mabuse_the_Gambler)*.[^3909][^3924] The cinematography and editing reflect the characters' mindsets: when West is homesick, the film superimposes American faces onto Soviet women,[^3925] and when Jeddy forgets West's license plate number, it shows the number 999 dissolve into 666.[^3926] Instead of simply providing exposition, the [title cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertitle) offer comments like "Comfort is a relative concept".[^3909] In one instance, an intertitle explains that West sees the room spinning, and the camera shows the spinning room that he perceives.[^3921]

Kuleshov arranged objects, characters, and motion along grid lines and 45 degree angles, which he felt made the action easiest for audiences to understand. For example, when Jeddy crosses the tightrope between buildings, the wire is horizontal and the buildings are vertical.[^3913][^3917] In one scene, a jug is placed close to the camera to emphasize its eventual destruction; Kuleshov determined the most impactful framing of the jug using a mathematical formula he devised.[^3917]

The actors' performances are physical and exaggerated.[^3927] In contrast, the production design is minimalist. Many scenes avoid sets by using [close-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close-up)[^3924] or filming against solid black backgrounds.[^3917] This was partly a stylistic choice to focus on the actors and key objects, and partly a response to material shortages.[^3909]

#### Themes and analysis

J. S. West is modeled on [Harold Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Lloyd).[^3914][^3909] He is gullible, effeminate, [bourgeois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeoisie), naive, prudish, and excessively patriotic, waving an American flag when arriving in Moscow and wearing American flag socks.[^3924][^3909][^3921] Jeddy, modeled on [Tom Mix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mix)[^3914] and [Douglas Fairbanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_Fairbanks),[^3909] is a caricature of a [cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy), complete with a [lasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso) and gun.[^3924][^3921] His appearance and behavior are conspicuously out of place in snow-covered Moscow.[^3928] West and Jeddy are satirical characters, but they are portrayed as well-intentioned and more noble than the Russian criminals.[^3909] For example, West's patriotism inspires him to fight like a "real American" to defend himself and the Countess. As Jeddy learns that Russia does not match his stereotypes, he also stops looking like a stereotypical cowboy. By the end of the film, he wears plain contemporary clothes.[^3921]

The film satirizes Western perceptions of the Soviet Union,[^3911] but it has also been read as critiquing the Soviet Union itself. Rimgaila Salys says the film showcases the negative effects of Lenin's New Economic Policy.[^3909] Vlada Petrić suggests that West's kidnapping and show trial, as well as the police raid that saves him, echo the tactics of the Soviet [secret police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_police). He argues that Soviet audiences would have recognized the implication that the gang does represent the Bolsheviks after all, and he interprets West's final telegram as mocking unrealistic communist rhetoric.[^3922] Peter Christensen believes the name "J. S. West" not only alludes to the [Western world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world) and the [Wild West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_frontier), but also to [Edward Bellamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Bellamy)'s 1888 novel *[Looking Backward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looking_Backward)*, in which a time traveler named Julian West visits a utopian Socialist future. In Christensen's analysis, this allusion emphasizes the Soviet Union's failure to achieve Bellamy's ideals. He notes that the film depicts Russia as a nation of poor criminals, and that the ending merely celebrates pre-revolutionary architecture, not anything created by the Bolsheviks themselves.[^3929] Conversely, Marina Levitina does interpret the film's final shot of a Russian radio tower as a boast of new technological achievements.[^3924]

Greta Matzner-Gore observes that the film is built around nested and metatextual imitations, highlighting cinema's potential to mislead. West's kidnappers imitate pictures of Americans who were imitating stereotypical Russians, but in reality, the "Americans" in the photos were played by the same Russian actors who "imitate" them. She notes that the film compares Zhban to a [film director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director), commanding actors in a performance and orchestrating [visual effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects) to deceive Mr. West, and that West remains equally credulous throughout the film. He accepts the police officer's tour exactly as he accepted Zhban's fake tour, and he's impressed by the military parade, which a title card asserts is "real" although it's actually an editing trick.[^3930] Likewise, David Gillespie finds the ending "ambivalent". He notes that the film consistently emphasizes false images of Russia, and therefore the audience can't be confident the closing images are actually true.[^3931] The ending includes an incongruous scene of factory workers, which is unconnected to the plot and not observed by West himself. Denise Youngblood speculates Kuleshov may have been forced to include the scene,[^3932] but Miguel Gaggiotti suggests the film juxtaposes the workers' naturalism against the artificiality of the parade, emphasizing that the parade is merely another performance.[^3927]

#### Reception and legacy

Audiences responded positively to *Mr. West*'s accessible American style,[^3932] and it was Kuleshov's most popular film.[^3933] In retrospect, it is considered the beginning of a "golden age" of Soviet cinema.[^3934][^3935][^3936] Peter Christensen notes that the film has endured better than other Soviet comedies of the time,[^3937] and David Gillespie considers it a "masterpiece of technique".[^3931] The film also has historical value as a record of Moscow in the 1920s, showcasing architecture like the original [Cathedral of Christ the Saviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_Christ_the_Saviour).[^3928] In a 2008 survey by *[Seans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seans)* magazine, film critic Veronika Khlebnikova listed it fifth among her 10 favourite Russian films.[^3938]

Despite the film's success, Kuleshov was criticized for his focus on aesthetics and technique over ideology[^3939] and his focus on American characters;[^3933] six of Kuleshov's 13 films would feature American characters and themes.[^3924] In particular, [Viktor Shklovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Shklovsky) criticized the film for not being sufficiently Russian.[^3932] Critics unfavorably compared Kuleshov to [Sergei Eisenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Eisenstein) and [Vsevolod Pudovkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vsevolod_Pudovkin), whose films were unequivocally pro-Bolshevik.[^3939] By September 1926, *Mr. West* was censored.[^3940] Despite this backlash, Kuleshov was eventually awarded the [Order of Lenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Lenin) shortly before his death in 1970.[^3941]

### Taylor Lautner

**Taylor Daniel Lautner** (/ˈlaʊtnər/ *LOWT-nər*;[^3942] born February 11, 1992) is an American actor, martial artist, and producer. He is best known for playing the [werewolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werewolf) [Jacob Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Black) in *[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twilight_Saga_%28film_series%29)* film series (2008-2012). His accolades include a [Scream Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream_Awards), seven [Teen Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards), two [People's Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards), and an [MTV Movie Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Movie_Award).

Born in [Grand Rapids, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Rapids,_Michigan), Lautner began practising [martial arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_arts) at the age of six. He became a [black belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_belt_%28martial_arts%29) at the age of 10, and by the age of 14, he was a four-time world champion.[^3943][^3944] He began his acting career playing bit parts in comedy series such as *[The Bernie Mac Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bernie_Mac_Show)* (2003) and *[My Wife and Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Wife_and_Kids)* (2004), before having voice roles in television series like *[What's New, Scooby-Doo?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_New,_Scooby-Doo?)* (2005) and *[Danny Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Phantom)* (2005). In 2005, he got his big break when he landed the role of Sharkboy in the film *[The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl in 3-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Sharkboy_and_Lavagirl_in_3-D)*. Also that year, he starred in *[Cheaper by the Dozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheaper_by_the_Dozen_2)*.

The late 2000s saw Lautner become a [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol) and [sex symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_symbol), after extensively changing his physique to keep the role of Jacob Black in further *Twilight* installments and generating media attention for his looks. In 2010, he was ranked second on *[Glamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glamour_%28magazine%29)*'s "The 50 Sexiest Men of 2010" list, and fourth on *[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_%28magazine%29)*'s "Most Amazing Bodies" list. Also in the same year, Lautner was named the highest-paid teenage actor in Hollywood.

In 2011, Lautner starred in the action film *[Abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abduction_%282011_film%29)*, in which he did almost all of his [stunts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stunts).[^3945] In 2013, he appeared in the comedy film *[Grown Ups 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grown_Ups_2)*. From 2014 to 2018, Lautner starred in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) sitcom [*Cuckoo*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuckoo_%28TV_series%29) as the son of the titular character. In 2015, he starred in the action film *[Tracers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracers_%28film%29)* and the comedy film *[The Ridiculous 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ridiculous_6)*. The following year, he portrayed Dr. Cassidy Cascade in the second season of [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company) [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_comedy) series *[Scream Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream_Queens_%282015_TV_series%29)*.

#### Early life

Taylor Daniel Lautner was born on February 11, 1992,[^3946][^3947] in [Grand Rapids, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Rapids,_Michigan),[^3946] the son of Deborah (née Bos) and Daniel Lautner.[^3948][^3949] His mother works for a [software development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development) company, while his father was a [Midwest Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwest_Airlines) pilot.[^3949][^3950] He has one younger sister named Makena.[^3949] Raised as a [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church),[^3951][^3952] Lautner has [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people), [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_people), and [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germans) ancestry. He has claimed that he has "distant" [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States) ancestry (specifically [Ottawa Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_Indian) and [Potawatomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi)) through his mother. This claim is challenged by scholars.[^3953][^3954][^3955] He grew up in [Hudsonville, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudsonville,_Michigan), a town near Grand Rapids.[^3956] He has stated that he was bullied in school because he was an actor. He commented, "I just had to tell myself 'I can't let this get to me. This is what I love to do. And I'm going to continue doing it.'"[^3957]

He took his first karate class at the age of six.[^3949] A year later, he attended the national karate tournament in [Louisville, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville,_Kentucky), where he met [Michael Chaturantabut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Chaturantabut), the founder of [Xtreme Martial Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xtreme_Martial_Arts). Chaturantabut invited Lautner to a camp he held at [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles).[^3949] Lautner trained with Chaturantabut for several years, earning his black belt by the age of eight, and winning several junior world championships.[^3956] He appeared in an [ISKA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISKA) karate event, the US Open ISKA World Martial Arts Championships, televised on [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN) in 2003[^3958] that was later lampooned on the sports-comedy show *[Cheap Seats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheap_Seats_%28TV_series%29)* that first aired in 2006.[^3959]

In junior high, Lautner, who was involved in karate, baseball and hip-hop dance, won the award for "Best Smile" and played in the school's Turkey Bowl American Football game.[^3960] He went to public school at [Valencia High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_High_School_%28Santa_Clarita,_California%29) in [Santa Clarita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clarita,_California) until his sophomore year.[^3961] Chaturantabut, who once portrayed the Blue Ranger in *[Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_Rangers_Lightspeed_Rescue)*, suggested to Lautner that he take up acting.[^3949] For a few years, the Lautners flew from Michigan to Los Angeles for auditions when his talent agency called, and returned to Grand Rapids for school sometimes the same day.[^3949] Lautner balanced karate and acting with being on the football and baseball teams at his school, and taking up [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz) and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop) dance.[^3962] After that became tiring, Lautner and his family decided to move to California for a month, to try it out, before moving to [Santa Clarita, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clarita,_California), in 2002.[^3949][^3962]

#### Career

##### 2001-2007: Career beginnings

In his first months after moving to Los Angeles, Lautner appeared in small television roles, small film roles, and ads and commercials. In 2001, Lautner first appeared in the made-for-television film, *Shadow Fury*. He then got a voice-over job in a commercial for *[Rugrats Go Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugrats_Go_Wild)*.[^3956] He then appeared in small television roles on *[The Bernie Mac Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bernie_Mac_Show)*, *[My Wife and Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Wife_and_Kids)*, and *[Summerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summerland_%28TV_series%29)*.[^3949] Lautner then earned voice-over roles in animated series such as *[Danny Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Phantom)*, *[Duck Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck_Dodgers)*, and *[What's New, Scooby-Doo?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_New,_Scooby-Doo?)*. The same year, he earned his first breakout role, starring in the film, *[The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl in 3-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Sharkboy_and_Lavagirl_in_3-D)*.[^3949] Lautner spent three months on location in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas), to film the movie,[^3949] which was received with negative reviews from critics, and was a minor international success. However, Lautner was nominated at the [2006 Young Artist Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Artist_Awards_2006) for Best Performance in a Feature Film by a Leading Actor.[^3963] For the film, Lautner choreographed all of his fight scenes after director [Robert Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Rodr%C3%ADguez) learned of his extensive martial arts training.[^3962] Months later, he played Eliot Murtaugh in *[Cheaper by the Dozen 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheaper_by_the_Dozen_2)*, which was panned by critics, being named one of the "Worst Films of the 2000s" by [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes).[^3964] After returning from Canada filming the latter movie, Lautner said he realized his newfound fame, from *Sharkboy and Lavagirl*.[^3949] In 2006 he appeared in the show *[Love Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love,_Inc._%28TV_series%29)* and the TV special *[He's a Bully, Charlie Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He's_a_Bully,_Charlie_Brown)*. Two years later, Lautner appeared in a lead role in the short-lived NBC drama *[My Own Worst Enemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Own_Worst_Enemy_%28TV_series%29)*, portraying [Christian Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Slater)'s son, Jack Spivey.[^3965] *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone)* coined his early roles as either "the popular kid, jock, or bully."[^3957]

##### 2008-2009: Breakthrough and *The Twilight Series*

In 2007, filmmakers began a search for actors to portray [Jacob Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Black), a [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas) friend of lead character [Bella Swan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Swan) in *[Twilight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight_%282008_film%29)*, the first film in [The *Twilight* Saga film series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twilight_Saga_%28film_series%29).[^3965] In January 2008, an open casting call was held in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon). Lautner had not heard of the *Twilight* series before, but was urged by his agent to audition.[^3965] At his audition, he read lines with [Kristen Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Stewart), who had already been cast as Bella, and they acted out scenes from *The Twilight Saga: New Moon* and *The Twilight Saga: Eclipse*.[^3965] The film was a commercial success, earning \$69 million its opening weekend, and has grossed \$392 million worldwide. It received mixed reviews from critics, having a "Rotten" rating with a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_average) of 5.5/10.[^3966] In describing the critical consensus, it stated: "Having lost much of its bite transitioning to the big screen, *Twilight* will please its devoted fans, but do little for the uninitiated."[^3966] On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic), which assigns a [weighted mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_mean) rating out of 100 reviews from film critics, it has an average score of 56 from the 37 reviews.[^3967] At the [2009 MTV Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_MTV_Movie_Awards), Lautner was nominated for Male Breakthrough Performance, which was won by co-star [Robert Pattinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Pattinson).[^3968]

Initially, director [Chris Weitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Weitz) wanted to recast the role of Jacob Black for *Twilight*'s sequel, *The Twilight Saga: New Moon*, due to the major physical changes that occur in Black between the two novels, and have an actor that would accurately portray "the new, larger Jacob Black."[^3969] Black's role in the novel also increases significantly, with him falling in love with Bella and becoming a [shapeshifter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapeshifting), putting the actor in a starring role. Representatives for Weitz had stated that they would make a full effort to recast the "high-profile gig", and [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News) confirmed that Weitz was looking at [Michael Copon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Copon) to take on the role; however, [Summit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_Entertainment) said a decision had not been made.[^3969] In an attempt to keep the role, Lautner weight-trained extensively and gained approximately 30 pounds of muscle.[^3970] In January 2009, Weitz and Summit Entertainment announced that Lautner would continue to play the role of Jacob in the sequel.[^3970] In an interview, fellow cast member Kristen Stewart talked about Lautner's transformation saying, "He's an entirely different person physically."[^3971] Stewart later said, "He gets a lot of attention because he's buff, but I think as soon as the movie comes out, people are going to realize that's not why he got the job."[^3957] Co-star Robert Pattinson said after seeing Lautner's body, "I saw him and thought 'Jesus, I'm going to get fired.'"[^3972] In an interview with *[The Wrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wrap)*, Weitz said Lautner deserved a lot of credit for the movie's box office, stating, "If you look at the movie, it should have been the weakest in the franchise, because Robert Pattinson doesn't play as big a role."[^3973] Weitz said Lautner had to "pick up that slack, and if his character hadn't been emotionally, not just physically, appealing, the movie wouldn't have been as big a hit."[^3973] The commercial performance of the film outpaced the first film, setting several box office records including the biggest midnight opening in the United States and Canada and the biggest single-day opening.[^3974] The opening weekend of *New Moon* is the [third highest opening weekend in domestic history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biggest_opening_weekends) with \$142,839,137.[^3975] *The Twilight Saga: New Moon* also has the sixth highest worldwide opening weekend with \$274.9 million total.[^3976] Critical reception was less favorable, with the movie getting a 4.6/10 average from Rotten Tomatoes, and a 44 on Metacritic.[^3977][^3978] Lautner won Favorite Breakout Movie Actor at the [35th People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35th_People's_Choice_Awards).[^3979]

Although it began after the release of the first film, upon release of *New Moon*, Lautner and his co-stars Stewart and Pattinson transitioned to [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol) status, with Lautner particularly admired by teens for his new physical characteristics, becoming a [sex symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_symbol). The trio appeared on many covers and televised appearances together.[^3980] In between the second and third films in the *Twilight* series, Lautner was a part of the [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast) in the movie *[Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day_%282010_film%29)* as Willy Harrington, acting alongside his rumored girlfriend at the time, American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift).[^3981] The duo was nominated at the [2010 MTV Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_MTV_Movie_Awards) for Best Kiss. Although it received generally negative reviews,[^3982] the film grossed \$213 million and had the second biggest opening in the United States for a romantic comedy film.[^3983] Lautner presented at the [2009 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_MTV_Video_Music_Awards) and the [82nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Academy_Awards).[^3984][^3985] Lautner hosted *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live)* on December 12, 2009, making him one of the [youngest celebrity hosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live_hosts) in the show's history.[^3986]

##### 2010-present: Continuing *Twilight*, later projects, and hiatus

Lautner returned for the third *Twilight* film, *The Twilight Saga: Eclipse*, in 2010. Despite receiving mixed reviews from critics, the film surpassed its predecessor to become the highest-grossing film of the [franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twilight_Saga_%28film_series%29) and the highest-grossing romantic fantasy, shapeshifter and vampire movie of all time at [the American and Canadian box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_Canada_and_the_United_States).[^3987] It ranked as the [36th highest-grossing film of all-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_in_Canada_and_the_United_States) in the U.S. and Canada. The popularity of Lautner and his cast members continued to summit, especially via the "Team Edward vs. Team Jacob" campaign that promoted the film.[^3988] Lautner's fanbase also began to expand to older audiences.[^3988] Lautner won Best Fantasy Actor at the [2010 Scream Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Scream_Awards), and he is nominated for Favorite Movie Actor for his role in *Eclipse* at the [37th People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37th_People's_Choice_Awards).[^3989] In November 2010 *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter)* named Lautner as one of the young male actors who are "pushing - or being pushed" into taking over Hollywood as the new "A-List".[^3990][^3991]

Lautner was initially supposed to be in two films, *Northern Lights* and a movie based on [Max Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Steel), but pulled out of both films due to scheduling conflicts and better offers.[^3973] Other planned projects were the lead in a movie about [Stretch Armstrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stretch_Armstrong) and a hostage thriller, *Cancun*.[^3973] Lautner filmed a *[Bourne Identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bourne_Identity_%282002_film%29)*-esque spy film with [Lily Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Collins), entitled *[Abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abduction_%282011_film%29)*. It was released in September 2011 to universally negative reviews from critics[^3992] and Lautner's performance was mostly criticised.[^3993][^3994] For *Abduction*, Lautner won a [Teen Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards) for [Choice Action Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Teen_Choice_Awards) in 2012.[^3995] He appeared in the remaining parts of the *Twilight* series, *The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn* films, which were released over a two-year period from 2011-2012.[^3973] Lautner then filmed *[Grown Ups 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grown_Ups_2)* alongside [Adam Sandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Sandler) and [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock). It was released in September 2013.[^3996]

In 2010, Lautner was considered to be the highest-paid teen actor in Hollywood.[^3997] In February 2014, it was confirmed that Lautner would be joining the [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three) comedy series *[Cuckoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuckoo_%28TV_series%29)*, replacing [Andy Samberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Samberg).[^3998] Lautner has continued in this role, co-starring in the BBC comedy for three series. From September to December 2016, Lautner co-starred on the [Ryan Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Murphy_%28producer%29) comedy horror series *[Scream Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream_Queens_%282015_TV_series%29)*.[^3999] On July 7, 2023, Lautner appeared onstage after singer [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift) premiered a new music video for the song "[I Can See You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Can_See_You_%28song%29)" at the [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour) in Kansas City. The video stars Lautner, [Joey King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_King), and [Presley Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presley_Cash). Lautner inspired her *[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now)* album's single "[Back to December](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_December)".[^4000]

#### Public image

Publications such as *[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ_%28magazine%29)*, *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone)*, and *[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_%28magazine%29)* have referred to Lautner as a [sex symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_symbol), with the latter publication calling the actor a future epitome of [pop culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture).[^3950][^3957][^4001] He has been called the new young adult star that can "both woo the girls with his intensity and impress the boys with his rugged agility."[^3962] According to Mickey Rapkin of *GQ*, the use of Lautner's physique in films has been compared to [Megan Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Fox) in her work.[^3950] After his massive physical change following *[Twilight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight_%282008_film%29)*, Lautner became a tabloid [teen idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_idol) with his co-stars [Robert Pattinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Pattinson) and [Kristen Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Stewart). Lautner, determined to stay in the series, worked out every day and gained over 30 pounds (14 kg) of muscle in order to bulk up for the role of [Jacob Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Black) in the remaining films in *[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twilight_Saga_%28film_series%29)*.[^4002] Michelle Lanz of [MSN Wonderwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSN) said that Lautner's change may have saved his career.[^4003] Several critics credit Lautner's physical characteristics for much of the success of the *Twilight* series, with critic [Sharon Waxman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Waxman) stating, "as a tabloid teen idol, he certainly deserves some credit for *New Moon's* \$700 million worldwide gross."[^3973] Lautner's [abs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen) in particular have been subject to media attention, with *[The Wrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wrap)* stating that companies bidding for the actor in movies in 2011 would "shell out for the young actor's much-on-display though mostly untried abs."[^3973] Mickey Rapkin of *[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ_%28magazine%29)* said, "the film's marketing issues were solved when Lautner's "abdominal muscles became *New Moon*'s main talking point, not to mention his calling card."[^3950] He was named number one on [Access Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_Hollywood)'s "Top 5 Hollywood Abs" list.[^4004]

Before the actor turned 18, his sexualized image was often critiqued, and subject to controversy. In December 2009, Lautner appeared on the cover of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone)* in a wet T-shirt. Jennifer Cady of [E! Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E!) said to wait a few months when Lautner would "be of age, which will make this whole operation you got going on completely legal."[^4005] In his interview with the magazine, after declining to talk about whether he was dating [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift), the magazine pressed Lautner on rumors of him being [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual), which he brushed off.[^4006] Brent Hartinger, a columnist for [AfterElton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AfterElton), blasted the magazine, calling the questioning "unimaginably irresponsible", commenting that Lautner was just "a 17-year old kid" and that while the rumors were baseless and speculation from certain blogs and fans, it was disappointing that a "legitimate media outlet" would print gossip.[^4006] Hartinger said the magazine reached a "new low" and did not have common decency, noting that the line between child and adult "is there for a good reason".[^4006]

Lautner has stated that he does not want to be just known for his looks, as some have attributed his popularity to that and not his actual acting skill. In an interview, the actor revealed that he was originally supposed to have a baring scene in the movie *[Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day_%282010_film%29)*.[^3950] He stated, "The script said we were walking into school and Willy takes off his shirt. I said, 'Whoa, whoa, whoa. Time out. He's gonna take off his shirt in the middle of school? No, no, no. The reason I took off my shirt for *New Moon* is because it's written in the book that way. And there's reasons behind it."[^3950] Lautner later said he would not bare his chest for any role that did not call for it.[^3950] In June 2010, Lautner covered *[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ_%28magazine%29)* magazine.[^3950] The actor was lampooned in conservative writer [Laura Ingraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Ingraham)'s [satirical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire) *[The Obama Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Obama_Diaries)*, commenting to have Lautner as a mascot for the [White House Easter Egg Roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Easter_Egg_Roll), to fit their health-conscious theme, and have Lautner don a furry bunny head and appear shirtless.[^4007] In 2010, Lautner was ranked number two on *[Glamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glamour_%28magazine%29)*'s "50 Sexiest Men of 2010 " list.[^4008] *Men's Health* ranked him at third on their list of "Top 10 Summer Bodies".[^4009] Additionally in 2010, he was ranked fourth on *[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_%28magazine%29)*'s "Most Amazing Bodies" list.[^4010]

#### Personal life

Lautner has an intensive workout regimen, which was profiled by *[Men's Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_Health)*, and follows a specific diet developed while preparing for his role in *The Twilight Saga: New Moon*.[^3950] As of the early 2010s, he continued to train in martial arts regularly.[^3950][^3957] Around the same time, Lautner stated that he does not use drugs or alcohol.[^3957]

Lautner is a fan of the [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions).[^4011]

While filming *[Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day_%282010_film%29)* in October 2009, Lautner began a romantic relationship with his co-star [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift); they ended the relationship later that year.[^4012][^4013] After working with [Lily Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Collins) on *[Abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abduction_%282011_film%29)*, he began dating her in November 2010, and they separated in September 2011.[^4014] From 2013 to 2015, he was in a relationship with Canadian actress and *[Tracers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracers_%28film%29)* co-star [Marie Avgeropoulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Avgeropoulos). Lautner began dating actress and *[Scream Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream_Queens_%282015_TV_series%29)* co-star [Billie Lourd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Lourd) in December 2016; they separated in July 2017.[^4015]

Lautner announced in 2018 that he was in a relationship with Taylor Dome, a nurse.[^4016] The couple married on November 11, 2022, at Epoch Estate Wines in California. Before their wedding, Lautner stated that Dome planned to take his surname, resulting in both partners being named Taylor Lautner.[^4017] She often goes by the nickname "Tay", which helps distinguish between them.[^4018] In September 2026, their first child, a daughter, was born.[^4019]

### The Overcoat (animated film)

***The Overcoat*** ([Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language): Шине́ль, *Shinyél’*) is an unfinished Russian animated [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film) that has been the main project of Russian director and animator [Yuri Norstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Norstein) since 1981. It is based on "[The Overcoat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Overcoat)" (1842), a [short story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_story) by [Nikolai Vasilyevich Gogol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Gogol).

Around 25 minutes were completed by 2004.[^4046] The unfinished film has been shown publicly in several exhibitions of Norstein's work around the world and clips of it have been included in a few documentary films about Russian animation and culture. A Japanese theatrical documentary, *Yuriy Norshteyn: Making The Overcoat*, premiered in 2018.[^4047]

On March 13, 2007, Norstein stated that he planned to release the first 30 minutes of the film with a soundtrack into theatres by the end of 2007.[^4048] However, as of 2026, the film remains unfinished, and its production time of nearly 45 years is the longest for any animated motion picture in history.

#### Plot

The film is based on "The Overcoat" (1842), a short story by Nikolai Vasilyevich Gogol. However, Yuri Norstein has said that "the cinematographer should not be interested in that which is described in detail - he should look to that which is skipped, to that which is implied but is not explicitly written. The break in the text is the most promising, the most alive place for cinema."[^4049]

#### History

Upon finishing his film *[Tale of Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tale_of_Tales_%281979_film%29)* in 1979, Norstein decided that the next project for his small team (consisting of himself as the animator and director, his wife [Francheska Yarbusova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francheska_Yarbusova) as the artist, and his friend Aleksandr Zhukovskiy as the cinematographer) would be an approximately 60-minute-long film based on Gogol's short story *The Overcoat*. Norstein has said that he considers *The Overcoat* to be as important a work of literature as one of the chapters of the [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible) for him personally.[^4050]

By 1981, when work on the film began, Norstein had been working at [Soyuzmultfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuzmultfilm) (the main [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union) animation studio) for 13 years and had worked on some 40 films and directed or co-directed six. Progress was slow, with many interruptions (Norstein estimates that only about three years of work were actually done). Norstein says that Viktor Tinyaev (Виктор Тиняев) helped him during this period. In 1986, with only 10 minutes of the film completed, Norstein was fired from the Soyuzmultfilm studio in which he had worked. This was despite the fact that his films had gathered many international awards and that *Tale of Tales* had been voted the best animated film of all time by a large panel of international critics in 1984.

With the help of [Rolan Bykov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolan_Bykov), Norstein managed to set up his own animation studio in his home. There, he and his team continued to slowly work on the film. Funding has been sporadic and has come from many different sources, including the [Savings Bank of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sberbank) (Sberbank) and [TNK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNK-BP) oil company. A few minutes were shot under the [Soros Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soros_Fund_Management) before 1999.[^4051] Norstein has been known for refusing funding from certain sources. He refused to accept money from [Mikhail Shvydkoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Shvydkoy), the Russian Minister of Culture, saying "one cannot take money from those who don't care about you."[^4052] He also refused help from [Nick Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Park)'s company [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations), accepting from them only a few boxes of lightbulbs.[^4053]

Production came to a temporary halt on November 17, 1999 with the death of cinematographer Aleksandr Zhukovskiy (Александр Жуковский). The loss was crippling for Norstein; he said of Zhukovskiy that he was the only person who ever saw exactly eye-to-eye with him both as an artist and as a friend. By 2001, production had resumed with a new cinematographer, Maksim Granik (Максим Граник), one of Zhukovskiy's students. Production soon halted again, this time for three years. Norstein spent a year and a half making a 3-minute animation for the introduction to *[Good Night, Little Ones!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Night,_Little_Ones!)*, a popular Russian nightly show for young children to watch before they go to bed (it was replaced by a computerized version of the iconic sequences made by [Alexander Tatarsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Tatarsky)).[^4054] He also spent nine months working on a 2-minute sequence for the Japanese collaborative film *[Winter Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Days)* (released in [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_film)).[^4055] Norstein said that this sequence required as much work as a 10-minute film, and that his work on it influenced *The Overcoat* and vice versa (the sequence contains a scene with [Bashō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsuo_Bash%C5%8D) searching for [ticks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick) in his cloak which is similar to a scene in *The Overcoat*).

In a July 4, 2004 interview, Norstein said that 25 minutes of *The Overcoat* had been shot.[^4056]

The studio stopped working on the film for nearly a year while Norstein worked to release his two-volume book, *Snow on the Grass*, released on August 10, 2008.[^4057]

As of March 2013,[^4058] Norstein was still working on the film, his ardent perfectionism has earned him the nickname "The Golden Snail".[^4059] Although he has been offered chances to leave Russia, Norstein believes that finishing his film in "circumstances approaching comfort" would be impossible.[^4051]

In a February 2014 interview, Norstein revealed that profits from sales of his recent books and licensing deals are going into supporting his work on a new film, but refused to confirm whether that film is *The Overcoat*.[^4060] In April 2015, Norstein said in an interview that most of his time is being spent working on *The Overcoat*.[^4061]

#### Cast and crew

Yuri Norstein is the writer, director, and animator for the film. His wife, Francheska Yarbusova, is the main artist responsible for the characters and backgrounds. Other artists who were working on the film as of 2004 were Larisa Zenevich, Lena Sharapova and Valentin Olshvang (who earlier worked with Norstein on the *[Spokoynoy nochi, malyshi!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Night,_Little_Ones!)* sequence).[^4062] Aleksandr Zhukovskiy was the cinematographer until his death on November 17, 1999. A student of his, Maksim Granik, has been the cinematographer since 2001.

There is not expected to be much dialogue in the film. Norstein originally had [Alexander Kalyagin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Kalyagin) in mind to play the main role. However, he has said that his idea of the main character has since changed, and that he is not yet sure who the final voice actor will be.[^4048]

#### Technique

The animation used is [cut-out animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutout_animation), a type of [stop motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_motion). Norstein uses a special technique involving multiple glass panels to give his animation a [three-dimensional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension) look. The camera is placed at the top looking down on a series of glass panels about a meter deep (one every 25-30 cm). The individual glass panels can move horizontally as well as toward and away from the camera (to give the effect of a character moving closer or further away).[^4056] Some scenes required a different approach, as can be seen in the image on the right.

Norstein refuses to use a computer in his work, and says that even watching computer-animated films makes him ill.[^4063]

The film is being shot in black-and-white film. Due to the closure of [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow) labs that develop black-and-white film, Norstein's team is currently being forced to develop it themselves.[^4064]
