### No soap, radio

"**No soap, radio**" is a form of [practical joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Practical_joke) and an example of [surreal comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surreal_comedy). The [joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke) is a prank whereby the punch line has no relation to the body of the joke, but participants in the prank pretend otherwise. The effect is either to trick someone into laughing along as if they "get it" or to ridicule them for not understanding.

The joke became popular in New York in the 1950s.[^4779] The punch line is known for its use as a basic [sociological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociology) and [psychological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology) experiment, specifically relating to [mob mentality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mob_mentality) and the [pressure to conform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_pressure). The basic setup is similar to the [Asch conformity experiments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asch_conformity_experiments), in which people showed a proclivity to agree with a group despite their own judgments.

#### Execution of the prank

This prank usually requires a teller and two listeners, one of whom is an accomplice who already knows the joke and secretly plays along with the teller. The joke teller says something like, "The elephant and the hippopotamus were taking a bath. And the elephant said to the hippo, 'Please pass the soap.' The hippo replied, 'No soap, radio.'"[^4780] The accomplice laughs at the punchline, while the second listener is left puzzled. In some cases, the second listener will pretend to understand the joke and laugh along with the others to avoid appearing foolish.

The purpose of the prank is to elicit one of two responses from the victim:

- *False understanding* - when the victim acts as if the joke is humorous, when in fact the victim does not understand the joke at all.
- *Negative understanding* - when the victim expresses confusion about what the joke means and feels left out (e.g., "I don't get it"). The conspirators are now prepared to mock the victim for the victim's "inability to get it".

Sometimes, if the second listener does not respond right away, there is an "explanation" of the joke to the second listener, which involves the teller and the first listener emphasizing words or elongating pauses, but providing no further information, e.g. "Don't you get it? No *soooap*... *radio*!"

Other examples of the joke:

- A woman goes into her bathroom and is shocked to find an elephant in her bathtub. She asks the elephant, "What are you doing in my bathtub?" The elephant responds, "No soap, radio!"
- Two polar bears are sitting in a bathtub. The first one says, "Pass the soap." The second one says, "No soap, radio!"
- A foreign man is flying in an airplane. He points out of the window at the unfamiliar countryside below and exclaims, "No soap... radio?"

#### Origin

The phrase *[no soap](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/no%20soap)* possibly originated around 1860 when it was first recorded, meaning "I haven't any money" or "I will not lend you money". Its contemporary connotation is "not a chance" or "nothing doing".[^4781] However, the phrase itself was being employed in an absurd and humorous context as early as the 1750s, when it appeared in a well-known piece of [literary nonsense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literary_nonsense) by English dramatist and actor [Samuel Foote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Foote) in order to test the memory of a rival: "So she went into the garden to cut a cabbage-leaf to make an apple-pie; and at the same time a great she-bear, coming up the street, pops its head into the shop. 'What! No soap?' So he died, and she very imprudently married the barber..."[^4782]

[Eric Partridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Partridge) and [William Safire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Safire) dated the phrase to the 1930s or 1940s.[^4783]

#### Comedy

As a [practical joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Practical_joke), the trick is an example of [anti-humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-humor) or [surreal comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surreal_comedy). The scenario resulting from false understanding is a demonstration of [groupthink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groupthink) and [peer pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_pressure) - the desire to conform to one's peers - despite the fact that the entire joke has no hidden meaning, nothing to "get" and no punchline.

#### Popular culture

The joke has become widely known and entered popular culture in other forms, including a radio show named "No Soap-Radio!" It has been used as the name for [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music) bands, as well as a short-lived TV [sketch comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy) show (*[No Soap, Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Soap,_Radio_%28TV_series%29)*) starring [Steve Guttenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Guttenberg) that aired on ABC in spring 1982.[^4784] No Soap Radio was also the name of a radio commercial production company in New York City formed in 1970,[^4785] later renamed No Soap Productions.

In the episode of *The Simpsons* "[Homer the Heretic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homer_the_Heretic)", a radio is seen hanging in the shower, with a label on it showing the brand of radio to be "No Soap,  Radio!"[^4786]

In "[Pie-O-My](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pie-O-My)", the fifth episode of the fourth season of *[The Sopranos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sopranos)*, the name of the band playing at The Crazy Horse is No Soap Radio.

In "Brain Scramblies", the third episode of the second season of *[What We Do in the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_We_Do_in_the_Shadows_%28TV_series%29)*, the vampires' human neighbor Sean exclaims "No soap, Radio!" during an imaginary phone conversation after being "over-hypnotized."

### Blood as food

[Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) is used as [food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_food) in many [religions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion) and [cultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture), often in combination with [meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat). The blood may be in the form of [blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage) or other solidified form, as a thickener for sauces, a [cured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curing_%28food_preservation%29) salted form for times of food scarcity, or in a [blood soup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_soup).[^4787] This is a product from [domesticated animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesticated_animal), obtained at a place and time where the blood can run into a container and be swiftly consumed or processed. In many cultures, the animal is slaughtered. In some cultures and religions, blood is a [taboo food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taboo_food_and_drink).

Blood consists predominantly of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) and [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water), and is sometimes called "liquid meat" because its composition is similar to that of [lean meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean_meat). Blood collected hygienically can be used for human consumption; otherwise it is converted to [blood meal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_meal). Certain [fractions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraction_%28chemistry%29) of animal blood are used in human [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine).[^4788]

#### Methods of preparation

##### Blood sausage

[Blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage) is any [sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sausage) made by cooking [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) with a filler until it is thick enough to congeal when cooled. [Pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig) or [cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle) blood is most often used. Typical fillers include [meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat), [fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat), [suet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suet), [bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread), [rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice), [barley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barley) and [oatmeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oatmeal). Varieties include [biroldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biroldo), [black pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding), [blood tongue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_tongue), [blutwurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blutwurst), [drisheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drisheen), [kishka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishka_%28food%29) ([kaszanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaszanka)), [morcilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morcilla), [moronga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moronga), [mustamakkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustamakkara), [sundae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundae_%28Korean_food%29), [verivorst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verivorst), and many types of [boudin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudin).

##### Pancakes

Blood pancakes are encountered in [Galicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galicia_%28Spain%29) (filloas), Scandinavia, and the Baltic; for example, Swedish [blodplättar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blodpl%C3%A4ttar), Finnish [veriohukainen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veriohukainen), and Estonian veripannkoogid.

##### Soups, stews and sauces

[Blood soups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_soup) and stews, which use blood as part of the broth, include [czernina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czernina), [dinuguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinuguan), [haejangguk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haejangguk), [mykyrokka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mykyrokka), [pig's organ soup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig's_organ_soup), [tiết canh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%E1%BA%BFt_canh) and [svartsoppa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svartsoppa).

Blood is also used as a thickener in [sauces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauce), such as [coq au vin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coq_au_vin) or [pressed duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressed_duck), and puddings, such as [tiết canh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%E1%BA%BFt_canh). It can provide flavor or color for meat, as in [cabidela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabidela).

##### Solidified

Blood can also be used as a solid ingredient, either by allowing it to congeal before use, or by cooking it to accelerate the process. Blood curd is a dish typically found in Asia that consists of cooled and hardened animal blood.

In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China), "[blood tofu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig_blood_curd)" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language): 血豆腐; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin): *xiě dòufǔ*) is most often made with pig's or [duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck)'s blood, although [chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken)'s or cow's blood may also be used. The blood is allowed to congeal and simply cut into rectangular pieces and cooked. This dish is also known in Java as *saren*, made with chicken's or pig's blood. Blood tofu is found in [curry mee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curry_Mee) as well as the [Sichuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan_cuisine) dish, *[mao xue wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_xue_wang)* (毛血旺). Chinese people use pig blood, tofu, and vegetables to make a healthy soup. This soup has a reputation as a healthy and tasty meal in China.[^4789]

In [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary), when a pig is slaughtered in the morning, the blood is fried with onions and served for breakfast.[^4790] *Hagymásvér*, as it is called, is made from pig's blood and [onions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onion), often flavoured with [paprika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paprika) and [marjoram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjoram).

Chicken blood has been used alongside organ meats to combat the [anemia crisis in Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malnutrition_in_Peru).[^4791]

In the Philippines, the street food made from grilled chicken blood is called "betamax", owing to its boxy shape, which resembles [Betamax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betamax) tapes. It is typically sold alongside grilled pork and chicken [isaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_barbecue) (intestines) and other types of [Filipino barbecue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_barbecue).[^4792][^4793]

In [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_cuisine), blood curd is typically made of [cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle) blood and is often used as an ingredient for different kinds of soups and stews, such as [hangover soup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haejang-guk).[^4794]

In [Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibet), congealed [yak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yak)'s blood is a traditional food.[^4795]

In [Vietnamese cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_cuisine), pig blood curd is used in soup based noodle dishes such as [Bún bò Huế](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%BAn_b%C3%B2_Hu%E1%BA%BF) or [Bánh canh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A1nh_canh), [bún riêu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%BAn_ri%C3%AAu), [tiết canh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%E1%BA%BFt_canh) and cháo lòng.

##### Raw

In some cases, blood is used as an ingredient without any additional preparation. Raw blood is not commonly consumed by itself, but may be used as an addition to drinks or other dishes. One example is the drinking of [seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinniped) blood which is traditionally believed by the [Inuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inuit) to bring health benefits.[^4796]

##### Nutrition bars

Russia and ex-USSR countries produce sweet nutrition bars containing cattle blood, known under the generic name [Hematogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hematogen); originally created for treating [anemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anemia), they are also used like regular sweets nowadays.[^4797]

#### Religious consumption of blood

The [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church), as well as the [Eastern Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox), [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran), [Oriental Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriental_Orthodox), and some [Anglican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican) churches, believe that in the [sacrament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrament) of the [Eucharist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucharist), the participants consume the real [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_of_Christ) and [body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_of_Christ) of [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ). The post-communion prayer of the 1662 Anglican Book of Common Prayer describes the meal as "spiritual food". Many other Christian denominations symbolically consume the Eucharist.

The cult of saint [Thomas Becket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Becket) in England included the drinking of "water of Saint Thomas", a mix of water and the remains of the martyr's blood miraculously multiplied. The procedure was frowned upon by the more orthodox due to the similarities with the Eucharist.[^4798]

#### Cultural and religious considerations

Some cultures consider blood to be a [taboo form of food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taboo_food_and_drink). The taboos may be rooted in the fact that consuming greater quantities of blood may cause [iron overload](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_overload) in some genetically predisposed individuals.

In [Abrahamic religions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abrahamic_religions), [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_dietary_laws) and [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_dietary_laws) forbid the consumption of blood. In Judaism, the following passages from the Torah[^4799] are relevant:

- [Leviticus 7:26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leviticus_26) "You may not partake of any blood from a fowl or an animal in all your dwellings."
- Deuteronomy 12:16 "However, you must not consume the blood; you must spill it on the ground like water."
- [Deuteronomy 12:23-24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re'eh) "However, be resolute not to consume the blood, for blood is the animal's life-force. You must not consume it; you must spill it onto the ground like water."

Blood and its by-products are forbidden in [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam), in the Qurʼan, surah 5, [al-Ma'idah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ma'ida), verse 3. In the Christian [New Testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Testament), blood was forbidden by the [Apostolic Decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Decree) due to banning sacrifice of animals before idols ([Acts 15:19-21](https://bible.oremus.org/?passage=Acts%2015:19%E2%80%9321&version=nrsv)), and is still forbidden among [Eastern Orthodox Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church).[^4800]

The Catholic Church determined in the Council of Florence in 1438 that

> the prohibition of the apostles "from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood and from things strangled" \[ [Acts 15:29](https://bible.oremus.org/?passage=Acts%2015:29&version=nrsv)\] befitted that time in which one Church arose from the Jews and the Gentiles, who before lived according to different ceremonies and customs, so that even the Gentiles observed some things in common with the Jews, and occasion was furnished for coming together into one worship of God and one faith, and ground for dissension was removed; since to the Jews, by reason of an ancient custom, blood and things strangled seemed abominable, and they could think that the Gentiles would return to idolatry because of the eating of things sacrificed. But when the Christian religion is so propagated that no carnal Jew appears in it, but all passing over to the Church, join in the same rites and ceremonies of the Gospel, believing "all things clean to the clean" \[ [Titus 1:15](https://bible.oremus.org/?passage=Titus%201:15&version=nrsv)\], with the ending of the cause for this apostolic prohibition, the effect also ended. Thus it declares that the nature of no food, which society admits, is to be condemned, and no distinction is to be made by anyone at all, whether man or woman, between animals, and by whatever kind of death they meet their end; although for the health of body, for the exercise of virtue, for regular and ecclesiastical discipline many things not denied should be given up, since, according to [the Apostle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_the_Apostle), "all things are lawful, but \[not all things are\] expedient" \[ [1 Corinthians 6:12; 10:22](https://bible.oremus.org/?passage=1%20Corinthians%206:12&version=nrsv)\].

#### Dishes

##### Africa

Among the [Maasai people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people), drinking blood from cattle is a part of the traditional diet, especially after special occasions involving a loss of blood such as ritual bloodletting or giving birth.[^4801]

Cow blood is also consumed by the [Bahima people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nkole_people).[^4802][^4803]

The [Herero people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herero_people) consumed cow blood with sour milk.[^4804]

##### Americas

As in Europe, several varieties of [blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage) are also popular in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico) ([moronga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moronga)), [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec) ([boudin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudin)), [Newfoundland and Labrador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_and_Labrador) and the [southwest United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwest_United_States), [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile) (prietas, [ñache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%91ache)), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil) ([chouriço](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chouri%C3%A7o)), [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina), [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay), [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba), and [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico) ([morcilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morcilla)).

###### Brazil

In [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil), the traditional Portuguese dish known as [cabidela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabidela) (see above) is also eaten, as well a stew made of pork blood and offal called [sarapatel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarapatel).

###### Colombia

In the western region of Santander [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia), a dish called pepitoria is made from [rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice) cooked in [goat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat) blood.

###### Mexico

Mexicans from certain regions eat goat's stomach stuffed with [pork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pork) blood and [vegetables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetable) as a delicacy.

###### Peru

In [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru), clotted chicken blood is fried with chili peppers and [Welsh onion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_onion). This dish is called [sangrecita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangrecita).

###### Ecuador

Yaguarlocro is a [potato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potato) [soup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soup) made with sprinklings of goat's blood.

##### Asia

###### China

In [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China) and some regions of [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia), coagulated [chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken), [duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck), [goose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goose) or [pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig) blood, known in Chinese as "blood tofu" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language): [血豆腐](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E8%A1%80%E8%B1%86%E8%85%90); [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin): *xiě/xuè dòu fǔ*) is used in soups. In [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan), *[pig's blood cake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig's_blood_cake)* ([simplified Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters): [猪血糕](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%8C%AA%E8%A1%80%E7%B3%95); [traditional Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters): [豬血糕](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E8%B1%AC%E8%A1%80%E7%B3%95); [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin): *zhū xiě/xuè gāo*) is made of [pork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pork) blood and [sticky rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sticky_rice). It is [fried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frying) or [steamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steaming) as a [snack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snack) or cooked in a [hot pot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_pot).

###### India

In the [South Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_India) state of [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu), [stir-fried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir_frying) [lamb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamb_and_mutton) blood is a common dish for breakfast and lunch. When prepared alone it is called இரத்த பொரியல் (*irattha poriyal*). More commonly it is stir-fried with lamb [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach) and [intestines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intestine) with spices like [ginger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginger), [garlic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garlic), [cloves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clove), [cinnamon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinnamon), red [chili powder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chili_powder), [green chilies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_chilies), [coriander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coriander) powder, [cumin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumin), [shallots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallot) and grated [coconut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut). This dish is very common in the [Kongu Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kongu_Nadu) region as a Breakfast delicacy and [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai) region of Tamil Nadu.

In the coastal [Konkan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konkan) region of India, [Sorpotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarapatel), a dish of [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal) origin is commonly cooked that includes parboiled meat and [offal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offal) which is cooked in a spicy and vinegary sauce. Some people also use the animals' blood for boiling the curry. Sorpotel is primarily made by Catholics of [Goa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goa), [Mangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangalore) and [Bombay East Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_East_Indians) of [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai). In [Kumaon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaon_division), a spicy dish called Luvash is made by pan frying lamb blood with pahadi ghee.

###### Indonesia

In [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia), especially the [Batak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batak_%28Indonesia%29) tribe in [North Sumatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sumatra), pig's blood is used as an ingredient and sauce mixed with [andaliman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andaliman) (*Zanthoxylum acantophodium*) for a cuisine named Sangsang (read [saksang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saksang)). In [Balinese cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balinese_cuisine), pork blood is sometimes added into [lawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawar_%28food%29) dish, a mixture of vegetables, coconut and minced meat mixed with rich herbs and spices to create *lawar merah* (red lawar).

In [Joshua Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Oppenheimer)'s film *[The Look of Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Look_of_Silence)*, several of the anti-Communist militias active in the [Indonesian mass killings of 1965-66](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_mass_killings_of_1965%E2%80%9366) claim that drinking blood from their victims is what prevented them going mad.[^4805]

###### Korea

In [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_cuisine), blood as food is known as *seonji* (선지 \[sʌn.dʑi\]; derived from the [Manchu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchu_language) word *senggi* (ᠰᡝᠩᡤᡳ) meaning "blood").[^4806][^4807] Coagulated cattle *seonji* and [dried radish greens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siraegi) are added to the [beef legbone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagol) broth in order to make *[seonji-guk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seonji-guk)* (blood curd soup).[^4808] *[Sundae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundae_%28sausage%29)*, a blood sausage made generally by boiling or steaming cow or pig's intestines that are stuffed with various ingredients, such as pig's blood, cellophane noodles, [kimchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimchi), scallions, etc.

###### Nepal

In northern region of [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal), *[Gyuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gyuma)* a blood sausage is a popular dish commonly eaten by locals. It is made of yak's blood and meat. The fillings also include buck wheat flour and other spices. The sausage is also used in lentils or prepared in stir fry dishes.

People of Newar community also consume popular dish called "cho hee," which means blood that is prepared by steaming the blood with some local spices. It is consumed by most of the locals in Patan, Kathmandu, Bhaktapur area of Nepal.

###### Philippines

In the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines), a popular dish called *[dinuguan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinuguan)* is made from pig's blood and [offal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offal) seasoned with [chili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siling_mahaba) and is traditionally eaten with white rice or steamed rice cakes (*[puto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puto_%28food%29)*). Numerous variants exist throughout the islands. Dinuguan can also be served without using any [offal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offal), using only choice cuts of pork. In [Batangas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batangas), this version is known as *sinungaok*. It can also be made from beef and chicken meat, the latter being known as *dinuguang manok* ('chicken dinuguan').[^4809][^4810] The Northern [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon) versions of the dish namely the Ilocano *dinardaraan* and the [Ibanag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibanag_people) *zinagan* are often drier with toppings of deep-fried pork intestine cracklings. These versions are sometimes known as "crispy dinuguan" elsewhere. The [Itawis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itawis) of Cagayan also have a pork-based version that has larger meat chunks and more fat, which they call *twik*.

Aside from *dinuguan*, a native [blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage) known as *[pinuneg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinuneg)* also exists among the [Kankanaey people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankanaey_people) of the highlands of [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon).[^4811][^4812] Cubes of pork blood grilled on skewers is also a common street food throughout the Philippines. These are known colloquially as "betamax" (after its resemblance to [Betamax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betamax) tapes).[^4813]

The Ilocano crispy pork dish *[bagnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagnet)* may also sometimes be dipped in raw pig's blood. Though this is rare.[^4814] In [Western Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Visayas), the meat-and-liver stew *bas-uy* can also be enriched with blood.[^4815]

###### Thailand and Laos

Coagulated [chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken), [duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck), [goose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goose) or [pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig) blood is used in soups, such as the classic Thai dish *Tom Lued Moo* (pork blood soup). Thailand also has a dish known as *[Nam Tok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_tok_%28food%29)*, which is a spicy soup stock enriched with raw cow or pig's blood. It is often used to enrich regular [noodle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noodle) dishes, as well as in [Khao soi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khao_soi).[^4816]

In [Laos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laos) and [Northeast Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isan)), a raw version of *[laap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laap)*, a meat [salad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salad), is made with [minced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mincing) raw meat, [seasoned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasoning) in [spices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice), and covered with blood. The spicy noodle soup [Nam ngiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_ngiao) and certain variants of [Khao soi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khao_soi) of the cuisine of [Shan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shan_State) and [Northern Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Thailand) contain diced curdled blood.[^4816][^4817]

###### Vietnam

In [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam), congealed pork blood is used in [Bún bò Huế](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%BAn_b%C3%B2_Hu%E1%BA%BF) (a spicy noodle soup), as well as [congee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congee) (a type of rice porridge). It is simply solidified, then put into the broth to absorb the flavor. Blood is also consumed raw in Vietnam although it is not so popular nowadays due to health concern and a better understanding of how raw blood may contain parasites and other organisms that are harmful to humans.

This type of raw blood dish is called "[tiết canh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%E1%BA%BFt_canh)", literally translated as "blood soup". As its name suggests, the soup is prepared with raw and uncooked animal blood. Firstly, blood is collected when the animal is slaughtered, then it is mixed with a little bit of fish sauce or salt water to prevent it from congealing (this step varies a lot from person to person and from region to region), this is to have time to prepare the other part of the dish, usually a mixture of the slaughtered animal's heart, liver, stomach, some time, its kidney, being diced and cooked.

Then, the cooked mixture is divided into serving portions. The blood is now mixed with regular drinking water (there is specific ratio between the blood and the water), then it will be poured onto the cooked mixture. After 10-15 minutes, the blood will start to congeal and the final product will have a consistency similar to jelly. Various herbs, roasted and smashed peanut are topped on the congealed blood to enhance its flavor.

This dish is usually made with pig's blood and duck's blood but it can also be made from any type of animal's blood.

In China and Vietnam certain types of [snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake) blood are considered to be an [aphrodisiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphrodisiac), and are drunk with [rice wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_wine).

##### Europe

###### Czech Republic

In the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic), pig's blood from traditional [pig slaughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig_slaughter) is used to make blood soup *[prdelačka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prdela%C4%8Dka)* and blood sausages *[jelito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaszanka)*.

###### Finland

In [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland), pig's blood is used, with [milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milk), [flour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flour) and [molasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molasses), to make blood [pancakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancake) (*[veriohukainen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veriohukainen)*), usually served with [lingonberry jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingonberry_jam).[^4818] Different types of sausages are also common, including [mustamakkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustamakkara) and [ryynimakkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryynimakkara). *Verileipä* is a type of bread made with blood. *[Veripalttu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blodpalt)* is another dish available in some parts of the country.

###### France

In France, there is "[sanquette](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanquette)", a solidified/curd blood in a pan, and "[boudin noir](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudin%20noir)", a sort of sausage.

###### Germany

In [Northern Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Germany) pig's blood used to be traditionally mixed with [vinegar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinegar), scraps, spices and [sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar) to make [schwarzsauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarzsauer). It is eaten warm or [preserved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_preservation) in jars. Changes in taste and lifestyle have made this an uncommon dish.[^4819]

###### Greece

In ancient [Lakedaimon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakedaimon), the [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greece) [city-state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-state) of [Sparta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparta), the [black broth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_broth) was common: a soup with pork meat and blood.

###### Hungary

In [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary), *hagymás vér* (pan-fried pig's/[mangalica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangalica)'s blood with onions) often served with [hot peppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chili_pepper) and *véres hurka* (a kind of blood sausage made with pig's blood, bacon, pork, rice, onion, salt and various herbs and spices) are common winter foods. The dark mahagony colored Véres pite (bloody pie) is also made.[^4820] [Pig slaughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig_slaughter) is considered a cultural event, when the villagers feast together. Here, all parts of the pig are used, from its blood and [cloven hoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloven_hoof) (out of which they make körömpörkölt) to its head. In fact, the pig's heart and lungs are also often consumed.

In the old days, they also used to make a soup/sauce called Black soup (fekete leves) out of it, similar to [svartsoppa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svartsoppa). Currently, the word *black soup* (in [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary)) is used to describe an unpleasant obligation, an impending sudden negative event. Legend has it that the [Turks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_people) invited a Hungarian nobleman to dinner. The soldiers were ordered to attack him when "The black soup is still left" was said, hence the phrase.[^4821]

###### Italy

In [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy), the [sanguinaccio dolce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanguinaccio_dolce) is a [pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudding) made with pig blood, chocolate, sugar, pine nuts, raisins and milk.[^4822]

[Biroldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biroldo) is a [blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage) traditionally made with parts of [pigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigs) [offal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offal) like heart, lungs and tongues.[^4823]

###### Netherlands

[Balkenbrij](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkenbrij) is a Dutch food made by combining pig's blood with a variety of ingredients, principally flour or oatmeal, and pig organs, such as intestines. Black pudding, in Dutch "[bloedworst](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/bloedworst)," is also consumed. In the [Limburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limburg_%28Netherlands%29) province bloedworst, in Limburgish "[poetes](https://li.wikipedia.org/wiki/poetes)" or "trip," is consumed with apples baked in a thick syrup called stroop.

###### Poland

[Czernina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czernina) (black soup) is a Polish soup made of duck blood and clear poultry broth, sometimes known as "duck soup". Hen, rabbit or pig blood can also be used.

[Kaszanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaszanka) is the Polish incarnation of [blood sausage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_sausage). It's made of pig's blood and [buckwheat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckwheat) or [barley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barley) [kasza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasha).

###### Portugal

In [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal), the northern region known as Minho has a traditional blood soup named papas de sarrabulho. "Papas" translates as "mash" and "sarrabulho" is a popular expression for coagulated blood, so the literal translation would be "mashed blood". The soup is made with pig's blood, chicken meat, pork, [ham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ham), [salami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salami), [lemon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemon) and [bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread), and is typically sprinkled with [cumin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumin), which provides the dish with its distinctive odor. It is usually served in the winter because it is a rather heavy dish. The dish is seldom eaten in southern Portugal. Also very popular, is [*morcela*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding) sausage, a type of black pudding. Another traditional Portuguese dish known as [cabidela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabidela) is also made by cooking chicken or [rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit) in its own blood, sometimes diluted with vinegar. The same [cabidela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabidela) dish is done with lamprey eel's blood and flesh along with rice, during the months of March and April following the migration of these fishes throughout Portugal's rivers.[^4824]

There is also a candy called Papas de moado, which is prepared from pig's blood, flour, sugar, nuts and spices, mainly in the [Mondego River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondego_River) region.

###### Romania

In [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania) there is a traditional sausage prepared with blood named *sângerete*,[^4825] literally meaning "a thing from hemoragy" (it came from *sângera* - "hemoragy" from *sânge* - "blood")), and it is prepared especially during the Ignat (the pig carving holiday).

###### Spain

In [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain), the *morcilla* sausage is a kind of [black pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding) mainly made with pig blood, with spices, fat, and sometimes vegetables. In [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia) *sangre encebollada* and [Valencian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencian_language) *sang amb ceba* are popular dishes made with chicken or pork solidified blood and onion.[^4826] In [Galician cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galician_cuisine), *filloas* (a dish similar to [crêpes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cr%C3%AApe)) are sometimes made with pork blood.

###### Sweden

In [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden), the blood soup [svartsoppa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svartsoppa), made with goose blood, is traditionally eaten on the eve of St. Martin, especially in the southern region of [Skåne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sk%C3%A5ne).[^4827] Other popular dishes, with blood as one of the ingredients include [blodpudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding) (blood pudding), [blodplättar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blodpl%C3%A4ttar) (blood pancakes), [blodpalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blodpalt) (potato dumplings flavoured with reindeer or pig blood) and [paltbröd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paltbr%C3%B6d) (bread with blood in it, which is dried and boiled and eaten together with fried pork and bèchamel or onion sauce).

###### United Kingdom and Ireland

In [Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland), and some [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations) countries, "[black pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding)" or "[blood pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pudding)" is made from blood and some filler [grains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_grain) and spices, often [oatmeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oatmeal).

In [Montgomeryshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomeryshire), [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales), goose blood was used to make a pastry tart at Christmas time.[^4828]

In [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland), there is ample evidence of the persistence of the practice of bleeding live cattle until well into the 19th century. It was considered to be a preventative measure against cattle diseases, and the blood drawn, when mixed with butter, herbs, oats or meal, provided a nutritious emergency food.[^4829]

#### In Fiction

- [Klingons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klingon_culture) drink Klingon bloodwine in [Star Trek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek).

### Feetloaf

**Feetloaf** is a novelty dish intended to be served on [Halloween](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween). The earliest known reference is a 2009 cooking blog which was based on a recipe found in a seasonal cookbook sold at a [grocery store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grocery_store) checkout counter. The original recipe described a [meatloaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meatloaf) molded into the shape of a [human foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_foot), using [brazil nuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_nut) as [toenails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_%28anatomy%29) and [ketchup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ketchup) or [barbecue sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbecue_sauce) to mimic [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).[^4830]

The dish was originally called "Bloody Stump" or "Feet of Meat".[^4831] The first known use of the term "Feetloaf" was in a 2014 *[Today Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_%28American_TV_program%29)* interview with Laurin Sydney, [Kathie Lee Gifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathie_Lee_Gifford) and [Hoda Kotb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoda_Kotb).[^4832][^4833] A contemporaneous [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News) story alternately referred to the dish as "Feet Loaf" (two words) and "Meat Foot".[^4834] A 2016 *[New York Times Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Magazine)* article mentioned feetloaf as being the subject of an [Amy Sedaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Sedaris) Instagram post.[^4835]

In 2019, *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post)* featured the dish in a pre-Halloween article, citing a [tweet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter) by rapper Richard Wilson (known by his stage name Lil Rich Aka Crash). According to *The Post*, the tweet had nearly 28,000 incoming links and had amassed almost 9,000 retweets. The version of the recipe described by *The Post* used slivers of [onion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onion) instead of brazil nuts for toenails, and [parsnips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsnip) to simulate a sawed-off [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia). Serving suggestions included using a small [handsaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand_saw) instead of a knife, and a quarter-size [sheet pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheet_pan) as a platter, mimicking a laboratory tray.[^4831] In the same year, Chris Prosperi of [NBC Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WVIT) noted that there were "tons of pictures" of feetloaf available on the internet.[^4836]

In 2021, *[The Daily Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Mirror)* reported on a variation of the recipe which included a [cheese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese) topping. The dish was described as "absolutely disgusting".[^4837]

#### In fiction

Feetloaf is mentioned in the 1967 [children's book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_literature) *The Hungry Thing*. When the [title character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_character), a creature with a "Feed Me" sign hung around its neck, requests feetloaf, other characters ponder what it might be. A wiseman suggests it might be "a kind of shoe pudding that grows in a tree", and the cook counters that it "tastes sweet, and it's eaten by kings when they dine in bare feet".[^4838] The book uses incremental rhyming changes to lead the reader from made-up nonsense spoken by the monster to an actual culinary dish; "feetloaf" becomes "beetloaf" and then "meatloaf".[^4839]

### Milbenkäse

**Milbenkäse** ("[mite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mite) cheese"), called **Mellnkase** in the local dialect and often known as **Spinnenkäse** ("spider cheese"), is a German speciality [cheese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese). It is made by flavouring balls of [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark_%28cheese%29) (a type of soft cheese) with [caraway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caraway) and [salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt), allowing them to dry, and then leaving them in a wooden box containing [rye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rye) flour and [cheese mites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese_mite) for about three months. An [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) in the [digestive juices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastric_acid) excreted by the mites causes the cheese to ripen.[^4840] Milbenkäse tastes similar to [Harzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harzer) cheese, but with a bitter note (increasing with age) and a zesty aftertaste. Mites clinging to the cheese rind are consumed along with the cheese.

Historically, the cheese was produced in the [Zeitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitz) and [Altenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altenburg) districts of the Saxony-Anhalt / [Thuringia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thuringia) border region; today it is produced exclusively in the village of [Würchwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W%C3%BCrchwitz), in the state of [Saxony-Anhalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxony-Anhalt).

The traditional method of making Milbenkäse, which dates back to the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages), was nearly lost by 1970, with only the elderly Liesbeth Brauer knowing the technique. Local science teacher Helmut Pöschel was taught the proper way to make it and together with his associate, Christian Schmelzer, succeeded in revitalizing the tradition. A Cheese Mite Memorial was later erected at Würchwitz to celebrate the renaissance of Milbenkäse production.

#### Production

[Quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark_%28cheese%29) flavoured with salt and caraway is shaped into small balls, cylinders or wheels, and dried. It is then placed in a wooden box containing rye flour and inhabited by *[Tyrophagus casei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrophagus_casei)* mites for at least three months. The digestive juices of the mites diffuse into the cheese and cause [fermentation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermentation_%28food%29); the flour is added because the mites would otherwise simply eat the whole cheese instead of just nibbling away at the crust as is desired. After one month, the cheese rind turns yellow; after three months, reddish brown. Some producers allow the cheese to ripen for up to one year, until it has turned black.

#### Legality

Milbenkäse falls into a legal grey area: [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) regulations allow the sale of foodstuffs containing living animals if they are "prepared for placing on the market for human consumption".[^4841] On the other hand, cheese mites or their digestive juices are not explicitly permitted as [additives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_additive) for cheese according to the relevant German food ordinances (*Zusatzstoff-Zulassungsverordnung* and *Käseverordnung*). Milbenkäse is produced under a permit by the local [food safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_safety) office, and [Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard_Analysis_and_Critical_Control_Points) compliance of the product is enforced.

[^4840]: ["Würchwitzer Milbenkäse \| Ein lebendiger Käse mit Tradition"](https://www.slowfood.de/was-wir-tun/arche_des_geschmacks/die_arche_passagiere/wuerchwitzer_milbenkaese) \[Würchwitz mite cheese \| A living cheese with tradition\]. *Slow Food Deutschland (SFD)* (in German).

[^4841]: [Consolidated text: Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 January 2002 laying down the general principles and requirements of food law, establishing the European Food Safety Authority and laying down procedures in matters of food safety](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:02002R0178-20240701): Article 2(b)

### Spotted dick

**Spotted dick** is a traditional [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom) steamed [pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudding), historically made with [suet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suet) and [dried fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dried_fruit) (usually [currants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zante_currant) or [raisins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raisin)) and often served with [custard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Custard).

Non-traditional variants include recipes that replace suet with other fats (such as butter), or that include eggs to make something similar to a sponge pudding or cake.[^4842]

#### Etymology

*Spotted* is a reference to the [dried fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dried_fruit) in the pudding (which resembles spots).[^4843] The word *dick* refers to pudding. In late 19th century [Huddersfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield), for instance, a glossary of local terms stated: "*Dick*, plain pudding. If with [treacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treacle) sauce, treacle dick."[^4844] This sense of *dick* may be related to the word *dough*.[^4845] In the variant name *spotted dog*, *dog* is a variant form of *dough*.[^4846]

#### History

The dish is first attested in [Alexis Soyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Soyer)'s *The Modern Housewife or, Ménagère*, published in 1849,[^4847] in which he described a recipe for "Plum Bolster, or Spotted Dick - Roll out two pounds of paste \[...\] have some [Smyrna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smyrna) raisins well washed".[^4848]

The name "spotted dog" first appeared in 1855, in C.M. Smith's "Working-men's Way in the World" where it was described as a "very marly species of plum-pudding". This name, along with "railway cake", is most common in Ireland where it is made more similar to a [soda bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soda_bread) loaf with the addition of currants.[^4843]

The *[Pall Mall Gazette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pall_Mall_Gazette)* reported in 1892 that "the Kilburn Sisters \[...\] daily satisfied hundreds of dockers with soup and Spotted Dick".[^4844]

### Carmona wine urn

The **Carmona wine urn** is a first-century [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire) [glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass) urn containing intact [wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine). The urn was discovered in 2019 in [Carmona, Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmona,_Spain) during excavations of the city's western Roman [necropolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necropolis). Analysis of the urn's contents five years after its discovery demonstrated the contents to be the oldest surviving liquid wine in the world. This surpasses the previous record holder, the [Speyer wine bottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speyer_wine_bottle) (discovered in 1867), by three centuries.[^4849][^4850]

#### Discovery

Carmona, known as *Carmo* during Roman rule, was part of the province of [Hispania Baetica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispania_Baetica). In the first century, agriculturalist [Columella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucius_Columella) wrote of the production of [white wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_wine) in the locality, as well as that of olive oil and wheat.[^4850][^4851][^4852]

In 2019, house renovations at 53 Sevilla Street revealed an access shaft to an unlooted Roman [mausoleum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausoleum) measuring 3.29 m long, 1.73 m wide, and 2.41 m high; the chamber contained eight niches with [grave goods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_goods) and the remains of two individuals named Hispanae and Senicio.[^4850][^4853] Niche 8 contained a glass vessel called an *olla ossuaria* inside of a lead case. The vessel contained five liters of wine mixed with the [cremains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cremains) of the deceased and a gold ring at the bottom.[^4849][^4850]

#### Content analysis

Roman wine in the Baetic region was often preserved by adding [gypsum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gypsum), cooked [musts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Must) high in sugar, or [salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt).[^4850]

Analysis of mineral salts in the wine revealed a high concentration of [potassium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potassium) salts, indicative of the cremains in the wine, and of [silicon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon), [sodium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium), and [aluminium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aluminium), probably due to two millennia of contact with the glass urn.[^4850][^4854] The wine's mineral content was similar to that of [sherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherry) from [Jerez de la Frontera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerez_de_la_Frontera) and [fino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fino) from [Condado de Huelva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condado_de_Huelva) and [Montilla-Moriles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montilla-Moriles).[^4850]

Analysis of [polyphenols in the wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenolic_content_in_wine) identified [quercetin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercetin), [4-hydroxybenzoic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4-hydroxybenzoic_acid), [apigenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apigenin), [vanillin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanillin), [isoquercetin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isoquercetin), [naringin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naringin), and [rutin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutin), confirming the liquid's identification as wine. Each of these polyphenols is present in fino produced in [Doña Mencía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do%C3%B1a_Menc%C3%ADa). Although the wine is now reddish, a lack of [syringic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syringic_acid) indicated that the wine was originally [white wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_wine).[^4850][^4855]

### Vodka eyeballing

**Vodka eyeballing** is the practice of consuming [vodka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodkas) by pouring it into the [eye sockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_socket), where it is absorbed through the mucous membranes of the region into the bloodstream. Reports of this practice as a new [fad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fad) surfaced in the media beginning in 2010,[^4856][^4857][^4858][^4859][^4860][^4861] as hundreds of clips of persons purporting to engage in the practice were posted on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube).[^4862] The practice is promoted by advocates as causing rapid intoxication, but the amount of [alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_%28drug%29) absorbed by the eye is low.[^4863]

Some observers maintained that the phenomenon was not a real craze, describing the coverage as a [media feeding frenzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_feeding_frenzy) and part of "a long history of trend pieces that come out of nowhere". The initial press coverage in British tabloid *[The Daily Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Mail)* was criticized for basing its entire story on an injury from a single student stunt, and extrapolating this into a "trend" after a YouTube search showed hundreds of similar videos.[^4864][^4865][^4866] Journalist [Michael Strangelove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Strangelove) said that the videos, which date back to 2006, seemed genuine and should not be dismissed as a deceptive "prank" against the media.[^4867]

The 2000 comedy film *[Kevin & Perry Go Large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_&_Perry_Go_Large)* includes a character called Eyeball Paul who engages in the practice.[^4862]

The practice formed part of the fictional plot of the February 6, 2013 episode of the Canadian TV series *[Trauma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trauma_%28Canadian_TV_series%29)*, leading to a young woman receiving (successful) [cornea transplants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneal_transplantation).[^4868]

#### Adverse effects

Vodka eyeballing can cause [corneal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneal) abrasions and scarring, promote [angiogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiogenesis) in the eye (and thereby cause loss of vision), and increase the risk for eye infections;[^4863] it has been condemned by the [American Academy of Ophthalmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Ophthalmology).[^4869]

### MaDonal

**MaDonal** ([Sorani Kurdish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorani_Kurdish_language): مادۆنال) is a [restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurant) located in the city of [Sulaymaniyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulaymaniyah), [Iraqi Kurdistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Kurdistan). It is designed to resemble the fast food chain [McDonald's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's) both in appearance and in [menu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menu);[^4870][^4871][^4872][^4873] for instance, MaDonal's menu includes "[Big Macks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Mac)."[^4874][^4875] It is one of two McDonald's-like restaurants in the town; the other one, Matbax, claims that MaDonal is "cheap quality".[^4876]

The owner, Suleiman Qassab, fought in the [Kurdish resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshmerga) during the 1970s. He became a refugee in [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna), [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria), where he got a job as a [cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_%28profession%29) at McDonald's. In the 1990s, he applied for permits to create a McDonald's in Iraq, but the McDonald's Corporation turned him down, due to [economic sanctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_sanction) imposed during the regime of [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein), as well as the [controlled economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_economy) of Iraq at the time. In response, he established MaDonal Restaurant, which is still in business.[^4877] Since establishing MaDonal, Qassab has offered free food to [U.S. forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_force_in_Iraq), been [threatened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_attack),[^4878][^4879][^4880][^4881][^4882][^4883] and has become a "Kurdish celebrity."[^4884] Qassab hopes to one day turn MaDonal into an actual McDonald's restaurant.[^4885][^4886]

MaDonal is popular with Sulaymaniyah's youth,[^4887][^4888] and the [upper middle class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_middle_class).[^4889] It is open even during [Ramadan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramadan), the month of [fasting in Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fasting_in_Islam).[^4890]

[Sociologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociologist) [George Ritzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Ritzer) sees MaDonal as part of a trend of other countries developing their own regional variations of McDonald's.[^4891][^4892] [Journalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalist) [Christopher Hitchens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Hitchens) said it was "reassuring" to see signs of progress like MaDonal "in an atmosphere that only a few years ago was heavy with miasmic decay and the reek of poison gas."[^4893]

Qassab is just one of many who have requested permission to open up a McDonald's in Iraq.[^4894][^4895] Should this happen, there has been speculation by some about whether McDonald's will eventually take legal action against MaDonal.[^4896][^4897][^4898][^4899] However, MaDonal appears safe for now, as one journalist notes: "The flow of applications to open an Iraqi McDonald's stopped as quickly as it started, and the corporate lawyers never came to Sulaymaniyah."[^4900]

### Bat and trap

**Bat and trap** is an English bat-and-ball [pub game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pub_game).[^4901] The game has its origins from the early 14th century and existed in its modern form by 1825. It is still played in [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent), and occasionally in [Brighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton).

There are several active leagues in Kent and local trophy competitions such as between [The Handsome Sam](https://camra.org.uk/pubs/handsome-sam-whitstable-132831) and [The Brickfield](https://camra.org.uk/pubs/brickfield-micropub-swalecliffe-197289) pubs. The Brickfield has Bat & Trap set up in their garden.

By the late 20th century it was usually only played on [Good Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday) in Brighton, on the park called [The Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Level,_Brighton), which has an adjacent pub called The Bat and Ball, whose sign depicts the game. Brighton & Hove City Council started a Bat and Trap club based at The Level in 2013, as part of the Activities Plan associated with a £2.2m Heritage Lottery Fund and Big Lottery Fund-funded restoration of the park.

#### Rules

The game is played between two teams of up to eight players. At any one time, one team is batting and the other is bowling. The game involves placing a heavy solid-rubber ball, similar to a [lacrosse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrosse) ball, on one end of a "trap", which is a low wooden box 22 inches (560 mm) long, 5 inches wide, and 5 inches (130 mm) high, on top of which is a simple see-saw mechanism. Each player in turn on the batting side hits the opposite end of the see-saw lever (the "striker") with their bat, so as to propel the ball into the air, and then, using the same bat, attempts to hit the ball between two 7-foot (2.1 m) high posts situated 21 yards (19 m) away and 13 feet 6 inches (4.11 m) apart at the other end of the playing area, or "pitch".

The bowling side stand behind and between the posts. If any of them catches the ball before it hits the ground the batsman is out. The batsman is also out if he or she fails to hit the ball between the posts at a height not exceeding 7 feet (2.1 m). After each successful hit, one fielder (the one whose turn it is to bowl next), returns the ball to the batting end by hurling, tossing, or bowling it back towards the trap, attached to the front of which is a 5-inch (130 mm) square target, or "wicket", hinged at the bottom. If the bowler hits the wicket with the ball so as to knock it flat, the batsman is "bowled out". If the bowler does not succeed, the batsman scores one run and continues to play. Once all the members of the first batting team are out, the batting and bowling teams change places and the game continues until all players on both sides have batted.

#### American version

In the American rules of bat and trap, there are several differences in the equipment and game mechanics as well as the layout of the pitch. Each team is limited to 4 players. The trap is 6 inches by 6 inches, and it has a yellow background with a black "X" mark across the front. The posts are 1-2 feet high. There are two additional lines, one of which extends across the field at a right angle 10 yards in front of the trap; this line is the "foul line". Balls put into play must not touch the ground prior to hitting this line or the batter is called out. In addition, there is an additional line 5 yards behind the posts; this line is known as the "back line", and fair hit balls that cross the line, either before touching a fielder or after, or on the ground or in the air but below the imaginary line demarcating the fair zone, score four runs for the batting side. This is known as a "four", and the fielding team does not have the opportunity to roll out the batter following a four. Since the posts are only 1-2 feet, the top of the fair hit zone is demarcated by an imaginary line running from the top of the tallest fielding player's head. Batted balls that travel above this imaginary line are automatically out.

### The Gay Footballer

**The Gay Footballer** or **@FootballerGay** was an [anonymous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymity) account on the social media website [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter) during July 2019. In its posts beginning on 5 July, the account claimed to be owned by a British [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football) player in the [English Football League Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EFL_Championship), and alleged that he was a [closeted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closeted) [gay man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_men) under the age of 23. The user promised that he would [come out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out) on 24 July by revealing his identity, which if true would have made him the first player to come out as gay while playing in the top four [divisions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system) of English football since [Justin Fashanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fashanu) in 1990. The @FootballerGay account was instead deleted on 24 July, after its alleged owner had posted that he was "not strong enough to do this" the previous day.

While live, the account went [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_phenomenon), but received mixed responses including expressions of support from current and former players such as former footballer [Gary Lineker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lineker), active footballer [Marvin Sordell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Sordell), and [rugby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union) player [Gareth Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Thomas_%28rugby,_born_1974%29), as well as [homophobic abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia). There was significant skepticism of the account's legitimacy from other Twitter users and media as well as Justin Fashanu's niece [Amal Fashanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Fashanu), and accusations from [LGBTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_people) activist [Peter Tatchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Tatchell) and others that it was a [hoax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoax). Media coverage on the topic was international,[^4902] and there was widespread speculation on the account's true identity.

#### Background

In 2019, no active professional footballer had come out as gay while playing in the top four divisions of English football since Justin Fashanu in 1990.[^4903][^4904] Fashanu had committed suicide eight years after coming out.[^4905]

#### History

##### Launch

| **The Gay Footballer** (@FootballerGay) tweeted: |
|--------------------------------------------------|

> I'm a professional footballer, playing for a club in the @SkyBetChamp. I will be revealing my identity soon, but I am a proud gay man, hoping to break the mould. I am under the age of 23, and today I came out to my family. Soon, I will come out publicly. \#loveislove \#Pride \#LGBT

5 July 2019[^4906][^4907]

The user launched their account by following multiple leading LGBTQ organisations and media outlets.[^4903] The account then posted a [tweet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweet_%28social_media%29) on 5 July 2019,[^4906] which said, "I'm a professional footballer, playing for a club in the \[EFL Championship\]. I will be revealing my identity soon, but I am a proud gay man, hoping to break the mould. I am under the age of 23, and today I came out to my family. Soon, I will come out publicly."[^4903][^4906] The account's bio similarly read, "I'm a professional footballer, currently playing in The Championship. I will reveal my identity soon, but I am a PROUD gay man."[^4908]

A few days after launching the account, the user tweeted that their [football club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_club_%28association_football%29) was aware of his sexuality and had shown support for his decision to come out to the public, stating that "It was reassuring for them to be fully aware that performance and consistency is based around individuals that are at peace with themselves and the decision to be open is instrumental in ensuring I can be myself."[^4903] The account tweeted about seeking advice on the issue from his manager and club chairman,[^4907] noting that "they have assured me that they would both do absolutely everything to support me in this process," and that there would be a further meeting 14 July to discuss the 'next steps'.[^4909] The account claimed that the club would organise a press conference, also noting that homophobic abuse had been directed at the account since it had opened.[^4907] On 9 July, sports broadcaster [Jim White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_White_%28presenter%29) said he had been in correspondence with the alleged footballer and said "he has my full support." At this time, the account had over 26,000 followers.[^4909]

Gay rugby player [Gareth Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Thomas_%28rugby,_born_1974%29) has since said he had offered private support to the alleged footballer, and that he had not asked for his name but that the account holder told him the club he had played for.[^4910] [Ryan Atkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Atkin), a football [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_%28association_football%29) who had come out as gay in 2017 and whom had been followed by The Gay Footballer on Twitter, said he had followed the account back and similarly sent a direct message of support, and had messaged with him over the following weeks, receiving a phone call from the account holder with a withheld number. Atkin also said they had arranged to meet in person for coffee in London, but that the alleged footballer cancelled this meeting.[^4911] In [direct messages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_message) to the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC), the alleged account holder said he had received "positive messages" as well as "[death threats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_threat) and vile abuse," and wrote that "Whilst I know several others within the game who are gay/bi they are too scared to be open about it, some of them go as far as employing girlfriends to keep it secret. I don't want to do that. I want to be able to go anywhere, with anyone, without the fear of being outed by the rag tops \[newspapers\] or someone with a camera phone. I truly believe that I need this to be in the open, which will hopefully make it easier for others to do the same."[^4905] *[Sky News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_News)* also spoke to the account holder in a phone interview around 12 July, by which point the account had 31,000 followers, but could not verify if his claims were true despite his insistence that he was "genuine".[^4907] On 21 July,[^4906] the user stated that they would announce their identity on 24 July and promised a news conference and media interviews.[^4903] With the account at over 40,000 followers, many users were arguing that the account was fake at this time.[^4908]

##### Deletion

| **The Gay Footballer** (@FootballerGay) tweeted: |
|--------------------------------------------------|

> I thought I was stronger. I was wrong.

23 July 2019[^4904][^4912]

On 23 July, by which time the account had gained over 50,000 followers, The Gay Footballer put out two posts. The first post read, "I thought I was stronger. I was wrong", and the second explained, "Call me all the names under the sun, belittle me and ridicule me, a lot will, and I can't change that, but I'm not strong enough to do this. Just remember that I've got feelings, without coming out I can't convince anybody otherwise, but this isn't a hoax. I wouldn't do that."[^4904] The account's bio was also changed to "I thought I was strong enough. I'm not."[^4913] Following this, the account was deleted on 24 July.[^4904][^4903]

#### Responses

When it was active, the account went [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_phenomenon).[^4906] It received a mixed response with some users openly questioning the account's legitimacy and others either tweeting their support or responding with abuse.[^4903][^4914] Former [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team) striker Gary Lineker showed his support,[^4903][^4906] as did [Burton Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burton_Albion_F.C.) [forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_%28association_football%29) Marvin Sordell,[^4904][^4906] who wrote, "Wish you nothing but good fortune with this next step in life. So many things will be said, but your vulnerability in this situation is such a powerful sign of your strength! I've got huge respect for you doing something that is monumental for our sport".[^4908] Tabloid publications such as *[The Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sun_%28United_Kingdom%29)* alluded that they were aware of the player's identity.[^4906] On 12 July, [Amal Fashanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Fashanu), the niece of Justin Fashanu, said she doubted the authenticity of the account, and said that if the account were a hoax, it would be "detrimental" to the campaign against [homophobia in football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_and_association_football) and "almost \[...\] mocking it in a way."[^4907]

| **[Peter Tatchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Tatchell)** (@PeterTatchell) tweeted: |
|----|

> Gay footballer cancels plan to come out, claiming he isn’t 'strong enough'. This may be true but he must have known his weakness during the months he has been touting his intention to come out. It smells like a con / hoax. What do you think?

23 July 2019[^4915]

Amal Fashanu stated that she was "pretty disheartened" by the account's deletion,[^4904] and became concerned over whether the social environment in football was stopping players from coming out. She also questioned whether Twitter was an appropriate environment in which to come out.[^4916] The director of sport at LGBTQ charity [Stonewall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonewall_%28charity%29), Robbie de Santos, said that "We do not live in a world that is accepting of everyone's sexual orientation or gender identity. Some of the negative tweets directed at 'The Gay Footballer' were a clear reminder of this. We can't rely on the bravery of individuals alone. It's important we understand and respect why not everyone can be out."[^4906] De Santos also critiqued the "media frenzy" over the account as well as the speculation around it, which he called "unhelpful".[^4913] Ryan Atkin said that individuals in football who were or would in the future be looking to come out "will see the support that person has been given", but he also stated his worry that there would be prolonged speculation over whether each of the players under 23 in the Championship were gay.[^4911] Prominent LGBTQ activist Peter Tatchell, in response to the account's final statement that he was not "strong enough", tweeted that the account "may be true but he must have known his weakness during the months he has been touting his intention to come out. It smells like a con/hoax."[^4906][^4912] Phil Francis, a member of the LGBT football team the Bristol City Panthers, said that while he had hoped the account was genuine, if it was fake it would have showed the lengths homophobic supporters would go to "to make it harder for someone to come out in sport".[^4913] Openly gay Australian association footballer [Andy Brennan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Brennan) compared the Gay Footballer account to an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram) post made by Australian cricketer [James Faulkner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Faulkner_%28cricketer%29) in April that year, in which Faulkner had falsely claimed to have a "boyfriend" who was in fact his housemate. Brennan also remarked that, "I personally hope it isn’t a hoax, but even if it is I think you just focus on the positives. The positive energy it created with all the supportive reactions from people was more important than anything negative, and that’s what you have to focus on - otherwise you let the negativity win."[^4917]

##### Copycat accounts

The virality of the initial @FootballerGay account led to copycat accounts being created. This included @thatgaypro, an account which claimed to be manned by a footballer for [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C.). This account was confirmed as "a hoax and a fraud" by Norwich City's sporting director [Stuart Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Webber).[^4918]
