### SpoGomi

**Sport Gomihiroi** (スポゴミ拾い), [lit.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literal_translation) 'sport picking up trash',[^4919] abbreviated to **SpoGomi**, is a sport invented in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan) in which teams collect [garbage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garbage) and [litter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litter) with in a time limit and specified area. Invented in 2008, the first SpoGomi World Cup was held in Japan in November 2023; it was won by [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain).[^4920][^4921] The second SpoGomi World Cup was held in October 2025 and was won by Japan with Germany as runner up.[^4922]

#### Rules

SpoGomi involves teams of three players collecting items of rubbish within a designated playing area. The teams have one hour to pick up any rubbish found in the area, and 20 minutes to correctly sort the rubbish. Teammates cannot be more than 10 metres apart from each other, and are not allowed to run.[^4923] Points are rewarded for both the amount of waste collected by the teams, and what kind of waste is collected. For example, [cigarette butts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigarette) are the highest-scoring items.[^4924]

Teams are not allowed to collect waste that is already in bins or rubblish collection points or belongs to someone else. Teams are also not allowed to collect bulky items that cannot fit into the [trash bags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bin_bag) provided; hazardous waste; or trash picked up by lifting road gutters and dovetails. They are also not allowed to enter rivers, oceans or private property. Teams which break the rules may be cautioned, deducted points or disqualified. Grounds for points deduction include incorrect sorting of items, picking up prohibited items, or failure to return within ten minutes after completing the trash pick-up. Teams may be disqualified if they are over ten minutes late after time has ended, travel by any method other than walking, adding weight to their trash bags with items other than fallen trash, bad sportsmanship, or repeated rule violations.[^4923]

#### Culture

An [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime) film entitled *SpoGomi: World Cup Exhibition Match Arc* has been made to promote the sport. The anime is a [coming-of-age story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming-of-age_story) set in a [near-future world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near_future_in_fiction) where SpoGomi is a sport as popular as [soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football).[^4925]

##### Malaysia

SpoGomi was introduced in Malaysia through local organizers including Kazuki Foo, who helped promote the sport as part of environmental sustainability initiatives.[^4926]

The Malaysia stage of the 2025 event was supported by the Brewspark Technologies Group.[^4927]

### Hamster racing

**Hamster racing** is a sport in which [hamsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamster) are placed in [hamster wheels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamster_wheel) or [hamster balls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamster_ball) - often fitted to miniature racing vehicles - and raced down a straight 9 meter (30 ft) course. The hamster crossing the finish line in the shortest amount of time wins. According to a 2001 media report, the world-record time for this course setup is 38 seconds.[^4928]

Events may feature as few as two hamsters or many teams of hamsters and human [pit crews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit_stop). Hamster balls may be simple spheres or feature many design modifications purported to increase the performance and style of the race vehicle.

#### Professional racing

In 2001, an epidemic of [foot and mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot_and_mouth) disease caused the cancellation of some British [horse races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_racing) and other sporting events. To boost their lagging [bookmaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmaking) incomes, betting agencies introduced and promoted the concept of professional hamster racing. Online bookmaker [Blue Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rank_Group) organized the first hamster racing series, with the rodents racing in hamster [dragsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragster_%28car%29). A series of qualifying rounds were held over a week, with a final race. The event was webcast live on the internet.

While largely confined to the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom), professional hamster racing has since made inroads in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) and [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia).

Race hamsters are almost always divided into at least two race classes, which follow their [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) classifications: [dwarfs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricetulus) and [Syrians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_hamster). They are also often divided into other race classes, such as [novice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novice), patterned and long-hair or short-hair.

Not all hamster racing is done professionally or for betting purposes. [Amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur) hamster races are popular at [church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_body) outings and frequently occur at [hamster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamster_show) and [rodent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodent) shows. Amateur races generally do not conform to the professional 9 meter (30 ft) track distance but may use shorter "[sprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_%28running%29)" tracks designed to make sure all hamsters finish in a reasonable time. Fast hamsters are capable of winning sprint races in just a few [seconds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second).

#### Sponsorship

**Petco**

In early 2007, [Petco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petco) announced the return of biannual hamster races in all of its stores.[^4929] The event is branded the "Petco Hamster Ball Derby" and takes place in late March and early September of each year. The 2006 races featured more than 14,000 amateur race hamsters and their owners in Petco stores across the country.

Petco uses a nonstandard short 8-foot (2.4 m) track and hamsters run in common spherical balls rather than the elaborate "drag racers" that professional race hamsters often use (see [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV) Sponsorship *infra*). Races usually only last a few seconds due to the length of the track. Winners receive various prizes such as gift cards, training equipment and hamster treats.

**MTV**

In May 2006 [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV) began promotion of "HamTrak '06," a world tour of [professional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional) [hamster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamster) racers featuring hamster teams sponsored by *[The Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sun_%28United_Kingdom%29)*, *[XFM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XFM)*, *[Pimp My Ride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pimp_My_Ride)* and others.[^4930]

The first HamTrak race, held on May 19, 2006, at the Hammywood Hills Rodent Raceway, was won by the [New Media Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Media_Age) sponsored "Team Hot Rodent," powered by the eight-month-old female Syrian hamster Michelle Schuhamster. It was her 24th career win.

### Paula Barila Bolopa

**Paula Barila Bolopa** (born 12 October 1979), nicknamed 'The Crawler', is an Equatoguinean former [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footballer) and [swimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimmer). She was one of two Equatorial Guinean swimmers to [compete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equatorial_Guinea_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics) at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics) in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney), the other being [Eric Moussambani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Moussambani).

#### Biography

Originally a footballer who played for women's first division side E Waiso Ipola,[^4931] she was submitted to a swimming trials to participate at the 2000 Olympic Games and was selected after a month and a half of training.[^4932]

Following Moussambani's struggling but courageous performance in the men's 100 metres freestyle event, the media turned their attention to his female compatriot. According to *[The Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph)*, "the spectator gallery was almost full as the news spread that a female Eric was making an appearance."[^4933] A correspondent for *[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times)* reported:

"Paula Barila Bolopa, still dripping wet from her swim, was under siege. Tape recorders were being thrust in her face and an interpreter was translating her comments from Spanish for American television stations. Somebody passed her a mobile phone so she could talk live to a radio presenter in Madrid and when she was asked whether she had signed any autographs since fame embraced her, she furrowed her brow in indignation. "Muchos," she said. She and Celebrity had quickly become fast friends."[^4934]

Barila Bolopa competed in the women's 50 metres freestyle, and finished last in her heat with a time of 01:03.97, which was double the second-worst time,[^4935][^4936] and reportedly the slowest time in Olympic history for that event.[^4937] She received loud support and encouragement from spectators.[^4938][^4939]

Barila Bolopa gained entry to the Olympics without meeting the minimum qualification requirements via a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_%28sports%29) draw designed to encourage participation by [developing countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country) without expensive training facilities. Equatorial Guinea only had two pools, neither of them Olympic-sized, and she had never swum in a 50-metre pool before. After the race, she commented: "It's the first time I've swam \[*sic*\] 50 metres. It was further than I thought. I was very tired."[^4940]

The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) commented: "Bolopa and Moussambani have become two of the stars of the Sydney Olympics much like [Eddie "the Eagle" Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_%22The_Eagle%22_Edwards) became a hero at the [1988 Calgary Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Winter_Olympics) for his brave but laughable attempts at ski-jumping."[^4940] *The Telegraph* likewise commented that Barila had "recapture\[d\] the spirit of Eddie the Eagle".[^4933] The [Agence France-Presse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agence_France-Presse) reported that she had "gained Olympic hero status", and commented: "She brought out the spectators' affection for a courageous, have-a-go hero who dared to compete knowing she would probably be the worst-ever Olympian in that event."[^4939]

Barila worked as a supermarket cashier at the time of the Games.[^4941]

### Dolly Gray impostor

The **Dolly Gray impostor**, also known as **Jack** "**Dolly**" **Gray**, was an unknown [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football) player who played for the [St. Louis All-Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_All-Stars) and [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers) during the [1923 National Football League (NFL) season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1923_NFL_season). The impostor played under an alias, claiming to be an [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-American) from [Princeton University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University) in 1922; the only known player with the surname "Gray" to be awarded consensus All-American honors at Princeton in 1922 was [Howdy Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howdy_Gray), who was also an [end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_%28American_football%29).

The impostor first tricked [Ollie Kraehe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollie_Kraehe), the owner and [player-coach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player-coach) of the All-Stars. However, after a few games of poor play on the field, Kraehe realized his error. Instead of releasing "Gray", he exchanged him for cash with the Packers. "Gray" played only one game for the Packers and then disappeared. A few weeks later, Packers head coach [Curly Lambeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curly_Lambeau) cornered Kraehe after a game against the All-Stars; Kraehe admitted to the deception but said that it was only done as a joke. The impostor's identity remains unknown.

#### Background

[Howard Kramer "Howdy" Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howdy_Gray) played as an [end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_%28gridiron_football%29) for the [1922 Princeton Tigers football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1922_Princeton_Tigers_football_team),[^4942] which had a record of 8-0 and were named National Champions for that year.[^4943] He was the only known player with the surname "Gray" to be awarded consensus [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-American) honors at Princeton in 1922; he was also part of the [1922 College Football All-America Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1922_College_Football_All-America_Team).[^4944] On September 29, 1923, the *[Green Bay Press-Gazette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Press-Gazette)* reported that "Howard 'Dolly' Gray, regular left end on the Princeton varsity team of last season, is the latest addition" to the [St. Louis All-Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_All-Stars), a recently formed [NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League) team owned by [Ollie Kraehe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollie_Kraehe).[^4945][^4942]

#### Professional career

##### St. Louis All-Stars

Sources differ on the number of games played by "Gray" for St. Louis, but what is clear is that he participated in a game against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers) on October 7, 1923.[^4942] The *Press-Gazette* noted that "Gray" was an All-American, started at the end position for St. Louis, and played well.[^4946] A St. Louis newspaper noted that a "Jack Gray" injured his shoulder during the game.[^4947] "Gray" was mentioned in various game summaries in local newspapers for the rest of the month, likely playing in his last game for St. Louis on October 21.[^4942] Kraehe had at least witnessed "Gray's" poor performance and understood that the man playing for him was not likely to have been an All-American college football player. He sold "Gray" to the Packers, knowing that he was deceiving head coach [Curly Lambeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curly_Lambeau) into giving up what appeared to be one of his better players. Kraehe's purpose for selling "Gray" was to recoup funds to help keep his team financially viable.[^4948]

##### Green Bay Packers

With local newspapers playing up "Gray's" performance, it appeared that the Packers had received an All-American football player. Local Wisconsin newspapers noted "Gray's" speed and stated that he was "one of the greatest ends that ever wore the orange and black" (Princeton's colors).[^4942] Gray officially played in one game for the Packers, a 24-3 loss to the [Racine Legion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racine_Legion) on October 28.[^4949][^4950] Gray was noted in pre-game coverage as the newest addition to the Packers' team and in post-game coverage it was mentioned he recovered a [fumble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fumble).[^4951][^4950] A few weeks later, the Packers played the All-Stars again, winning 3-0. After the game, Curly Lambeau cornered Kraehe and questioned him about "Gray". Lambeau stated that "Gray" played poorly and then disappeared after boarding the train for the team's game against St. Louis. Kraehe admitted to the ruse, saying that it was done as a joke and that he had always intended to return the money the Packers spent to purchase "Gray". St. Louis' team was dissolved at the end of the season, while the true identity of the impostor remained unknown.[^4948]

#### Identity

Packers historian [Cliff Christl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Christl) noted in a 2024 article that the true identity of the impostor is unlikely to ever be solved. He noted a few challenges: "[Goodbye, Dolly Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye,_Dolly_Gray)" was a common battle chant during the 1898 [Spanish-American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish-American_War) and the name "Dolly Gray" was extremely common, both for men and women. Additionally, three separate names, all with the surname "Gray", were used by various newspapers to reference an end from Princeton who played in 1922. In addition to the impostor merely fooling everyone, Christl also speculated that the All-Stars may have used the signing as a publicity stunt or that early sportswriters were "guilty of [puffery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puffery)" after assuming that "Gray" was the famous end from Princeton.[^4942]

### José Offerman

**José Antonio Offerman Dono** (born November 8, 1968) is a Dominican professional [baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball) [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manager_%28baseball%29) and former [infielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infielder) who most recently served as the manager for the [Algodoneros de Unión Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algodoneros_de_Uni%C3%B3n_Laguna) of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League). He played professional baseball for nearly 20 years, including 15 seasons in [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball) (MLB) and four seasons of [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_league_baseball) and Mexican League baseball after leaving MLB.

Offerman most recently managed the [Tigres del Licey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigres_del_Licey) of the [Dominican Professional Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Professional_Baseball_League) (LIDOM), leading them to the 2008-2009, 2013-2014 and 2022-2023 LIDOM Championship. During a baseball game on January 16, 2010, Offerman attacked an umpire during an argument and, as a result, was banned from LIDOM for three years.[^4952] He managed the [Rojos del Águila de Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rojos_del_%C3%81guila_de_Veracruz) of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League) in 2014.[^4953]

#### Early career

After attending Colegio Biblico Cristiano High School in [San Pedro de Macorís](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Pedro_de_Macor%C3%ADs), Offerman signed with the [Los Angeles Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers) as an amateur [free agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agent) in 1986. In [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_in_baseball), he completed his first season of professional play being named as Best Prospect in the [Pioneer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_League_%28baseball%29). Progressing rapidly through the minor leagues, he made his major league debut against the [Montreal Expos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal_Expos) on August 19, [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_in_baseball), becoming the 55th player in major league history to hit a [home run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_run) in his first major league [at-bat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-bat).

#### Major leagues

By [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_in_baseball), Offerman became the Dodgers' starting shortstop. On opening day 1993, he was the first batter to ever face the [Florida Marlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Marlins), striking out against [Charlie Hough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Hough). He made his first appearance in the [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game) in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game) but was traded to the [Kansas City Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Royals) after the season, mostly because of his very poor defense. After a year as a utility player, he won the starting [second baseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_baseman) job in 1997. Offerman had his best offensive seasons in Kansas City, culminating in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_in_baseball), when he hit .315 with a league-leading 13 triples and the fifth most stolen bases, 45. After that season, he signed with the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox) as a free agent, making the All-Star Game for the second time in [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game).

Offerman was a more productive hitter than fielder; in 1992, 1993 and 1995, he committed 42, 37 and 35 errors respectively.[^4954] Offerman's offensive production declined beginning in [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_in_baseball). He was sent to the [Seattle Mariners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Mariners) during the [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_in_baseball) season, but was released afterwards. In [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_in_baseball), he joined the [Montreal Expos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal_Expos) in [spring training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_training) but was cut before the regular season began. He spent the entire year with the [Bridgeport Bluefish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport_Bluefish) of the independent [Atlantic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_League_of_Professional_Baseball). In [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_in_baseball), he won a spot on the [Minnesota Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Twins) roster and led the league in pinch-hits with 12 in 29 attempts. He started [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_in_baseball) with the [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies) but was released after a slow start. Later, he signed with the [New York Mets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Mets) and was called back up to the majors in June.

#### Post-USA major leagues

Offerman played in the [2008 Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Caribbean_Series) for the [Tigres del Licey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigres_del_Licey) and assisted the team in winning its tenth Caribbean Series title. During the series he signed a contract with the 2008 [Veracruz Red Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rojos_del_%C3%81guila_de_Veracruz) of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League).

In December 2008, Offerman was named player-manager of Tigres del Licey of the [Dominican Professional Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Professional_Baseball_League) (LIDOM). With Offerman as manager, Licey swept the LIDOM championship, winning five straight against the [Gigantes del Cibao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigantes_del_Cibao). As champions, Licey was then invited to participate in the [2009 Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Caribbean_Series) with Offerman as manager (the series was ultimately won by Venezuela).

On January 7, 2014, Offerman was again named manager of the Tigres del Licey of LIDOM, replacing Mike Guerrero. With Offerman at the helm, Licey won the LIDOM Championship, winning five games to three over the [Leones del Escogido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leones_del_Escogido). As champions again, Licey was invited to the [2014 Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Caribbean_Series) with Offerman as manager.

##### Bat incident

He has not played or managed professional baseball in the United States since 2007. On August 14, 2007, while playing for the [Long Island Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island_Ducks) of the [Atlantic League of Professional Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_League_of_Professional_Baseball), Offerman was thrown out of a game against the [Bridgeport Bluefish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport_Bluefish) for charging Bluefish pitcher [Matt Beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Beech) with a bat after he was hit by a pitch. Beech sustained a broken finger in the resulting melee. Bluefish catcher [John Nathans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Nathans) was also hit in the back of the head during the bench-clearing melee, receiving a severe concussion that effectively ended his playing career.[^4955] Beech and Nathans were taken to Bridgeport Hospital where they were treated and released. After being removed from the game, Offerman was arrested by the [Bridgeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport,_Connecticut) Police.[^4956]

On August 15, 2007, he was suspended indefinitely. The independent Atlantic League announced on August 17, 2007, that Offerman would remain suspended at least until the legal case was resolved.[^4957]

On September 24, 2007, Offerman pleaded not guilty to two second degree assault charges.[^4958]

His case was pending in Bridgeport Superior Court GA#2 in Bridgeport, Connecticut. On October 30, 2007, Offerman was given two years special probation called "Accelerated Rehabilitation." The Court determined that his actions on August 14, 2007, were of an aberrant nature. The Court also found that Offerman is not likely to offend again in the future.[^4959]

Nathans filed a \$4.8 million civil suit against Offerman in February 2009, alleging that he still has [post-concussion syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-concussion_syndrome) and that the injury caused by Offerman ended his baseball career.[^4960][^4961] On July 29, 2014, Nathans won his suit, and Offerman was ordered to pay \$940,000.[^4962]

##### LIDOM incident

On 16 January 2010, Offerman once again engaged in an on-field assault when he struck an umpire while managing a LIDOM game.[^4963] Offerman, manager of the Tigres del Licey, came onto the field during the third inning while losing a 6-0 game to the Gigantes del Cibao, to protest ejection of his catcher for arguing balls and strikes and ended up arguing with first-base umpire [D.J. Reyburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.J._Reyburn). He swung with a right hook at Reyburn, who then fell to the ground. Offerman was detained by stadium security, eventually being transported to the local police station to await the end of the game and Reyburn's decision whether to ask for charges to be pressed against him or not.

A day after the incident, the American crew that umpired the game resigned their positions with LIDOM and left the country, reportedly due to threats and concerns about their own safety. Because of this incident Offerman received a lifetime ban from LIDOM, a suspension that was eventually lifted in February 2013.[^4964] Coincidentally, at the time he was suspended, Offerman was replacing [Dave Jauss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Jauss) as Licey manager after Jauss was suspended himself for two years for bumping an umpire during a playoff game.[^4965]

#### Coaching career

##### Conspiradores de Querétaro

On February 6, 2024, Offerman joined the [Conspiradores de Querétaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiradores_de_Quer%C3%A9taro) of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League) as their manager.[^4966] He was awarded the 2024 [Mexican League Manager of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_League_Manager_of_the_Year_Award).[^4967]

On June 6, 2025, it was announced that Offerman would be leaving the team, and would be replaced by Rafael Rijo.[^4968]

##### Algodoneros de Unión Laguna

On July 21, 2025, Offerman was hired as the manager for the [Algodoneros de Unión Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algodoneros_de_Uni%C3%B3n_Laguna) of the [Mexican League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Baseball_League), replacing [Carmelo Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmelo_Mart%C3%ADnez), who had been serving in the interim.[^4969] On October 7, Offerman was fired by the Algodoneros.[^4970]

#### Personal life

He is the father of former [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE) ring announcer and former reality television star [JoJo Offerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JoJo_Offerman).[^4971]

### Federated States of Micronesia national under-23 football team

The **Federated States of Micronesia national under-23 football team**, nicknamed **the Four Stars**, is the national U-23 [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football) team representing the [Federated States of Micronesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia) and is controlled by the [Federated States of Micronesia Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_Football_Association). The team is managed by Australian coach [Stan Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Foster_%28football_manager%29), with the assistant manager Curtis Graham.

Although the [senior team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_football_team) had been competing on the international stage sporadically for a number of years, the nation lacked any junior teams until the under-23 team was founded in 2014. Having never played together as a full squad until a training camp in Guam, and traveling to the games with kit donated by their hosts, they made their competitive debut in international football at the [2015 Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_Football_at_the_2015_Pacific_Games) with a view to using the tournament as both a development opportunity for young players in the country and also as the first steps towards gaining official recognition from and membership of [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA).[^4972]

Their performance was the worst recorded in international football as they lost all three games, conceding 114 goals (an average of 38 goals each game) in the process without scoring themselves. On two occasions, against Fiji and Vanuatu, they conceded a record number of goals in international competition. However, although these matches count as official records for the [Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Games), they are not recognized by FIFA as official world records, as the games did not involve senior teams. Despite the unofficial nature of their record defeats, numerous international media outlets have branded them the worst football team on the planet.

#### History

##### Background

The four states of the [Federated States of Micronesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia): [Yap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yap_State), [Chuuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuuk_State), [Pohnpei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pohnpei_State) and [Kosrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosrae_State) are spread out over six hundred islands in an isolated area of the Pacific Ocean.[^4973] Many of the islands, although touched by western influences, have had very little contact with modern media, [stone money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rai_stones) is still used symbolically on occasions[^4973] and many of the team selected for the 2015 Pacific Games still live in huts in small villages, lacking hot water and modern conveniences.[^4973] There are only two full-sized football pitches in the country,[^4973] both of which are on Yap, the multi-use Yap Sports Complex and the dedicated football pitch at the Yap State Soccer field.[^4974] In regions such as Chuuk, the lack of facilities means that all football played is street football.[^4973]

##### Foundation

Previously the [senior team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_football_team) had entered the [2003 South Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_football_at_the_2003_South_Pacific_Games), performing poorly, losing all four games and conceding 52 goals without reply.[^4975] This was the last recorded time that any Micronesian team had played against full international sides,[^4976] although individual islands of Micronesia competed in the 2014 Micronesia Games.[^4977] However, before the tournament, [Kiribati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiribati_national_football_team) withdrew, [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam_national_football_team) chose not to send a team and the [Northern Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands_national_football_team) were unable to send a team as their regular squad was playing in the [EAFF East Asian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_EAFF_East_Asian_Cup), leaving [non-FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-FIFA_international_football) member [Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau_national_football_team) as the only international representative and Micronesia competing as separate states.[^4977]

Under the auspices of manager Stan Foster[^4978] and assistant manager Curtis Graham,[^4979] The Federated States of Micronesia under-23 team, nicknamed the Four Stars,[^4980] began training in the second half of 2014 in unusual circumstances.[^4981] Due to the scattered nature of the islands, it was impossible for the team to get together initially to train as a full squad and instead individuals had to train in small groups on their islands of origin.[^4981] Although this method of selection meant the team was not able to get together as a single unit until their pre-tournament camp in Guam, it was a method that met with the approval of the [football association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_Football_Association) President Jim Wuthel as being one that allowed the selection of a squad that was truly representative of the islands despite an almost complete lack of money or sponsorship.[^4981]

The two-week extended pre-tournament camp in [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam), funded by the football association,[^4982] allowed the team to train together for the first time, make use of the significantly better facilities offered by the [Guam Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam_Football_Association) and gave them the chance to test themselves against a number of teams in the [Guam Men's Soccer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam_Men's_Soccer_League) prior to their departure for [Papua New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea).[^4981] The training camp also allowed the team to take possession of an away kit for the first time courtesy of the Guam Football Association[^4983] and were it not for a meeting with a local restaurateur during their training camp, some of the players would have travelled to the games without boots.[^4973]

##### 2015 Pacific Games

The Federated States of Micronesia national under-23 football team had never taken part in a tournament until 2015 when they entered the [Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Pacific_Games),[^4981] competing in the 14th edition of the [men's football tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_Pacific_Games), which was held in [Port Moresby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Moresby), [Papua New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea) between 3 and 17 July 2015. The Micronesian National Olympic Committee stated that the reason they entered the competition was to try to enhance their chances of membership of FIFA,[^4982] although they had tentatively begun their application process back in 2001,[^4984] and the national Olympic committee, via the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee) provided a [\$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Dollar) 50,000 grant to cover airfares, insurance and accommodation costs while in Port Moresby to enable the team to compete.[^4979]

The [Oceania Football Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania_Football_Confederation) (OFC) used this tournament as the [OFC Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OFC_Men's_Olympic_Qualifying_Tournament) for the [2016 Summer Olympic men's tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament).[^4985] A separate qualifying tournament was initially set to take place at [Tonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonga) between 2-12 December 2015[^4986] however, it was later decided to absorb the qualifying tournament into the Pacific Games, leading to the [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_national_under-23_football_team) team participating for the first time in the Pacific Games men's football tournament.[^4987][^4988] As a result of this, the [Federated States of Micronesia Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_Football_Association) sent their under-23 team to make their debut on the international stage. Despite initial claims that the team should not be underestimated and that they were not simply there to make up the numbers,[^4989] their performance was to be the worst on record for international competition.

###### Micronesia 0-30 Tahiti

Their debut at the [2015 Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_Football_at_the_2015_Pacific_Games) was an inauspicious start for the team, losing 0-30 to [Tahiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahiti_national_under-23_football_team), having arrived at the tournament with a squad of only 18 players.[^4978] Michel Maihi opened the scoring in the second minute with a fluke goal which he later admitted was intended to be a cross.[^4990] Maihi went on to score a further four goals in the match, but he was beaten to the title of top scorer by [Fred Tissot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Tissot), who scored six.[^4990] [Manuarii Hauata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuarii_Hauata), Tevairoa Tehuritaua, [Mauarii Tehina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauarii_Tehina), Yohan Tihoni and Raiamanu Tauira scored three or more each to complete the scoring.[^4991] This was the second time that Tahiti had recorded a 30-0 victory in the Pacific Games, matching the scoreline in a game against the [Cook Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_Islands_national_football_team) in 1971.[^4991] As Tahiti's onslaught went on, the crowd began to cheer for the Micronesians and nicknaming their number 10, Roger Nakasone, "[Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi)". Immediately following the match, the Tahitian team performed a post-match [haka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haka) towards their opponents, inflicting on them additional embarrassment.[^4990]

###### Micronesia 0-38 Fiji

Their next match produced an even more one-sided result, indeed to that point the most one-sided result in international football history, as they lost to [Fiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiji_national_under-23_football_team) 0-38,[^4992] with goalkeeper Walter Pengelbew conceding 21 goals in the first half[^4992] before being replaced in goal by erstwhile midfielder Dominic Gadad,[^4993] who himself went on to concede a further 17 goals as Micronesia eclipsed the former world record for number of goals conceded in official competition set by American Samoa when they [conceded 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_31%E2%80%930_American_Samoa) against [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_men's_national_soccer_team) in 2001.[^4994] However, this result did not replace the American Samoa match in the record books firstly as Micronesia are not affiliated to [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA) and secondly as the competition, since it is doubling up as a qualifying tournament for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics), is being contested by under-23 teams.[^4995] However, the scoreline was deemed an official record for the Pacific Games.[^4996] Tony Tuivuna scored ten goals for Fiji, narrowly beating Chris Wasasala, who scored nine goals on his international debut to top scorer.[^4997] Also scoring were Iosefo Verevou and Garish Prasad with five each, Napolioni Qasevakatini with four, Masana Nawakula with two, while Savenaca Nakalevu and Tevita Waranaivalu scored one each.[^4997]

The result of the match was not a surprise to the manager of the team, Stan Foster, who stated that the team were at the tournament for development purposes, to try as hard as they could and to take any information they could glean from their experiences home with them to aid their progression.[^4998] Fiji manager, [Juan Carlos Buzzetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Carlos_Buzzetti) was apologetic after the match, acknowledging the inexperience and youth of the opposition,[^4998] and saying that they had little option but to finish with such a scoreline after Tahiti had set the benchmark in the previous match,[^4997] but was also critical of his own players for not always sticking to their game plan to play one-touch football.[^4998]

The reasons for the size of the defeat have been put down to the general lack of experience within the diminished squad as a whole, with most of the players only getting involved in the game at most eighteen months prior to the tournament starting.[^4993] Indeed, most of the players came from villages where they did not play the game at all and Gadad, who replaced Pengelbew in goal at half time, had only played as a goalkeeper for the first time three weeks prior.[^4993]

###### Vanuatu 46-0 Micronesia

Having suffered one record defeat to Fiji, the fledgling Micronesia team lost even more heavily in their final group game, defeated 46-0 by [Vanuatu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanuatu_national_under-23_football_team), with [Jean Kaltack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Kaltack) scoring a record 16 goals.[^5000] With Micronesia having lost so heavily in their opening games, Vanuatu were faced with the seemingly difficult task of having to score a minimum of thirty goals in order to stand a chance of progressing to the next round of competition.[^5001] However, the team, ranked 200th in the world at the time,[^5001] found themselves 24-0 ahead at half time having scored three more goals by that stage than Fiji had managed in their game.[^5001]

Tony Kaltack opened the scoring in the second minute, but by the end of the game, [Tafea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tafea_FC) striker [Jean Kaltack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Kaltack) was the top scorer in the match with 16 goals.[^5002] Tony Kaltack increased his tally by a further five goals in the match, [Bill Nicholls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nicholls_%28Vanuatuan_footballer%29) and Barry Mansale scored ten and six goals respectively while Dalong Damalip's hat-trick, Abraham Roqara's two and one each for [Brian Kaltack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Kaltack), Nemani Nikiau, Zicka Manuhi and Chris Andrews rounded out the scoring.[^5002]

###### Final standings

The team finished the tournament with three heavy losses and no wins, scoring no goals whilst conceding 114 in total. They finished last in the group and did not progress to either knockout round (although they could not have progressed to the Olympic games qualifying rounds as they are not members of FIFA).

| Pos | Team | Pld | W | D | L | GF | GA | GD | Pts | Qualification |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| 1 |  [Tahiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahiti_national_under-23_football_team) | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 32 | 1 | +31 | 7 | [Pacific Games knockout stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_under-23_football_team) |
| 2 |  [Fiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiji_national_under-23_football_team) | 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 39 | 1 | +38 | 5 | [Olympic Qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_under-23_football_team) and [Pacific Games knockout stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_under-23_football_team) |
| 3 |  [Vanuatu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanuatu_national_under-23_football_team) | 3 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 48 | 3 | +45 | 4 | [Olympic Qualifying knockout stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia_national_under-23_football_team) |
| 4 | Micronesia | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 114 | −114 | 0 |  |

###### Aftermath

Following the game against Vanuatu, Foster expressed relief that the team would be allowed back at the next Pacific Games, fearing they would be refused entry due to the quality of their results, but they received assurances from the organizers that they were aware that the side that competed was a development side and that he hoped, despite receiving criticism before the start of the tournament for selecting a team of such young players, that a number of the players would be able to use the Pacific Games to enhance their development for the next eight years.[^5005] Though he noted that it would be difficult for the nation to improve the standard of their football until they were recognized by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA),[^5005] he said that he anticipated a FIFA delegation would be visiting the islands in the following week to carry out an inspection and with a view to affiliating them with the [AFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Football_Confederation).[^5005] This would then entitle them to funding and technical assistance that would enable the nation to improve the standard of football.[^5005] National media reported that membership would allow the nation to build new stadium and renovate existing facilities, bring professional coaches to the islands and purchase much-needed equipment.[^4979]

To put into context the series of defeats his team had suffered, Foster said that for many of his players this was the first time that they had played a game on a full-size 11-a-side pitch.[^5006] He also said that in general the players were simply overawed with the occasion, noting that many of them had never even left their villages, let alone their respective islands and that during the pre-tournament training camp in Guam a number of the players gained their first experience of an escalator or elevator.[^5006] Following these defeats, several members of the squad said to the manager that they wanted to train as goalkeepers.[^5007] Despite conceding a record number of goals, and with media outlets labelling them the worst team in the world,[^4973] many of the outfield players were heartened by the cheers their goalkeeper received every time he made a save.[^5007] The major stumbling block facing Micronesia is, if they do not gain FIFA affiliation, then their next scheduled international match will not be for another four years, when they will travel to [Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samoa) for the [2019 Pacific Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pacific_Games).[^5007] Micronesia subsequently did not receive FIFA affiliation, nor did a football team from the nation contest the 2019 Pacific Games.

Despite the heavy defeats suffered by the team, national media was upbeat about the overall performances, remarking that despite the results, none of the athletes ever gave up, that they won the respect of the opposition in all three games they played and that the team as a whole could be very proud of their efforts.[^4979] It was noted that if, as a result of competing the nation could join FIFA that the benefits of membership would outweigh the losses in the tournament.[^4979] International media however was less complimentary, with numerous outlets focussing solely on the results and labelling the side the worst football team on earth.[^5008][^5009] Despite this, the players received a warm reception upon their return home. On Yap people were pleased simply because the players had had the chance to travel abroad and experience international competition, with such opportunities normally being limited to Guam if at all.[^5010] Indeed, as a result of their experiences, one player was looking to join a football club in Guam, with several others considering similar options.[^5010]

##### FIFA affiliation

The [Oceania Football Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania_Football_Confederation) had dissuaded Micronesia from applying to their association, saying that they would have better developmental opportunities within the [AFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Football_Confederation),[^4983] although with FIFA having more Pacific members than the United Nations, affiliation with FIFA is also not assured; they have cancelled previous visits and rejected membership of other nations in the past due to the level of hotel facilities on offer.[^4983] A FIFA delegate visited the islands following the tournament to review the condition of facilities in the country and the level of football development, with a decision on potential FIFA affiliation due before the end of 2015.[^5011] Foster remarked that the initial report provided by the delegate was positive.[^5010]

#### Stadium

The team has yet to play any home fixtures. There are only two full-sized football pitches in the country,[^4973] both of which are on Yap, the multi-use Yap Sports Complex and the dedicated football pitch at the Yap State Soccer field.[^4974]

### Vatican Taekwondo

**Vatican Taekwondo** is the official governing body for the sport of [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo) in the [Vatican City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City). The body is a part of [Vatican Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Athletics), and is the second Vatican sports governing body to gain membership of a world governing body after becoming a member of [World Taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo) in November 2021; it is also a member of the [European Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Taekwondo_Union). The president of the organisation is Giampaolo Mattei.

#### History

##### Prior to recognition

Before the creation of Vatican Taekwondo, the Vatican and [World Taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Taekwondo) held a close relationship with each other.[^5016] The latter's demonstration team first visited the nation in 2016 during the first Global Conference on Faith & Sport for an [exhibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhibition_game) [poomsae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poomsae) performance.[^5017] The team made a subsequent appearance in 2018 with five [South Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea) and [North Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea) taekwondo practitioners for a "demonstration for peace".[^5018]

In 2017, then-World Taekwondo president [Choue Chung-won](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choue_Chung-won), accompanied by president of the [Italian Taekwondo Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Taekwondo_Federation) (FITA) Angelo Cito, met with [Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis). There, Choue had gifted an honorary 10th [dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_%28rank%29) black belt to the Pope.[^5019][^5020] Pope Francis also stated his interest in humanitarian activities through the sport, citing the Taekwondo Humanitarian Foundation which teaches taekwondo to refugees. In the Vatican, taekwondo courses were held for twenty students at the Saint Pius X Institute through a partnership with FITA in 2020.[^5021]

##### Creation and recognition

Vatican Taekwondo was established in 2021 as part of [Vatican Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Athletics).[^5022][^5023] The body was voted the 211th member of World Taekwondo on 23 November 2021 at the World Taekwondo General Assembly, becoming the second sports organisation in the nation recognized by a world governing body, after [Vatican Cycling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Cycling).[^5023] It is also a member of the [European Taekwondo Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Taekwondo_Union).[^5022]

##### Competition

In 2026, [Diego Di Mattia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Di_Mattia) became Vatican Taekwondo's first registered athlete. He competed in the under-30 male individual event at the [2026 World Poomsae Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Poomsae_Championships), becoming the first Vatican athlete to appear at a taekwondo world championship.[^5024][^5025] He was defeated in the preliminary round.[^5026]

#### Management and status

Giampaolo Mattei has been the president of Vatican Taekwondo since it began,[^5021] and the secretary is Marco Alpigiani.[^5022]

### Rocket Racing League

The **Rocket Racing League** which existed from 2005 through 2014, was an organization created to race [rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket)-powered [aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft) around a closed-circuit air racetrack.

Founded in 2005, the league made its first public flights in 2010 and was working to begin regular racing seasons. The "Rocket Racers" were slated to compete in the air and on a virtual racetrack easily viewed by a live audience as well as projected on large screen and handheld electronic displays.

Three prototype [canard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canard_%28aeronautics%29)-style *Rocket Racer* aircraft were built between 2006 and 2010. The league had planned to hold its inaugural race season in 2008 with four races, but encountered financial difficulties that delayed fielding of *Rocket Racers* by the six teams that had been previously announced. With the addition of venture capital funding in mid-2009, technology development continued. One exhibition occurred in 2010, with another round of plans for an inaugural season of races in 2011. The 2011 races were never scheduled and the league was defunct by 2014.[^5027]

#### Background

Projected to be an hour and one half in length, the races were intended to be between Rocket Racer planes that used [liquid oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_oxygen) and either [kerosene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerosene) or [ethanol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol) fuel[^5028] with a burn time of four minutes. The rocketplanes were expected to cost less than US\$1 million each. The planes were based on the fixed-gear [Velocity SE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_SE) modified by [XCOR Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XCOR_Aerospace) and the retractible gear [Velocity XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_XL) modified by [Armadillo Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo_Aerospace) for the purpose of rocket racing. The Velocity airframe was derived from a commercially available kit plane that traced its design heritage to the [Rutan Long-EZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutan_Long-EZ), which had been modified to accept rocket power and custom avionics. In order to provide the airframes, RRL purchased the aircraft's manufacturer, [Velocity Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_Aircraft), in April 2008.[^5029]

The RRL had been called "[NASCAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR) with rockets", XCOR Aerospace flew the Rocket Racer for a public audience at the 2008 [EAA AirVenture Airshow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EAA_AirVenture_Oshkosh) at Oshkosh, Wisconsin.[^5030][^5031] If league competition were to begin, Whitelaw indicated tournament semifinals would be held each September in Nevada, with finals each October in New Mexico at the [X Prize Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Prize_Cup) competing for a \$2 million championship purse.

Races were to have taken place on a [race course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Course_%28navigation%29) two miles (3 km) long, one mile (1.6 km) wide, and 1,500 feet (460 m) in the air. A typical race would take about one hour, and fans would be able to see multiple camera views, including cockpit, "on-track," "side-by-side" and wing-angle views.

Additionally, a computer game had been planned which was to have interfaced with racer positional data in real time over the internet, allowing players to virtually compete with the rocket pilots.

##### The Track

The proposed "track" for a typical Rocket Race was to have begun with a staggered start. Pilots were to take off in pairs a few minutes apart, they would be competing against the clock but would maneuver around each other much like NASCAR. The pilots would be guided by a virtual three-dimensional "track" projected in their [head-up display](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head-up_display). Each racer was to have a separate track to follow but the courses were planned to be close together to build excitement.

##### Teams

As of 2008, there were six teams registered to compete in the inaugural 2008 race season, Rocket Star Racing, Team Extreme Rocket Racing, Canada-based Beyond Gravity Rocket Racing, Bridenstine Rocket Racing, Santa Fe Racing and Thunderhawk Rocket Racing.[^5031]

As of 2012, RRL claimed that "official team recruitment will commence as the production-level Rocket Racers near completion", listing five "candidate teams of the RRL franchise": Bridenstine Rocket Racing, Santa Fe Racing, Rocket Star Racing, Team Extreme Rocket Racing, and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)-based Beyond Gravity Rocket Racing.[^5032]

#### History

The formation of the league was announced by Granger Whitelaw, and [Peter Diamandis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Diamandis), founder of the [Ansari X-Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansari_X-Prize), in October 2005[^5033] in partnership with the [Reno Air Races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno_Air_Races). According to Diamandis, the purpose of the league was to "inspire people of all ages to once again look up into the sky and find inspiration and excitement."

Initial plans called for a four-team league finals in 2006, to be followed by 10 teams competing in 2007, with video games based on the competition also out in 2007.[^5033] In 2006, analysts identified doubts about the economics of the venture, and especially of the ability of RRL to attract a large fanbase similar to [IndyCar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndyCar_Series) and [NASCAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR).[^5034] In the event, no races occurred in either 2006 or 2007.

In April 2008, the league stated that it was "ready for competition \[announcing\] four exhibition races will be held later \[in the\] year, one in Las Cruces."[^5035]

On April 14, 2008, the Racing Rocket Racing Composite Corporation, a subsidiary of the Rocket Racing League, acquired Velocity Aircraft. The RRL announced their goal was to "produce an airframe that will be consistent for all competing Rocket Racers."[^5036]

On May 26, 2010, a Velocity employee posted to the builder's email-list a note from Scott and Duane Swing that stated that they had bought back full ownership of Velocity Inc from Rocket Racing League. The RRL now owns no share of Velocity Inc.[^5037]

##### League financial difficulties

None of the four planned 2008 races were actually run. The Rocket Racing League had difficulty in attracting and retaining sufficient financial backing, from both investors and sponsors, in order to get an initial racing season firmly scheduled in 2008, 2009, or 2010. Some progress with the rocket and aircraft technology continued however, but by 2014, the league had gone defunct.[^5027]

The league twice failed to complete construction of six hangars contracted to be built on land adjacent to [Spaceport America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaceport_America) near [Las Cruces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces,_New_Mexico), [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico). As of January 2009, the league was at risk of having their leases with the City of Las Cruces terminated.[^5038]

In July 2009, the league announced the closing of a [venture capital financing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital_financing) round of US\$5.5 million. The funds were to be used for ongoing operations and for the development of a next-generation Rocket Racer.[^5039]

As of February 2010, [Peter Diamandis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Diamandis) suggested that 2010 could be the year that we see "more than one racer in the air and possibly in exhibition races." Non-exhibition "live" races were to occur as early as 2011.[^5040] Also in February, the [Tulsa Air and Space Museum and Planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Air_and_Space_Museum) (TASM) announced that it would partner with the Rocket Racing League to host an exhibition flight of a Rocket Racer at the QuikTrip Air and Rocket Show at [Tulsa International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_International_Airport) in April 2010.[^5041]

The Rocket Racing League announced a "2010 World Exhibition Tour" on April 24, 2010, when they unveiled their *[Mark-III X-racer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark-III_X-racer)* rocket plane at the QuikTrip Air & Rocket Racing Show in [Tulsa, Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa,_Oklahoma). The RRL exhibition flights at Tulsa were the first simultaneous flights of two rocket-powered airplanes in the history of peacetime aviation. RRL duplicated this historic feat later that day. The league's intent in such exhibitions was to "build up the league's fan base, in addition to perfecting operations and technologies, before the league's official launch in 2012."[^5042] The April event in Tulsa was the only RRL exhibition of 2010.

The league's financial difficulties continued in 2011 and no races were organized.[^5043]

By 2014, persons formerly involved with the league had made public statements that the league had failed and was now defunct.[^5027]

#### Rocket Racers

The Rocket Racing League had been developing prototype *Rocket Racers* since 2006, working with one airframe manufacturer and two rocket engine producers on three prototype aircraft to date. All three of the airframes have been of the [canard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canard_%28aeronautics%29) configuration to more easily accommodate the [rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipropellant_rocket) [propulsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_propulsion) technology.

A fifth model was proposed, but not built, in 2011: the Mark-V X-Racer.[^5043]

##### Predecessor aircraft

[XCOR Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XCOR_Aerospace) developed the [XCOR EZ-Rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XCOR_EZ-Rocket), later flown under Rocket Racing League sponsorship as an X-Racer prototype rocketplane. First flight was July 21, 2001 at Mojave Airport in [Mojave, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojave,_California).[^5044] This XCOR technology demonstrator was a converted [Rutan Long-EZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutan_Long-EZ) and, in its final version, utilized two 400 lbf (1.8 kN) thrust XCOR Aerospace [isopropyl-alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isopropyl_alcohol)-powered [rocket engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_engine)[^5034] of engine type XR-4A3.[^5045] XCOR flew the EZ-Rocket for several years in development and demonstration flights, including, in collaboration with the RRL, at the 2005 [X-Prize Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Prize_Cup) in New Mexico.[^5034]

By 2006, the design-point for the RRL racer had become a single rocket engine utilizing [kerosene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RP-1) as the rocket fuel, carrying 1,000 lb (450 kg) of [liquid oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_oxygen) in its flight oxidizer tank.[^5034]

The first RRL prototype built, known as the Mark-I X-Racer, was built on a [Velocity SE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_SE) airframe and was also powered by XCOR Aerospace rocket technology, a regeneratively-cooled and [pump-fed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pump-fed_engine) XR-4K14 rocket engine.[^5045] This rocket-powered aircraft flew several demonstration flights at the 2008 [EAA AirVenture Oshkosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EAA_AirVenture_Oshkosh) [air show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_show).[^5046] The total thrust for the single-engine Mark-I X-Racer was 1,500 lbf (6,700 N),[^5034] approximately twice that of the EZ-Rocket.

##### Mark-II and Mark-III X-Racers

As of 2010, the Rocket Racing League was utilizing a highly modified [Velocity XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_XL) fixed-gear airframe and an [Armadillo Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo_Aerospace) 2,500 pound thrust [liquid oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_oxygen) (LOX) and [ethanol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol) [rocket engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_engine) in both its Mark-II X-Racer and Mark-III X-Racer demonstration vehicles.[^5047] The Mark-II and Mark-III racers could take off just 4 seconds after the rocket engine was ignited; both vehicles were limited to a top speed of 300 mph (480 km/h).[^5048] The rocket engine was a LOX-Ethanol, [film-cooled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_engine), [pressure-fed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure-fed_cycle_%28rocket%29), blow-down[^5049] design with a 10 to 15-foot (4.6 m)-long [exhaust plume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plume_%28hydrodynamics%29). Plume-seeding technology allowed the plume color to vary from red to green to yellow to better facilitate race spectators in keeping track of specific racers while in the air.[^5048]

The Mark-II (N205MB) racer utilized a standard fixed-gear XL airframe, modified for the addition of the Armadillo rocket propulsion. The Mark-III (N133XP) airframe was modified during manufacturing at [Velocity Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_Aircraft) explicitly for use as a Rocket Racer, with canopy top, center seat and control stick, and other enhancements.[^5047]

##### Mark V X-Racer

The Mark-V proposed design resembles "a sleek, rocket-powered sailplane" and may be built at [Velocity Aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity_Aircraft), although no firm contracts are in place to do so as of November 2011.[^5043]
