### List of animals awarded human credentials

This **list of animals awarded human credentials** includes nonhuman animals who have been submitted as applicants to suspected [diploma mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma_mill), and have been awarded a diploma. On occasion, they have been admitted and granted a degree, as reported in reliable sources. Animals are often used as a device to clearly demonstrate the lax standards or fraudulent activities of the awarding institutions. In at least one case, a cat's degree helped lead to a successful fraud prosecution against the institution that had issued it.

On occasion, accredited institutions award mock degrees to animals for humorous purposes, e.g. [UNSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNSW) awarded a "dogtorate" (not *doctorate*) to a dog;[^6235] such cases are not included below.

#### Cats

##### Colby Nolan (MBA)

Colby Nolan was a [house cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat) who was awarded an [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration) in 2004 by Trinity Southern University, a [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas)-based [diploma mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma_mill), sparking a [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud) [lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawsuit) by the [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania) attorney general's office.[^6236]

Colby Nolan lived with a deputy attorney general. In looking to [expose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sting_operation) Trinity Southern University for fraud, undercover agents had the then-six-year-old feline obtain a bachelor's degree in business administration for \$299. On the animal's application, the agents claimed that the cat had previously taken courses at a [community college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_college), worked at a fast-food restaurant, babysat, and maintained a newspaper route. In response, the institution informed Colby that, due to the job experience listed on his application, he was eligible for an executive MBA which he could obtain for an additional \$100. The [transcript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcript_%28education%29) submitted by the agents claimed that Colby had a [GPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_point_average) of 3.5.

Upon learning that the cat received the degree, Pennsylvania attorney general [Jerry Pappert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Pappert) filed a lawsuit against Trinity Southern University.[^6237] In the lawsuit, Pappert directed the diploma mill, which had used [email spam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Email_spam) to sell degrees, to provide restitution to anyone who had ordered a degree from them.

In December 2004, the Texas attorney general obtained a temporary [restraining order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restraining_order) under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act against Trinity Southern and its owners, Craig B. and Alton S. Poe. The court also ordered the school's assets frozen.[^6238] In March 2005, the Poes were assessed penalties of over \$100,000 by the court and were ordered not to market or promote fraudulent, substandard degree programs or to represent their university as being [accredited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_accreditation) or affiliated with legitimate universities.[^6239][^6240] It was reported that the Poes were also associated with Wesleyan International University and Prixo Southern University.[^6240] Trinity Southern University's website has been offline since 2005.[^6241]

##### George (registration for practice as a hypnotherapist)

In 2009, George, a cat owned by Chris Jackson (presenter of the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) show *[Inside Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Out_%282002_TV_programme%29) North East & Cumbria*), was registered as a [hypnotherapist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypnotherapist) after his owner created a fake certificate from a non-existing institution and used it to register with three professional organizations: the British Board of [Neuro Linguistic Programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuro-linguistic_programming), the United Fellowship of Hypnotherapists, and the Professional Hypnotherapy Practitioner Association.[^6242]

##### Henrietta (Hettie, certified member of the American Association of Nutritional Consultants)

In 2007, the cat Henrietta, despite having been dead for around a year, was successfully registered as a certified member of the [American Association of Nutritional Consultants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Nutritional_Consultants) by her owner [Ben Goldacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Goldacre), doctor and author of the [Bad Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Science_%28Goldacre_book%29) column in the *Guardian* newspaper and subsequent book. Goldacre registered Henrietta with AANC to showcase the complete lack of any verification for membership, beyond payment of \$60, after TV nutritionist [Gillian McKeith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillian_McKeith) promoted her AANC membership among other unverified qualifications.[^6243]

##### Kitty O'Malley (high school diploma)

In 1973, the [Lakeland, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakeland,_Florida) newspaper *[The Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ledger)* obtained a high school diploma from "Washington High Academy" for Kitty O'Malley, a cat also known as Spanky. While the diploma was deemed insufficient to gain Kitty admission to local colleges, the state attorney general's office planned to investigate the institution.[^6244]

##### Oliver Greenhalgh (fellowship of estate valuation professional society)

On December 10, 1967, *[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times)* reported that Oliver Greenhalgh had been accepted as a [fellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow) of the English Association of Estate Agents and Valuers, after a payment of eleven [guineas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_%28coin%29) (his two references were not verified). Oliver was a cat belonging to Michael Greenhalgh, a cameraman with [Television Wales and the West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Wales_and_the_West), who was pursuing an investigation of bogus professional associations.[^6245][^6246]

##### Oreo Collins (high school diploma)

Oreo C. Collins (born around 2007) is a [tuxedo cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuxedo_cat) who gained notoriety when she received a diploma from Jefferson High School Online in 2009, although her age was misrepresented in order to qualify.[^6247] The sting was an investigative operation by the [Better Business Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Business_Bureau) of Central Georgia headed by Kelvin Collins, Oreo's owner.[^6248]

##### Zoe D. Katze (psychotherapist and hypnotherapy certifications)

Zoe D. Katze ("Zoe the Cat" in German) was a house cat owned by psychologist Steve K. D. Eichel. Around 2001, Eichel obtained a psychotherapy certification for his cat from the American Psychotherapy Association and several hypnotherapy credentials from other organizations.[^6249][^6242] The certification of Zoe has been cited in several books and articles on credentialing scams, and has appeared in psychology and [forensic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic_science) curricula. Eichel also served as the consultant to the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) investigation that led to the certification of [George the cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_animals_awarded_human_credentials) by several UK hypnosis associations.[^6242]

#### Dogs

##### Chester Ludlow (MBA)

In 2009, Chester Ludlow, a pug from Vermont, was awarded an MBA by [Rochville University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochville_University). His owner submitted an application and US\$499 and received a "diploma, two sets of transcripts, a certificate of distinction in finance, and a certificate of membership in the student council".[^6250]

##### Lulu (college diploma)

In 2010, Mark Howard, a member of the legal team for the claimants ([BSkyB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BSkyB)) in *BSkyB Ltd & Anor v HP Enterprise Services UK Ltd & Anor* \[2010\][^6251] obtained a degree for his dog Lulu from Concordia College in the [US Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Virgin_Islands). Lulu "graduated" with higher marks than the defendant's key witness, who, the judge found, had lied that he had attended classes for his Concordia MBA.[^6252][^6253] In the legal community, the story of the witness' MBA is described as "infamous",[^6254] and a supervisory management cautionary tale.[^6255]

##### Maxwell Sniffingwell (theriogenology/animal reproduction degree)

In 2009, Dr. Ben Mays, a veterinarian in [Clinton, Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton,_Arkansas), obtained a degree in "theriogenology/animal reproduction" from [Belford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belford_University) on behalf of an English bulldog named Maxwell Sniffingwell. The application included his work as a reproductive specialist, noting his "natural ability in [theriogenology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theriogenology)" and "experimental work with felines" and his understanding of the merits of specialization despite a desire to "'do them all'". He obtained a diploma, transcript and letter of recommendation upon receipt of a payment of \$549 to the university, but declined an offer to be made an honors graduate for an additional \$75.[^6256]

##### Molly (high school diploma)

In February 2012, in a story on local diploma mills by [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston) television station [KHOU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KHOU), the reporters got a high school diploma and official transcript from Lincoln Academy for their photographer's [basset hound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basset_Hound) Molly for \$300 after filling out a "laughable", "easy take-home test".[^6257] According to a [homeschooling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeschooling_in_the_United_States) advocate, Lincoln Academy and other schools were improperly taking advantage of a Texas law that prohibits discrimination by public colleges and universities against homeschooled students.[^6257]

##### Ollie (associate editorship of medical journals)

In 2017, Professor Mike Daube, a public health expert in Western Australia, reinvented his dog Ollie as Dr. Olivia Doll. He made up credentials including "past associate of the [Shenton Park Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenton_Park,_Western_Australia) for Canine Refuge Studies" (where she was a rescue dog) and submitted her application for posts on the editorial boards of some [predatory medical journals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predatory_open_access_publishing). Several accepted her application, and the Global Journal of Addiction and Rehabilitation Medicine named her associate editor.[^6258]

##### Pete (MBA)

The [American University of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University_of_London) offered Pete, a four-year-old male short-haired [Lurcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lurcher)[^6259] in [Battersea Dogs and Cats Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battersea_Dogs_and_Cats_Home), London, an [MBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration) for £4,500 without requiring any course work. The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC) current affairs programme *[Newsnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsnight)* reported in 2013 that the dog, named "Peter Smith" on the faked CV for a management consultant, was offered an MBA by the university's Accreditation of Previous Experiential Learning board based on his "made-up work experience and a fictitious undergraduate degree" just four days after applying for the course.[^6260]

##### Phoebe (professional certifications)

Between 2024 and 2026, a nine-year-old pug from Alberta, Canada, named Phoebe obtained more than 250 online professional and workplace certifications as part of a demonstration conducted by the Calgary-based firm Cognisense.[^6261][^6262] Her certifications included workplace safety credentials, transportation of dangerous goods, defensive driving, boating, food handling, and Alberta’s ProServe Liquor Staff Training certificate.[^6263][^6264] Media reports stated that several of the online courses required only basic registration and lacked identity verification or participation monitoring.[^6265]

##### Sonny (medical degree)

The May 30, 2007 episode of the [Australian Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Broadcasting_Corporation) comedy show *[The Chaser's War on Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chaser's_War_on_Everything)* documented host [Chas Licciardello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chas_Licciardello) applying online and obtaining a medical degree for his dog Sonny from the diploma mill [Ashwood University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashwood_University). Sonny's "work experience" included "significant [proctology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proctology) experience sniffing other dogs' bums".[^6266][^6267] Ashwood University has since been listed as a Non Accredited Degree Supplier in the states of Michigan, Oregon, and Texas.[^6268]

##### Wally (associate's degrees)

In 2004, the [Albany, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_New_York) television station [WRGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRGB) ran a report in which reporter Peter Brancato applied to and received an associate degree from [Almeda University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almeda_University) on behalf of his dog, Wally.[^6269][^6270] On the application, Brancato listed, "Plays with the kids every day ... teaches them to interact better with each other ... Teaches them responsibilities like feeding the dog." Almeda University granted Wally a "life experience" associate degree in "Childhood Development". After the report aired, Almeda University protested that Brancato [perjured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury) himself by creating a false identity using a fabricated name and date of birth. In a public statement, an Almeda University representative wrote, "He completed an application that included a background of the following: Eight-years tutoring pre-K children, curriculum design and development, teaching coping skills, and volunteer coaching".[^6271] In March 2008, Wally was featured in a [Lake Geneva, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Geneva,_Wisconsin) mayoral campaign political cartoon, with a dialogue bubble reading, "I graduated with Bill Chesen", referring to candidate Chesen's Almeda University bachelor's degree.[^6272]

In 2021, environmentalist [George Monbiot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Monbiot) registered his childhood goldfish as a registered waste disposer in the UK.[^6273][^6274]

### List of English-language expressions related to death

This is a list of words and phrases related to [death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death) in alphabetical order. While some of them are [slang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slang), others euphemize the unpleasantness of the subject, or are used in formal contexts. Some of the phrases may carry the meaning of 'kill', or simply contain words related to death. Most of them are [idioms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idioms).

| Expression | Definition | Context | Notes |
|----|----|----|----|
| At peace[^6275] | Dead | [Euphemistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphemism) |  |
| At rest[^6275] | Dead | [Polite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politeness) |  |
| Augered in | Died via aircraft crash | [Slang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slang) | As documented in *[The Right Stuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Right_Stuff_%28book%29)* by [Tom Wolfe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Wolfe) |
| Belly up[^6275] | Dead | Informal | The orientation of fish when dead |
| Beyond the grave[^6275] | After death | Neutral | In reference to communication with the dead |
| Beyond the veil[^6276] | The mysterious place after death | Neutral | Originally used to refer to the ['veil'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veil_of_the_Temple) that hides the innermost [sanctuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanctuary) of the [Temple in Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_in_Jerusalem). Sometimes refers to just a mysterious place. |
| [Big sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Big_Sleep)[^6276] | To die or be killed | Euphemistic | Could be in reference to Raymond Chandler's 'The Big Sleep' |
| Bite the dust[^6276] | To die or be killed | Informal | Also means 'failed' |

### List of games with concealed rules

**Games with concealed rules** are [games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game) where the [rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game) are intentionally concealed from new players, either because their discovery is part of the game itself, or because the game is a hoax and the rules do not exist. In fiction, the counterpart of the first category are games that supposedly do have a rule set, but that rule set is not disclosed.

#### Actual games

##### Discovery games

- [Eleusis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleusis_%28card_game%29): A card game in which one player secretly decides on a rule which determines which cards may be played on top of each other. The other players then use deductive logic to work out the secret rule.
- [Game Changer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Changer_%28game_show%29): A game show in which the rules and objectives change from episode to episode.
- [Haggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haggle_%28game%29): A party game in which the [gamemaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamemaster) divides a set of cards and a subset of the full rules among players and allows them to trade for other cards and rules.
- [Mao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_%28card_game%29): A [shedding-type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shedding-type_game) card game where the winner of a round adds a concealed rule of their choice to all subsequent rounds.
- [Paranoia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paranoia_%28role-playing_game%29): A [tabletop role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabletop_role-playing_game) in which the rules are considered "classified". Only the gamemaster has full knowledge of the rules, while other players must deduce them by trial and error as they proceed through the game. (The game acknowledges that players may read the gamemaster section, but *demonstrating* knowledge of the rules is considered treasonous, and the gamemaster may also make arbitrary changes.)
- [Penultima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penultima): A chess variant in which the spectators make secret rules governing how the pieces move and capture. The two players are unaware of the rules and must discover them by inductive reasoning.[^6297]
- [Psychiatrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatrist_%28game%29): In variants of this game, players who do not know the concealed rules ask the other players personal questions and try to infer the rules from the answers and from the fact that players who know the concealed rules occasionally shout "Psychiatrist!" and switch seats.
- [Scissors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scissors_%28game%29): A party game in which a pair of scissors is passed between players, with the passer declaring that they are being passed "open" or "closed" based on an individual and secret rule. The other players must use observation to deduce the rule each player uses to make the declaration.[^6298][^6299]
- Whose Triangle Is It?: A party game in which one player points to three people or objects, forming an imaginary triangle, and then asks "Whose triangle is it?" The triangle belongs to the first person to speak after the triangle is drawn, but this rule is not told to new players, and the game is for new players to figure out what the rule is.[^6300][^6301]
- [Zendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zendo_%28game%29): A game in which one player creates a rule for structures to follow and the other players try to discover the rule by building structures

##### Hoax or joke games

- [52 Pickup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52_Pickup): A card game in which dealer scatters the cards on the floor and non-dealer must pick them up.
- [Mornington Crescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mornington_Crescent_%28game%29): Originally a round in the [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4) comedy panel game *[I'm Sorry I Haven't A Clue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Sorry_I_Haven't_A_Clue)*.[^6302] The game consists of each panelist in turn announcing a landmark or street, most often a tube station on the London Underground system. The apparent aim is to be the first to announce "Mornington Crescent", a station on the Northern Line. Despite appearances, however, there are no rules to the game, and both the naming of stations and the specification of "rules" are based on stream-of-consciousness association and improvisation.

#### Games in works of fiction

##### Games with undisclosed rules

- [43-Man Squamish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/43-Man_Squamish): [*Mad* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_%28magazine%29) published an article outlining a college sport designed to be unplayable. The sport features a pentagonal field, silly-sounding terms and a dummy on each team.
- [Calvinball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvinball): In the comic strip *[Calvin & Hobbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_&_Hobbes)*, *Calvinball* is a game regularly played by the main characters. The only consistent rule of *Calvinball* is that "Calvinball may never be played with the same rules twice".
- [Double Fanucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Fanucci): Featured in the computer game *[Zork Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zork_Zero)*, Double Fanucci has mind-bogglingly complex "rules". Legal play can depend on things like the phase of the Moon and the ancestry of the players.

##### Hoax games

- [Numberwang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That_Mitchell_and_Webb_Look): A recurring "game show" on the sketch series *[That Mitchell and Webb Look](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That_Mitchell_and_Webb_Look)*.[^6303] Similar to *Mornington Crescent* above, the "contestants" call out random numbers in an attempt to score a "Numberwang", though the responses are scripted and there are no actual rules to winning a "Numberwang".
- [Fizzbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fizzbin): In the *Star Trek* episode "A Piece of the Action", [James T. Kirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_T._Kirk) created this game while he and [Commander Spock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spock) were being held prisoner. They "taught" the game to the guards, improvising the rules until their captors were sufficiently distracted, then overpowered them and escaped.
- Cups: In the *[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends)* episode "[The One on the Last Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends_%28season_6%29)", Chandler invents the card game Cups, making up the result of each card turn in an attempt to give Joey money after he refuses a handout.

### List of major-party United States presidential candidates who lost their home state

Below is a **list of major party United States presidential candidates who lost their birth or resident states**. While many successful candidates have won the presidency without winning their birth state, only four ([James K. Polk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk), [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson), [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon), and [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)) have won an election despite losing their state of residence. Nixon, a lifelong Californian, had taken residence in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_%28state%29) after his [failed run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_California_gubernatorial_election) for [governor of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_California), but later switched back during his presidency and ahead of his reelection.

##### Lost the home states of their running mates

- In [1796](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1796_United_States_presidential_election), [John Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Adams) lost [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina), the home state of his running mate [Thomas Pinckney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Pinckney). [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson) lost [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_%28state%29), the home state of his running mate [Aaron Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Burr) as well as Burr's birth state of [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey).
- In [1800](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1800_United_States_presidential_election), [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson) lost [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey), the birth state of his running mate [Aaron Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Burr). [John Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Adams) lost [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina), the home state of his running mate [Charles Cotesworth Pinckney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Cotesworth_Pinckney).
- In [1804](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1804_United_States_presidential_election), [Charles Cotesworth Pinckney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Cotesworth_Pinckney) lost [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_%28state%29), the home state of his running mate [Rufus King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_King), as well as King's birth state of [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts).

### List of people who have been considered deities

This is a list of notable people who were considered [deities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity) by themselves or others.

#### Imperial cults and cults of personality

| Who | When | Notability |
|----|----|----|
| [Pharaohs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharaoh) | 3150-30 BCE | Egyptian pharaohs were the kings of [Ancient Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt), and were considered to have divine properties. Their titles equated associated them with aspects of deities, such as the king of the gods [Amun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amun) and the hawk god [Horus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horus). It was standard for Egyptians to [worship deceased](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veneration_of_the_dead) pharaohs as deities in the form of [mortuary cults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortuary_cult). However, with some [rare exceptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_pharaohs_deified_during_lifetime). See [List of pharaohs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_pharaohs).[^6304][^6305] |
| [Naram-Sin of Akkad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naram-Sin_of_Akkad) | 2255-2119 BCE | The first Mesopotamian emperor who claimed to be a god. |
| [Japanese emperors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_of_Japan) | ??? - 1945[^6306] | Claimed, at least by [some Shintoists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinto), including government officials, to be divine descendants of the goddess [Amaterasu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amaterasu). The [Shōwa Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hirohito) repudiated the "false conception" of his divinity in the [Humanity Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanity_Declaration) in 1945.[^6307] |
| [Chinese emperors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_of_China) | 221 BCE - 1911 CE | Deified as "[Sons of Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_of_Heaven)", at least by [some Confucianists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confucianism), since the [Qin dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin_dynasty) under [Qin Shi Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qin_Shi_Huang).[^6308] |
| [Alexander the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great) | 356-323 BC | To legitimize taking power (in Egypt) and be recognized as the descendant of the long line of pharaohs, Alexander made sacrifices to the gods at Memphis and went to consult the famous oracle of Amun-Ra at the Siwa Oasis in the Libyan desert, at which he was pronounced the son of the deity Amun. Henceforth, Alexander often referred to Zeus-Ammon as his true father; after his death, currency depicted him adorned with horns, using the Horns of Ammon as a symbol of his divinity. The Greeks interpreted this message, one that the gods addressed to all pharaohs, as a prophecy. Some believe he implied he was a [demigod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demigod) by actively using the title "Son of [Ammon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amun)-[Zeus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeus)". The title was bestowed upon him by Egyptian priests of the god [Ammon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amun) at the [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle) of the god at the [Siwah oasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siwa_Oasis) in the [Libyan Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libyan_Desert).[^6309] |
| [Natchez rulers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natchez_people) | 700-1730 CE | The Natchez were a theocracy ruled by "The Great Sun." This ruler has sometimes been deemed a God-king.[^6310] |
| [Purnawarman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purnawarman) | 395-434 CE | The king of [Sundanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_people) [Indianised kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianised_kingdom) called [Tarumanagara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarumanagara). According to these inscriptions he embarked on hydraulic project[^6311] and also identified himself with [Vishnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu), which indicates he and his kingdom were adhering to the [Vishnuite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnuite) faith. |
| The [Sailendras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sailendra) | 7th-11th centuries CE | The [Sailendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sailendra) dynasty of [Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java) were active promoters of Mahayana Buddhism and covered the plains of [Central Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Java) with Buddhist monuments, including the world-famous [Borobudur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borobudur).[^6312] |
| [Majapahit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majapahit) kings | 1293-1597 | [Javanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javanese_people) rulers of South East Asia's largest ever kingdom, in [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia). After death, they were depicted as Hindu gods (see for instance [Raden Wijaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raden_Wijaya)). |
| [Dalai Lamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalai_Lama) | 1391-present | Considered re-incarnations of [Avalokiteśvara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avalokite%C5%9Bvara) in [Tibetan Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_Buddhism). [Panchen Lamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchen_Lama) are incarnations of [Amitābha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amit%C4%81bha).[^6313][^6314][^6315] |
| [Inca emperors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapa_Inca) | 1438-1533 | The Inca Emperors had a status very similar to that of the Pharaohs of Egypt. |
| [Nepalese kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Nepal) | 1768-2008 | In [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Nepal), the kings of the [Shah dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_dynasty) were considered incarnations of [Vishnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu).[^6316] |

#### Posthumous deification

| Who | When | Notability |
|----|----|----|
| [Gilgamesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilgamesh) | Sometime between 2800 and 2500 BCE[^6317] | Most historians generally agree that Gilgamesh was a historical king of the Sumerian city-state of [Uruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruk),[^6318][^6317] who probably ruled sometime during the early part of the [Early Dynastic Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Dynastic_Period_%28Mesopotamia%29) (c. 2900-2350 BCE).[^6318][^6317] It is certain that, during the later Early Dynastic Period, Gilgamesh was worshipped as a god at various locations across Sumer.[^6318] In the twenty-first century BCE, [Utu-hengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utu-hengal), the king of Uruk adopted Gilgamesh as his patron deity.[^6318] The kings of the Third Dynasty of Ur were especially fond of Gilgamesh, calling him their "divine brother" and "friend".[^6318] During this period, a large number of myths and legends developed surrounding him.[^6318] Probably during the [Middle Babylonian Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kassites) (c. 1600 BCE - c. 1155 BCE), a scribe named [Sîn-lēqi-unninni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%AEn-l%C4%93qi-unninni) composed the *[Epic of Gilgamesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_of_Gilgamesh)*, an [epic poem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_poem) written in [Akkadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkadian_language) narrating Gilgamesh's heroic exploits.[^6318] The opening of the poem describes Gilgamesh as "one-third human, two-thirds divine".[^6318] |
| [Imhotep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imhotep) | c.2625 BCE | [Ancient Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt) architect and physician whose status, two thousand years after his death, was raised to that of a god, becoming the god of medicine and healing. In Memphis and on the sacred Island of Philae existed temples dedicated to him. The Greeks identified Imhotep with their own divine healer and physician, Asclepios (who also healed people in their dreams).[^6319] |
| [Heqaib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heqaib) | c.2250 BCE | A [nomarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomarch) of the [first nome of Upper Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta-Seti) during the reign of [Pepi II Neferkare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepi_II_Neferkare), who led several successful military expeditions in [Nubia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nubia).[^6320] |

| [Amenhotep, son of Hapu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amenhotep,_son_of_Hapu) | c.1356 BCE | An Egyptian [architect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Egyptian_architects), [priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clergy_of_ancient_Egypt), [herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reporter_%28Ancient_Egypt%29), [scribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ancient_Egyptian_scribes), and public official under the reign of [Amenhotep III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amenhotep_III).[^6322] |
| [Queen Dido of Carthage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dido_%28Queen_of_Carthage%29) | 814 BCE | Founder and first queen of [Carthage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carthage), after her death, she was deified by her people with the name of [Tanit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanit) and assimilated to the Great Goddess [Astarte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astarte) (Roman [Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_%28mythology%29)).[^6323] The cult of [Tanit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanit) survived Carthage's destruction by the Romans; it was introduced to Rome itself by Emperor Septimius Severus, himself born in North Africa. | [Romulus and Remus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romulus_and_Remus) | 771-717 BCE | Founders of [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome), sons of [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_%28mythology%29), [Romulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romulus) served as first king. Romulus was, according to the book [History of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ab_Urbe_Condita_Libri) (written between 27 and 9 BCE by the historian [Titus Livius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livy)), the son of [Rhea Silvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_Silvia), a [Vestal Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestal_Virgin) who became pregnant with the twins Romulus and Remus by the god [Mars.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_%28mythology%29)[^6324] After his death, Romulus was deified as the god [Quirinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quirinus), the divine persona of the Roman people. Romulus' ascension to heaven and deification as god Quirinus is mentioned in [Ovid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovid)’s poem *[Metamorphoses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphoses)*, Book 14 (written shortly before 8 AD). Ovid depicts god [Jupiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupiter_%28mythology%29) promising Mars the right to translate his son Romulus to immortality.[^6325] He is now regarded as a mythological figure, and his name a [back-formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back-formation) from the name Rome, which may ultimately derive from a word for "river". Some scholars, notably [Andrea Carandini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Carandini), believe in the historicity of Romulus, in part because of the 1988 discovery of the [Murus Romuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murus_Romuli) on the north slope of the Palatine Hill in Rome.[^6326] |

| [Hephaestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hephaestion) | 356-324 BCE | Deified by [Alexander the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great). |

| [Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Philip,_Duke_of_Edinburgh) | 1950s~1960s-present | Considered a god in the village of [Yaohnanen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaohnanen), a [cargo cult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cargo_cult) in [Vanuatu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanuatu).[^6363] See [Prince Philip movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Philip_movement). |
| [Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur) | later 20th century | Honored for his role in the [Battle of Inchon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Inchon), a few followers of [Korean shamanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_shamanism) venerated him as a deity around his statue at [Jayu Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayu_Park).[^6364] |
| Rabbi [Menachem Mendel Schneerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_Mendel_Schneerson) | 1990s-present | While considered the messiah by most of his followers following his death in 1994, one group has deified him.[^6365] |
| [Raj Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Patel) | 2010-present | In January 2010 some adherents of [Share International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_International), following an announcement by [Benjamin Creme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Creme), concluded that [Patel could be the Maitreya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_International).[^6366] Patel has denied being the [Maitreya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maitreya).[^6366] |

#### Self-deification

| Who | When | Notability |
|----|----|----|
| [Naram-Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naram-Sin_of_Akkad) | 2255-2119 BCE | The first Mesopotamian king to claim divinity.[^6367] He marked himself with the [dingir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingir) symbol, a determinative for a divinity. After him, his son [Shar-Kali-Sharri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shar-Kali-Sharri) and then later Mesopotamian Kings would carry the tradition onwards. These kings included [Shulgi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shulgi), [Amar-Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar-Sin), [Shu-Sîn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shu-S%C3%AEn), and [Ibbi-Sîn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibbi-S%C3%AEn) of the [Third Dynasty of Ur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Dynasty_of_Ur); [Shu-Ilishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shu-Ilishu), [Iddin-Dagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iddin-Dagan), [Ishme-Dagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishme-Dagan), [Lipit-Ishtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipit-Ishtar), [Ur-Ninurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ur-Ninurta), [Būr-Sîn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C5%ABr-S%C3%AEn), [Lipit-Enlil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipit-Enlil), [Erra-imitti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erra-imitti), [Enlil-bani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlil-bani), [Zambiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambiya), [Iter-pûsha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iter-p%C3%BBsha), [Ur-dukuga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ur-dukuga), [Sîn-magir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%AEn-magir), [Damiq-ilishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damiq-ilishu) of the [Isin dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isin_dynasty); and [Rim-Sîn I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rim-S%C3%AEn_I) and [Rim-Sîn II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rim-S%C3%AEn_II) of the [Larsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larsa) dynasty.[^6368] |
| [Shulgi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shulgi) | 2037-2028 BCE | Brought back self-deification during the Ur III Period.[^6368] |

| [Shu-Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shu-Sin) | 2037-2028 BCE | Built Temples for himself.[^6368] |
| [Empedocles of Acragas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empedocles) | c. 490 - c. 430 BCE | Empedocles of Acragas was a [Pre-Socratic philosopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-Socratic_philosophy) from the island of [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily), who, in one of his surviving poems, declares himself to have become a "[divine being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daemon_%28classical_mythology%29)... no longer mortal",[^6369] followed by descriptions of him performing activities normally reserved for the gods.[^6369] The later historian [Diogenes Laërtius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diogenes_La%C3%ABrtius) claimed that Empedocles committed [suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide) by jumping into [Mount Etna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Etna) in order to persuade people that he was an immortal god,[^6370] a legend which is also alluded to by the Roman poet [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace).[^6371] |
| [Pharnavaz I of Iberia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharnavaz_I_of_Iberia) | 326-234 BCE | [Iberian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Iberia_%28antiquity%29) king (r. 299-234 BCE) |
| [Antiochus IV Epiphanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiochus_IV_Epiphanes) | 215-164 BCE | [Seleucid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seleucid_Empire) ruler (r. 175-164); the only Seleucid king to claim divine honors, calling himself Theos Epiphaneus "God Manifest" and Nikephoros "Bringer of Victory." Nearly conquered [Ptolemaic Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ptolemaic_Kingdom), the primary rival of the Seleucids among the [Diadochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diadochi) states. Famously attempted to impose [ancient Greek religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek_religion) on the [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews) by persecution, leading to the [Maccabean Revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabean_Revolt); remembered as a major persecutor in Jewish tradition.[^6357] |
| [Antiochus I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiochus_I_of_Commagene) | c. 86 BCE-38 BCE | King of [Commagene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commagene) who instituted a cult for himself and several syncretistic Graeco-Persian deities at [Mount Nemrud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Nemrud) and elsewhere.[^6372] |
| [Simon Magus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Magus) | 1st-4th century | Considered a god in [Simonianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simonians). According to [Irenaeus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irenaeus), he "was glorified by many as if he were a god; and he taught that it was himself who appeared among the Jews as the Son, but descended in Samaria as the Father while he came to other nations in the character of the Holy Spirit. He represented himself, in a word, as being the loftiest of all powers, that is, the Being who is the Father over all, and he allowed himself to be called by whatsoever title men were pleased to address him."[^6373] |
| [Veleda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veleda) | 1st century | Germanic prophetess considered a deity during her lifetime. |

Poems attributed to him, preserved in the oldest surviving Yazidi manuscripts (13th century), express a pantheistic self-identification as God, including the line "In the secret of my knowledge there is no God but me." [Yazidis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis) venerate him as one of the three principal manifestations of God alongside [Sultan Ezid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Ezid) and [Tawûsî Melek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taw%C3%BBs%C3%AE_Melek).[^6374][^6375] |

| [Danila Filippovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khlysts) | 1700 | He believed that he was God and started the [Khlysts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khlysts). (There are various transliterations of his name including Danila Filipov, Danila Filipich, and Daniil Filippovich.)[^6378] |

Led the [Taiping Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiping_Rebellion), conquering a large part of China before defeat and suicide. |

He often donned sunglasses in order to hide his eyes and talked with the strong nasal tone associated with the *lwa*. The regime's propaganda stated that "Papa Doc was one with the *lwa*, [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus) and [God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God) himself".[^6397] The most celebrated image from the time shows a standing Jesus Christ with a hand on the shoulder of a seated Papa Doc, captioned, "I have chosen him".[^6398] Duvalier declared himself an "immaterial being" as well as "the Haitian flag" soon after his first election.[^6399] In 1964, he published a catechism in which the [Lord's Prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Prayer) was reworded to pay tribute to Duvalier instead of God.[^6399][^6400] |

#### Controversial deification

| Who | When | Notability |
|----|----|----|
| [Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus) | [Early Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity)-present | There is debate whether Jesus claimed to be divine, or whether divinity was attributed to him progressively by his followers.[^6412][^6413] According to [Bart D. Ehrman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_D._Ehrman) Jesus did not make public claims of divinity.[^6414] In the first three centuries of the Christian movement, Jesus' identity and relation to God were often subjects of debate and controversy, and the belief among Christians that Jesus was not divine was common.[^6415] Even early Christians who believed that Jesus was God often meant different things by it.[^6416] During [one such controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arian_controversy), the [First Council of Nicaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Council_of_Nicaea) of 325 AD crystallized the notion in the [Nicene Creed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicene_Creed) that Jesus was God Incarnate,[^6417] and he is now considered divine in most [Christian views of Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_in_Christianity). |
