| *[Gloria Patri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Patri)* | Glory to the Father | The beginning of the Lesser [Doxology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doxology). |
| *gloriosus et liber* | glorious and free | [Motto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_mottos) of [Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba) |
| *gradatim ferociter* | by degrees, ferociously | Motto of private spaceflight company [Blue Origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Origin), which officially treats "Step by step, ferociously" as the English translation |
| *gradibus ascendimus* | ascending by degrees | Motto of [Grey College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_College,_Durham), [Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durham,_England) |
| *Graecia capta ferum victorem cepit* | Conquered Greece in turn defeated its savage conqueror | [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace) [*Epistles*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistles_%28Horace%29) 2.1 |
| *Graecum est; non legitur* | It is Greek (and therefore) it cannot be read. | Most commonly from [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare)'s *[Julius Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar_%28play%29)* where Casca couldn't explain to Cassius what Cicero was saying because he was speaking Greek. The more common colloquialism would be: It's all [Greek to me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_to_me). |
| *grandescunt aucta labore* | By hard work, all things increase and grow | Motto of [McGill University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGill_University) |
| *gratia et scientia* | grace and learning | Motto of [Arundel School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arundel_School) |
| *gratiae veritas naturae* | Truth through mercy and nature | Motto of [Uppsala University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uppsala_University) |
| *graviora manent* | heavier things remain | [Virgil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil) *[Aeneid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneid)* 6:84; more severe things await, the worst is yet to come |
| *Gravis Dulcis Immutabilis* | serious sweet immutable | Title of a poem by [James Elroy Flecker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Elroy_Flecker)[^7630] |
| *gutta cavat lapidem \[non vi sed saepe cadendo\]* | a water drop hollows a stone \[not by force, but by falling often\] | main phrase is from [Ovid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovid), *[Epistulae ex Ponto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistulae_ex_Ponto)* IV, 10, 5.;[^7631] expanded in the Middle Ages |

#### H

| Latin | Translation | Notes |
|----|----|----|
| *[habeas corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habeas_corpus)* | \[we command\] that you have the body \[brought up\] | A legal term from the 14th century or earlier. Refers to a number of legal writs requiring a jailer to bring a prisoner in person (hence *corpus*) before a court or judge, most commonly *habeas corpus ad subjiciendum* ("that you have the body \[brought up\] for the purpose of subjecting \[the case to examination\]"). Commonly used as the general term for a prisoner's legal right to challenge the legality of their detention. |
| *[habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus_papam)* | we have a pope | Used after a [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church) [papal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_election) to announce publicly a successful ballot to elect a new pope. |
| *[habent sua fata libelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habent_sua_fata_libelli)* | Books have their destiny \[according to the capabilities of the reader\] | [Terentianus Maurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terentianus), *De litteris, de syllabis, de metris*, **1**:1286. |
| *hac lege* | with this law |  |
| *haec olim meminisse iuvabit* | one day, this will be pleasing to remember | Commonly rendered in English as "One day, we'll look back on this and smile". From [Virgil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil)'s *[Aeneid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneid)* 1.203. Also, motto of Handsworth Grammar School, and the [Jefferson Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Literary_and_Debating_Society). |
| *[haec ornamenta mea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haec_ornamenta_mea) \[sunt\]* | "These are my ornaments" or "These are my jewels" | Attributed to [Cornelia Africana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelia_Africana) (talking about her children) by [Valerius Maximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valerius_Maximus) in *Factorum ac dictorum memorabilium libri IX*, IV, 4, *[incipit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incipit)*.[^7632][^7633] |
| *Hannibal ad portas* | [Hannibal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal) at the gates | Found in Cicero's first *Philippic* and in Livy's *Ab urbe condita* Hannibal was a fierce enemy of Rome who almost brought them to defeat. Sometimes rendered "Hannibal *ante* portas", with similar meaning: "Hannibal *before* the gates" |
| *haud ignota loquor* | I speak not of unknown things | Thus, "I say no things that are unknown". From [Virgil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil)'s *[Aeneid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneid)*, 2.91. |
| *Hei mihi! quod nullis amor est medicabilis herbis.* | Oh me! love can not be cured by herbs | From [Ovid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovid)'s *[Metamorphoses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphoses)*, I, 523. |
| *hic abundant leones* | here lions abound | Written on uncharted territories of old maps; see also: [here be dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here_be_dragons). |
| *hic et nunc* | here and now | The imperative motto for the satisfaction of desire. "I need it, Here and Now" |
| *hic et ubique* | here and everywhere |  |
| *hic jacet* (HJ) | here lies | Also rendered *hic iacet*. Written on [gravestones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headstone) or tombs, preceding the name of the deceased. Equivalent to *hic sepultus* (here is buried), and sometimes combined into *hic jacet sepultus* (HJS), "here lies buried". |
| *hic locus est ubi mors gaudet succurrere vitae* | This is the place where death delights in helping life | A motto of many morgues or wards of anatomical pathology. |
| *hic manebimus optime* | here we will remain most excellently | According to [Titus Livius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livy) the phrase was pronounced by [Marcus Furius Camillus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Furius_Camillus), addressing the [senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Senate) who intended to abandon the city, invaded by [Gauls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaul), circa 390 BC. It is used today to express the intent to keep one's position, even if the circumstances appear adverse. |
| *hic mortui vivunt et muti loquuntur* | here the dead live and the mute speak | inscription on several libraries |
| *[hic Rhodus, hic salta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hic_Rhodus,_hic_salta)* | Here is [Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes), jump here | From the Latin version of "The Boastful Athlete" in [Aesop's Fables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aesop's_Fables)[^7634] as formulated by [Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus) in his *[Adagia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adagia)*. An athlete brags about his impressive jump at a past event in Rhodes, whereupon he is challenged to reproduce it then and there, not merely boast. In other words, prove what you can do, here and now. Cited by [Hegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Wilhelm_Friedrich_Hegel) and [Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Marx). |
| *[hic sunt dracones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hic_sunt_dracones)* | here there are dragons | Written on a globe engraved on two conjoined halves of ostrich eggs, dated to 1504. |
| *[hic sunt leones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hic_sunt_leones)* | here there are lions | Written on uncharted territories of old maps. |
| *hinc et inde* | from both sides |  |
| *[hinc illae lacrimae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinc_illae_lacrimae)* | hence those tears | From [Terence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence), *[Andria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andria_%28comedy%29)*, act 1, line 126.[^7635] Originally literal, referring to the tears shed by Pamphilus at the funeral of Chrysis, it came to be used proverbially in the works of later authors, such as [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace) (*[Epistulae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistles_%28Horace%29)* 1.XIX:41).[^7636] |
| *hinc itur ad astra* | from here the way leads to the stars | Written on the wall of the old astronomical observatory of [Vilnius University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilnius_University), Lithuania, and the university's motto. |
| *hinc robur et securitas* | herefore strength and safety | Motto of the Central Bank of Sweden. |
| *[historia vitae magistra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historia_vitae_magistra)* | history, the teacher of life | From [Cicero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero)'s *[De Oratore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Oratore)*, [II, 9](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/la:De%20oratore/Liber%20II). Also "history is the mistress of life". |
| *hoc age* | do this | Motto of [Bradford Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradford_Grammar_School) |
| *hoc est bellum* | This is war |  |
| *hoc est Christum cognoscere, beneficia eius cognoscere* | To know Christ is to know his benefits | Famous dictum by the Reformer Melanchthon in his *Loci Communes* of 1521 |
| *hoc est enim corpus meum* | For this is my Body | The words of Jesus reiterated in Latin during the Roman Catholic Eucharist. Sometimes simply written as *Hoc est corpus meum* or "This is my body". |
| *hoc genus omne* | All that crowd/people | From [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace)'s [*Satires*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satires_%28Horace%29), **1**/2:2. Refers to the crowd at Tigellio's funeral (c. 40-39 BC). Not to be confused with [et hoc genus omne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Et_hoc_genus_omne) (English: and all that sort of thing). |
| *hodie mihi, cras tibi* | Today for me, tomorrow for you | Inscription that can be seen on tombstones dating from the Middle Ages, meant to outline the ephemerality of life. |
| *hominem pagina nostra sapit* | It is of man that my page smells | From [Martial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial)'s *Epigrams*, [Book 10, No. 4](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/la:Epigrammaton%20liber%20X#IV), Line 10; stating his purpose in writing. |
| *hominem non morbum cura* | Treat the man, not the disease | Motto of the Far Eastern University - Institute of Nursing |
| *homo bulla* | man is a bubble | [Varro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Terentius_Varro) (116 BC - 27 BC), in the opening line of the first book of *Rerum Rusticarum Libri Tres*, wrote *quod, ut dicitur, si est homo bulla, eo magis senex* (for if, as they say, man is a bubble, all the more so is an old man)[^7637] later reintroduced by [Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus) in his *[Adagia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adagia)*, a collection of sayings published in 1572. |
| *[homo homini lupus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_homini_lupus)* | man \[is a\] wolf to man | First attested in [Plautus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plautus)' *[Asinaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asinaria)* (*lupus est homo homini*). The sentence was drawn on by [Thomas Hobbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hobbes) in *[De Cive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Cive)* as a concise expression of his views on human nature. |
| *Homo minister et interpres naturae* | Man, the servant and interpreter of nature | Motto of the [Lehigh University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_University) |
| *homo praesumitur bonus donec probetur malus* | One is innocent until proven guilty | See also: [presumption of innocence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presumption_of_innocence). |
| *homo sine pecunia imago mortis[^7638]* | a man without money is the image of death |  |
| *[Homo sum, humani nihil a me alienum puto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_sum,_humani_nihil_a_me_alienum_puto)* | I am a human being; I think that nothing human is strange to me | From [Terence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence)'s [*Heauton Timorumenos* (*The Self-Tormentor*)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heauton_Timorumenos) (163 BC). Originally "strange" or "foreign" (*alienum*) was used in the sense of "irrelevant", as this line was a response to the speaker being told to mind his own business, but it is now commonly used to advocate respecting different cultures and being humane in general. |
| *[homo unius libri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_unius_libri)* | a man of a single book | Attributed to [Thomas Aquinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Aquinas): «Hominem unius libri timeo» “I fear a man of a single book.” |
| *honestas ante honores* | honesty before glory | Motto of [King George V School, Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_George_V_School,_Hong_Kong) |
| *honor et virtus post morte floret* | honesty and virtue flourish after death | inscribed in the stonework in [Paolo Veronese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Veronese)'s (1565 c.) Painting *[Allegory of Virtue and Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allegory_of_Virtue_and_Vice_%28Veronese%29)* |
| *honor virtutis praemium* | esteem is the reward of virtue | Motto of Arnold School, Blackpool, England |
| *honoris causa* | for the sake of honor | Said of an [honorary title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_honors), such as "Doctor of Science *honoris causa*" |
| *hora fugit* | the hour flees | See [tempus fugit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempus_fugit) |
| *hora somni* (h.s.) | at the hour of sleep | [Medical shorthand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_prescription) for "at bedtime" |
| *horas non numero nisi serenas* | I do not count the hours unless they are sunny | A common inscription on [sundials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundial). |
| *horresco referens* | I shudder as I tell | From [Virgil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil)'s *[Aeneid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneid)*, 2.204, on the appearance of the sea-serpents who kill the Trojan priest [Laocoön](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laoco%C3%B6n) and his sons |
| *horribile dictu* | horrible to say | cf. *[mirabile dictu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirabile_dictu)* |
| *[horror vacui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_vacui_%28disambiguation%29)* | fear of the empty | [phenomenon in art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_vacui_%28art%29) and [hypothesis in philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_vacui_%28philosophy%29) |
| *hortus in urbe* | A garden in the city | Motto of the [Chicago Park District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Park_District), a playful allusion to the city's motto, *[urbs in horto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbs_in_horto)*, [q.v.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q.v.) |
| *hortus siccus* | A dry garden | A collection of dry, preserved plants |
| *[hostis humani generis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hostis_humani_generis)* | enemy of the human race | [Cicero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero) defined [pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracy) in [Roman law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_law) as being enemies of humanity in general. |
| *humilitas occidit superbiam* | humility conquers pride |  |
| *[hypotheses non fingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypotheses_non_fingo)* | I do not fabricate hypotheses | From [Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton), *[Principia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophi%C3%A6_Naturalis_Principia_Mathematica)*. Less literally, "I do not assert that any hypotheses are true". |

#### I

The [classical Latin alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_alphabet) did not have the letter "J". Although many Latin words starting with the letter "I" are now often spelled with "J", this list mainly uses the spelling with "I".

| Latin | Translation | Notes |
|----|----|----|
| *I, Vitelli, dei Romani sono belli* | Go, O Vitellius, at the war sound of the Roman god | Perfectly correct Latin sentence usually reported as funny by modern Italians because the same exact words, in Italian, mean "Romans' calves are beautiful", which has a ridiculously different meaning. |
| *[ibidem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibid.)* (*ibid.*) | in the same place | Usually used in [bibliographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibliography) citations to refer to the last source previously referenced. |
| *id est* (*i.e.*) | that is (literally "it is") | "That is (to say)" in the sense of "that means" and "which means", or "in other words", "namely", or sometimes "in this case", depending on the context. |
| *id quod plerumque accidit* | that which generally happens | Phrase used in legal language to indicate the most probable outcome from an act, fact, event or cause |
| *[idem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idem)* (*id.*) | the same | Used to refer to something that has already been cited; ditto. See also *ibidem*. |
| *idem quod* (*i.q.*) | the same as | Not to be confused with an [intelligence quotient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_quotient). |
| *Idus Martiae* | the [Ides of March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ides_of_March) | In the [Roman calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_calendar), the Ides of March refers to the 15th day of March. In modern times, the term is best known as the date on which [Julius Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar) was assassinated in 44 BC; the term has come to be used as a metaphor for impending doom. |
| *Jesu juva* (*J.J.*) | Jesus, help! | Used by [Johann Sebastian Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach) at the beginning of his compositions, which he ended with "S.D.G." ([Soli Deo gloria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soli_Deo_gloria)). Compare [Besiyata Dishmaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Besiyata_Dishmaya). |
| *Iesus Nazarenus Rex Iudaeorum* (*[INRI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRI)*) | [Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus) the [Nazarene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazarene_%28title%29), [King of the Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus,_King_of_the_Jews) | From [Vulgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulgate); [John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_John) [19:19](https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John+19:19&version=vulgate). [John 19:20](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible%20%28American%20Standard%29/John#19:20) states that this inscription was written in three languages, Aramaic, Latin and Greek, at the top of the [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_Cross) during the [crucifixion of Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucifixion_of_Jesus). |
| [*igitur qui desiderat pacem, praeparet bellum*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Si_vis_pacem,_para_bellum) | Therefore whoever desires peace, let him prepare for war | [Publius Flavius Vegetius Renatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publius_Flavius_Vegetius_Renatus), *[De re militari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_re_militari)*; similar to *[si vis pacem, para bellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Si_vis_pacem,_para_bellum)* and [*in pace ut sapiens aptarit idonea bello*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Latin_phrases_%28full%29). |
| *igne natura renovatur integra* | through fire, nature is reborn whole | An [alchemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alchemy) aphorism invented as an alternate meaning for the acronym [INRI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRI). |
| *igni ferroque* | with fire and iron | Phrase describing [scorched earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorched_earth) tactics. Also rendered as *igne atque ferro*, *ferro ignique*, and other variations. |
| *ignis aurum probat* | fire tests gold | Phrase referring to the refining of character through difficult circumstances |
| *ignis fatuus* | foolish fire | [Will-o'-the-wisp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will-o'-the-wisp). |
| *[ignorantia juris non excusat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignorantia_juris_non_excusat)* (or *ignorantia legis non excusat* or *ignorantia legis neminem excusat*) | ignorance of the law is no excuse | Legal principle whereby ignorance of a law does not allow one to escape liability |
| *[ignoratio elenchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignoratio_elenchi)* | ignorance of the issue | The [logical fallacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_fallacy) of irrelevant conclusion: making an argument that, while possibly valid, doesn't prove or support the proposition it claims to. An *ignoratio elenchi* that is an intentional attempt to mislead or confuse the opposing party is known as a *[red herring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignoratio_elenchi)*. *Elenchi* is from the Greek *[elenchos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elenchos)*. |
| *[ignotum per ignotius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignotum_per_ignotius)* | unknown by means of the more unknown | An explanation that is less clear than the thing to be explained. Synonymous with *obscurum per obscurius*. |
| *ignotus* (*ign.*) | unknown |  |
| *illum oportet crescere me autem minui* | He must become greater; I must become less | In the [Gospel of John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_John) [3:30](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible%20%28King%20James%29/John#3:30), a phrase said by [John the Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_the_Baptist) after baptizing [Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus). Motto of [Saint John the Baptist Catholic School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_John_the_Baptist_Catholic_School), [San Juan, Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Metro_Manila). |
| *[imago Dei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imago_Dei)* | image of God | From the religious concept that man was created in "God's image". |
| *[imitatio dei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imitatio_dei)* | imitation of a god | A principle, held by several religions, that believers should strive to resemble their god(s). |
| *imperium in imperio* | an order within an order | Group of people who owe utmost fealty to their leader(s), subordinating the interests of the larger group to the authority of the internal group's leader(s). A "[fifth column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_column)" organization operating against the organization within which they seemingly reside. "[State within a state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_within_a_state)" |
| *imperium sine fine* | an empire without an end | In [Virgil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil)'s *[Aeneid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneid)*, [Jupiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupiter_%28mythology%29) ordered [Aeneas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeneas) to found a city ([Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome)) from which would come an everlasting, never-ending empire, the endless (*sine fine*) empire. |
| *impossibilium nulla obligatio est* | there is no obligation to do the impossible | [Publius Juventius Celsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publius_Juventius_Celsus), *Digesta* L 17, 185. |
| *[imprimatur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprimatur)* | let it be printed | An authorization to publish, granted by some censoring authority (originally a [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church) bishop). |
| *[in absentia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_absentia_%28disambiguation%29)* | in the absence | Used in a number of situations, such as in a trial carried out in the absence of the accused. |
| *in absentia lucis, tenebrae vincunt* | in the absence of light, darkness prevails |  |
| *in actu* | in act | In the very act; in reality. |
| \[*Dominica*\] *in albis* \[*depositis*\] | \[Sunday in Setting Aside the\] White Garments | Latin name of the [Octave of Easter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octave_of_Easter). |
| *in articulo mortis* | at the point of death |  |
| *in bono veritas* | truth is in the good |  |
| *[in camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_camera)* | in the chamber | In secret. See also *camera obscura*. |
| *in casu* (*i.c.*) | in the event | In this case. |
| *in cauda venenum* | the poison is in the tail | Using the [metaphor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphor) of a [scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion), this can be said of an account that proceeds gently, but turns vicious towards the end, or more generally waits till the end to reveal an intention or statement that is undesirable in the listener's ears. |
| *in com. Ebor.* | In the county of Yorkshire | Abbreviation of *in comitatu Eboraci*. Eboracum was the Roman name for York and this phrase is used in some Georgian and Victorian books on the genealogy of prominent Yorkshire families. |
| *in Christi lumine pro mundi vita* | in the light of Christ for the life on the world | Motto of the [Pontifical Catholic University of Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Catholic_University_of_Chile). |
| *[incurvatus in se](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incurvatus_in_se)* | turned/curved inward on oneself |  |
| *in defensum castitatis* | in defence of chastity | Used in reference to the deaths of some [Christian martyrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_martyrs) in Catholicism |
| *in Deo speramus* | in God we hope | Motto of [Brown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_University). |
| *[in dubio pro reo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_dubio_pro_reo)* | in doubt, on behalf of the \[alleged\] culprit | Expresses the judicial principle that in case of doubt the decision must be in favor of the accused (in that anyone is innocent until there is proof to the contrary). |
| *in duplo* | in double | In duplicate |
| *in effigie* | in the likeness | In (the form of) an image; in effigy (as opposed to "in the flesh" or "in person"). |
| *in esse* | in existence | In actual existence; as opposed to *in posse*. |
| *in extenso* | in the extended | In full; at full length; complete or unabridged |
| *in extremis* | in the furthest reaches | At the very end. In extremity; in dire straits; also "at the point of death" (cf. *in articulo mortis*). |
| *in facie* | in the face | Refers to [contempt of court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_court) committed in open court in front of the judge; contrast *[ex facie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex_facie)*. |
| *in fide scientiam* | To our faith add knowledge | Motto of [Newington College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newington_College). |
| *in fidem* | into faith | To the verification of faith. |
| *in fieri* | in becoming | In progress; pending. |
| *in fine* (*i.f.*) | in the end | At the end. Used in footnotes, for example, "p. 157 *in fine*": "the end of page 157". |
| *[in flagrante delicto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_flagrante_delicto)* | in a blazing wrong, while the crime is blazing | Caught in the act (esp. a crime or in a "compromising position"); equivalent to "caught red-handed" in English idiom. |
| *in flore* | in blossom | Blooming. |
| *in foro* | in forum | In court ([legal term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_legal_Latin_terms)). |
| *[in forma pauperis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_forma_pauperis)* | in the character or manner of a pauper |  |
| *in girum imus nocte et consumimur igni* | We enter the circle at night and are consumed by fire | A [palindrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palindrome) said to describe the behavior of moths. Also the title of a film by [Guy Debord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Debord). |
| *in harmonia progressio* | progress in harmony | Motto of [Bandung Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandung_Institute_of_Technology), Indonesia. |
| *in hoc sensu*, or *in sensu hoc* (*s.h.*) | in this sense | Recent academic abbreviation for "in this sense". |
| *[in hoc signo vinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_hoc_signo_vinces)* | by this sign you will conquer | Words which [Constantine the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine_the_Great) claimed to have seen in a vision before the [Battle of the Milvian Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Milvian_Bridge). |
| *in hunc effectum* | for this purpose | Describes a meeting called for a particular stated purpose only. |
| *[in ictu oculi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_ictu_oculi)* | in the blink of an eye |  |
| *in illo ordine* (*i.o.*) | in that order | Recent academic substitution for the spacious and inconvenient "..., respectively". |
| *in illo tempore* | in that time | At that time, or in those days, often used at the start of a liturgical scripture reading to mark an undetermined time in the past or to replace contextual material which is not being read.[^7639] |
| *in inceptum finis est* | lit.: in the beginning is the end | or: the beginning foreshadows the end |
| *in limine* | at the outset/threshold | Preliminary, in law, a [motion in limine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_in_limine) is a [motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_%28legal%29) that is made to the judge before or during trial, often about the admissibility of evidence believed prejudicial. |
| *in loco* | in the place, on the spot | That is, 'on site', e.g. "The nearby labs were closed for the weekend, so the water samples were analyzed *in loco*." |
| *[in loco parentis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_loco_parentis)* | in the place of a parent | Assuming parental or custodial responsibility and authority (e.g., [schoolteachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schoolteacher) over students); a legal term. |
| *in luce Tua videmus lucem* | in Thy light we see light | Motto of [Valparaiso University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valparaiso_University). The phrase comes from [Psalm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Psalms) 36:9: "For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light." |
| *in lumine tuo videbimus lumen* | in your light we will see the light | Motto of [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University) New York City, [Presbyterian Boys' Senior High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterian_Boys'_Senior_High_School) Ghana, [Ohio Wesleyan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Wesleyan_University), [University of Fort Hare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Fort_Hare) South Africa |
| *in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum* | into your hands I entrust my spirit | According to [Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Luke) 23:46, the last words of [Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus) on the cross |
| *[in medias res](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_medias_res)* | into the middle of things | From [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace). Refers to the literary technique of beginning a narrative in the middle of, or at a late point in, the story, after much action has already taken place. Examples include the *[Iliad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iliad)*, the *[Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odyssey)*, *[Os Lusíadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Os_Lus%C3%ADadas)*, *[Othello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Othello)*, and *[Paradise Lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise_Lost)*. Compare *ab initio*. |
| *in memoriam* | into the memory | Equivalent to "in the memory of". Refers to remembering or honoring a deceased person. |
| *[in natura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_natura)* | in nature |  |
| *[in necessariis unitas, in dubiis libertas, in omnibus caritas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_necessariis_unitas,_in_dubiis_libertas,_in_omnibus_caritas)* | in necessary things unity, in doubtful things liberty, in all things charity | "[Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charity_%28virtue%29)" (*caritas*) is being used in the classical sense of "compassion" (cf. *[agape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agape)*). Motto of the [Cartellverband der katholischen deutschen Studentenverbindungen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartellverband_der_katholischen_deutschen_Studentenverbindungen). Often misattributed to [Augustine of Hippo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustine_of_Hippo). |
| *in nocte consilium* | advice comes in the night; "sleep on it" | Motto of [Birkbeck College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birkbeck,_University_of_London), University of London, an evening higher-education institution[^7640] |
| *in nomine diaboli* | in the name of the devil |  |
| *[in nomine Domini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_nomine_Domini)* | in the name of the Lord | Motto of [Trinity College, Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_College,_Perth), Australia; the name of a 1050 [papal bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_bull) |
| *in nomine patris, et filii, et spiritus sancti* | in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit | Invocation of the [Holy Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Trinity); part of the Latin Mass |
| *in nuce* | in a nut | in a nutshell; briefly stated; potential; in the embryonic phase |
| *[in odium fidei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_odium_fidei)* | in hatred of the faith | Used in reference to the deaths of some [Christian martyrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_martyrs) in Catholicism |
| *in omnia paratus* | ready for anything | Motto of the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army)'s [18th Infantry Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_Infantry_Regiment_%28United_States%29) |
| *in omnibus amare et servire Domino* | in everything, love and serve the Lord | The motto of [Ateneo de Iloilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Iloilo), a school in the Philippines |
| *in omnibus requiem quaesivi, et nusquam inveni nisi in angulo cum libro* | Everywhere I have searched for peace and nowhere found it, except in a corner with a book | Quote by [Thomas à Kempis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_%C3%A0_Kempis) |
| *in ovo* | in the egg | An experiment or process performed in an egg or embryo (e.g. in ovo electroporation of chicken embryo). |
| *in pace ut sapiens aptarit idonea bello* | in peace, like the wise man, make preparations for war | [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace), [*Satires*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satires_%28Horace%29) 2/2:111; similar to *[si vis pacem, para bellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Si_vis_pacem,_para_bellum)* and [*igitur qui desiderat pacem, praeparet bellum*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Latin_phrases_%28full%29). |
| [*in pace requiescat*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Requiescat_in_pace) | in peace may he rest | Alternate form of *requiescat in pace* ("let him rest in peace"). Found in this form at the end of [The Cask of Amontillado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cask_of_Amontillado) by [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe). |
| *in pari materia* | upon the same matter or subject | In [statutory interpretation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statutory_interpretation), when a statute is ambiguous, its meaning may be determined in light of other statutes on the same subject matter. |
| *[in pari delicto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_pari_delicto)* | in equal fault |  |
| *[in partibus infidelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_partibus_infidelium)* | in the parts of the infidels | "In the land of the [infidels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infidel)"; used to refer to bishoprics that remain as [titular sees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titular_see) even after the corresponding territory was conquered, usually by Muslim rulers. |
| *[in pectore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_pectore)* | in the heart | A [cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_%28Catholicism%29) named in secret by the [pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope). See also *ab imo pectore*. |
| *[In persona episcopi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_persona_episcopi)* | in the person of the bishop | Form of [Catholic diocesan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_diocese) union where one bishop administers several dioceses while they remain canonically distinct. |
| *[in personam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_personam)* | against a person | Directed towards a particular person |
| *in posse* | in potential | In the state of being possible; as opposed to *in esse*. |
| *in propria persona* | in one's own person | For one's self, for the sake of one's [personhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personhood); acting on one's own behalf, especially a person representing themselves in a legal proceeding; abbreviated *pro per*. See also *pro se*: [litigant in person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litigant_in_person), [*pro se* legal representation in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_se_legal_representation_in_the_United_States).[^7641] |
| *in principio erat Verbum* | in the beginning was the Word ([Logos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logos_%28Christianity%29)) | Beginning of the Gospel of John |
| *[in re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_re)* | in the matter \[of\] | Legal term used to indicate that a judicial proceeding may not have formally designated adverse parties or is otherwise uncontested. The term is commonly used in case citations of [probate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probate) proceedings, for example, *In re Smith's Estate*; it is also used in [juvenile courts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juvenile_court), as, for instance, *[In re Gault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_re_Gault)*. |
| *in rebus* | in the thing \[itself\] | Primarily of philosophical use to discuss properties and property exemplification. In [philosophy of mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_mathematics), it is typically contrasted with "ante rem" and, more recently, "post res" [structuralism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structuralism_%28philosophy_of_mathematics%29). Sometimes *in re* is used in place of *in rebus*. |
| *in regione caecorum rex est luscus* | In the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is king. | Quote of [Desiderius Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desiderius_Erasmus) from *[Adagia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adagia)* (first published 1500, with numerous expanded editions through 1536), III, IV, 96. |
| *[in rem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_rem)* | against the thing | Legal term indicating a court's jurisdiction over a piece of [property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property) rather than a [legal person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_personality); contrast with [personal (*ad personam*) jurisdiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_jurisdiction). See [In rem jurisdiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_rem_jurisdiction); [Quasi in rem jurisdiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasi_in_rem_jurisdiction) |
| *in rerum natura* | in the nature of things | See also [Lucretius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucretius)' *[De rerum natura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_rerum_natura)* (*On the Nature of Things*). |
| *in retentis* | among things held back | Used to describe documents kept separately from the regular records of a court for special reasons. |
| *in saecula* (*saeculorum*), *in saeculum saeculi* | *roughly*: down to the times of the times | forever (and ever); liturgical |
| *in saeculo* | in the times | In the [secular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularism) world, esp. outside a [monastery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monastery), or before death. |
| *in salvo* | in safety |  |
| *in scientia et virtue* | in knowledge and virtue | Motto of [St. Joseph's College, Colombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph's_College,_Colombo), Colombo. Sri Lanka |
| *in se magna ruunt* | great things collapse of their own weight | [Lucan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucan), *[Pharsalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharsalia)* 1:81 |
| *in silvam non ligna feras* | Do not carry wood to the forest | [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace), *[Satires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satires_%28Horace%29)* 1:10 |
| *[in situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ)* | in the place | In the original place, appropriate position, or natural arrangement. |
| *in somnis veritas* | In dreams there is truth |  |
| *in spe* | in hope | "future" ("my mother-in-law *in spe*", i.e. "my future mother-in-law"), or "in embryonic form", as in "[Locke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Locke)'s theory of government resembles, *in spe*, [Montesquieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montesquieu)'s theory of the separation of powers." |
| *in specialibus generalia quaerimus* | To seek the general in the specifics | That is, to understand the most general rules through the most detailed analysis. |
| *in statu nascendi* | in the state of being born | Just as something is about to begin |
| *in theatro ludus* | like a scene in a play | Surreal |
| *in toto* | in all | Totally; entirely; completely. |
| *in triplo* | in triple | In triplicate. |
| *in umbra, igitur, pugnabimus* | Then we will fight in the shade | [Laconic phrase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laconic_phrase) supposedly given by the Spartans in response to the Persian boast at the [Battle of Thermopylae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Thermopylae) that their arrows would obscure the sun. The response, though not in this form, was variously attributed to the soldier [Dienekes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dienekes) or to King [Leonidas I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonidas_I). |
| *in utero* | in the womb |  |
| *in utrumque paratus* | prepared for either (event) |  |
| *in vacuo* | in a void | In a vacuum; isolated from other things. |
| *[in varietate concordia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_varietate_concordia)* | united in diversity | The motto of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) |
| *in verbo tuo* | at your word | a reference to the response of [Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter) when he was invited by Jesus to "Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch" (Luke 5:4-5). |
| *invidiae prudentia victrix* | prudence conquers jealousy |  |
| *[in vino veritas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vino_veritas)* | in wine \[there is\] truth | That is, wine loosens the tongue (referring to [alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_%28drug%29)'s disinhibitory effects). |
| *[in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro)* | in glass | An experimental or process methodology performed in a "non-natural" setting (e.g. in a laboratory using a glass test tube or Petri dish), and thus outside of a living organism or cell. Alternative experimental or process methodologies include *in vitro*, *ex vivo* and *in vivo*. |
| *[in vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vivo)* | in life/in a living thing | An experiment or process performed on a living specimen. |
| *in vivo veritas* | in a living thing \[there is\] truth | An expression used by [biologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biologist) to express the fact that laboratory findings from testing an organism *[in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro)* are not always reflected when applied to an organism *[in vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vivo)*. Pun on *[in vino veritas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vino_veritas)*. |
| *incepto ne desistam* | May I not shrink from my purpose! | Motto of [Westville Boys' High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westville_Boys'_High_School) and [Westville Girls' High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westville_Girls'_High_School), from Virgil, *Aeneid*, Book 1. Used by Juno, queen of heaven, who hated the Trojans led by Aeneas. When she saw the fleet of Aeneas on its way to Italy, after the sack of Troy by the Greeks, she planned to scatter it by means of strong winds. In her determination to accomplish her task she cried out "Incepto ne desistam!" |
| *incertae sedis* | of uncertain position (seat) | Term used to classify a taxonomic group when its broader relationships are unknown or undefined. |
| *incredibile dictu* | incredible to say | Variant on *[mirabile dictu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirabile_dictu)*. |
| *intus et in cute* | inwardly and in the skin | Intimately, without reservation. [Persius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persius), *Satire* 3:30. |
| *[Index Librorum Prohibitorum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_Librorum_Prohibitorum)* | Index of prohibited (or, forbidden) books | List of books considered [heretical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heretical) by the [Roman Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church). |
| *indigens Deo* | being in need of God, beggar before God | From [Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustine_of_Hippo), *[De Civitate Dei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_God_%28book%29)* XII, 1.3: *[beatitudinem consequatur nec expleat indigentiam suam](https://web.archive.org/web/20130214070332/http://phil.flet.mita.keio.ac.jp/person/nakagawa/texts/august/cd/cd12.html)*, "[since it is not satisfied unless it be perfectly blessed](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nicene_and_Post-Nicene_Fathers:_Series_I/Volume_II/City_of_God/Book_XII/Chapter_1)". |
| *indignor quandoque bonus dormitat Homerus* | I too am annoyed whenever good Homer falls asleep | [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace), *[Ars Poetica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ars_Poetica_%28Horace%29)* 358 |
| *indivisibiliter ac inseparabiliter* | indivisible and inseparable | [Motto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_mottos) of [Austria-Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria-Hungary) before it was divided and separated into independent states in 1918. |
| *infinitus est numerus stultorum* | unending is the number of fools |  |
| *infirma mundi elegit Deus* | God chooses the weak of the world | The motto of Venerable [Vital-Justin Grandin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vital-Justin_Grandin), the bishop of the St. Albert Diocese, which is now the [Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Edmonton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Edmonton) |
| *infra dignitatem* (*infra dig*) | beneath (one's) dignity |  |
| *ingenio stat sine morte decus* | the honors of genius are eternal | [Propertius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propertius), *Elegies* Book III, 2 |
| *initium sapientiae timor Domini* | the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom | [Psalm 111:10](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible%20%28King%20James%29/Psalms#Psalm_111). Motto of the [University of Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Aberdeen), Scotland. |
| *iniuriae qui addideris contumeliam* | you who have added insult to injury | [Phaedrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phaedrus_%28fabulist%29), *Fables* 5/3:5. |
| *inopiae desunt multa, avaritiae omnia* | to poverty many things are lacking; to avarice, everything | [Publilius Syrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publilius_Syrus). |
| *insita hominibus libidine alendi de industria rumores* | men have an innate desire to propagate rumors or reports | [Titus Livius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titus_Livius) (XXVII, XXIV); [Michel de Montaigne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_de_Montaigne), *Essays*. |
| *instante mense* (*inst.*) | in the present month | Used in formal correspondence to refer to the current month, sometimes abbreviated as *inst*; e.g.: "Thank you for your letter of the 17th inst.", *ult. mense* = last month, *prox. mense* = next month. |
| *[Instrumentum regni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumentum_regni)* | instrument of government | Used to express the exploitation of [religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstition) by [State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_%28polity%29) or [ecclesiastical polity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesiastical_polity) as a means of controlling the masses, or in particular to achieve political and [mundane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_power_%28papal%29) ends. |
| *[Instrumentum vocale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumentum_vocale)* | instrument with voice | So [Varro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varro) in his *De re rustica* (*On Agriculture*) defines the slave: an instrument (as a simple plow, or etc.) with voice. |
| *intaminatis fulget honoribus* | untarnished, she shines with honor | From [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace)'s *Odes* (III.2.18). Motto of [Wofford College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wofford_College). |
| *integer vitae scelerisque purus* | unimpaired by life and clean of wickedness | From [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace)'s *Odes* (I.22.1)[^7642] Used as a funeral hymn. |
| *intelligenti pauca* | few words suffice for him who understands |  |
| *inter alia* (*i.a.*) | among other things |  |
| *inter alios* | among other persons |  |
| *[inter arma enim silent leges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_arma_enim_silent_leges)* | in a time of war, the law falls silent | Said by [Cicero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero) in *[Pro Milone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Milone)* as a protest against unchecked political mobs that had virtually seized control of Rome in the 60s and 50s BC. Famously quoted in the essay *[Civil Disobedience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Disobedience_%28Thoreau%29)* by [Henry David Thoreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_David_Thoreau) as "The clatter of arms drowns out the voice of the law". This phrase has also been jokingly translated as "In a time of arms, the legs are silent." |
| *[inter caetera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_caetera)* | among other (works) | title of a 1493 [papal bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_bull) |
| *inter mutanda constantia* | steadfast in the midst of change | Motto of [Rockwell College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwell_College) in [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland) and [Francis Libermann Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Libermann_Catholic_High_School) in [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada) |
| *inter spem et metum* | between hope and fear |  |
| *inter faeces et urinam nascimur* | we are born between feces and urine | Attributed to [Saint Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustine_of_Hippo). |
| *inter sacrum saxumque* | between the sacrifice and the stone | Being in a dilemma. From [Plautus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plautus), *[Captivi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captivi)*, listed in *[Adagia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adagia)* by [Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus).[^7643] See also: "[between a rock and a hard place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between_a_rock_and_a_hard_place_%28disambiguation%29)", "[between the devil and the deep blue sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between_the_Devil_and_the_Deep_Blue_Sea_%28disambiguation%29)". |
| *[inter vivos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_vivos)* | between the living | Describes property transfers between living persons, as opposed to a [testamentary transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testator) upon death such as an inheritance; often relevant to tax laws. |
| *interna praestant* | what is inside is better | or, virtue/character above all; see: *[prestant interna (coronae)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Latin_phrases_%28P%29)* |
| *intra muros* | within the walls | Not public; source of the word *intramural*. Can also refer to the portion of a city within the city walls (current or past); for example, [Intramuros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intramuros), Manila. |
| *intra vires* | within the powers | Within one's authority. Contrasted with *ultra vires*. |
| *invenias etiam [disiecti membra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disiecta_membra) poetae* | you would still recognize the scattered fragments of a poet | [Horace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace), [*Satires*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satires_%28Horace%29), I, 4, 62, in reference to the earlier Roman poet [Ennius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennius). |
| *inveniet quod quisque velit* | each shall find what he desires | Attributed to [Petronius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petronius)[^7644] or [Prudentius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudentius). Motto of the journal *Nature in Cambridgeshire*:[^7645] *Inveniet quod quisque velit; non omnibus unum est, quod placet; hic spinas colligit, [ille rosas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpe_diem)* ("Each shall find what he desires; no one thing pleases all; one gathers thorns, another roses"). |
| *invicta* | unconquered | Motto of the English county of [Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent) and the city of [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto) |
| *invictus maneo* | I remain unvanquished | Motto of the [Armstrong clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan_Armstrong) |
| *Iohannes est nomen eius* | John is his name | [Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Luke) 1:63, referring to [John the Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_the_Baptist). Motto of the [coat of arms of Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Puerto_Rico). |
| *ipsa scientia potestas est* | knowledge itself is power | Famous phrase written by Sir [Francis Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Bacon) in 1597 |
| *[ipse dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipse_dixit)* | he himself said it | Commonly said in Medieval debates and referring to [Aristotle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristotle). Used in general to emphasize that some assertion comes from some authority, i.e., as an [argument from authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument_from_authority), and the term *ipse-dixitism* has come to mean any unsupported rhetorical assertion that lacks a logical argument. Literal translation by [Cicero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero) (in his *[De Natura Deorum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Natura_Deorum)* 1.10) of the Greek *αὐτὸς ἔφα*, an invocation by [Pythagoreans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythagoreans) when appealing to the pronouncements of the master. |
| *[ipsissima verba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsissima_verba)* | the very words themselves | "Strictly word for word" (cf. *verbatim*). Often used in Biblical Studies to describe the record of Jesus' teaching found in the New Testament (specifically, the four Gospels). |
| *ipsissima voce* | in the very voice itself | To approximate the main thrust or message without using the exact words |
| *[ipso facto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipso_facto)* | by the fact itself | By that very fact |
| *[ipso jure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipso_jure)* | by the law itself | Automatically as a consequence of law |
| *ira deorum* | wrath of the gods | Like the vast majority of inhabitants of the ancient world, the [ancient Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome) practiced [pagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paganism) rituals, believing it important to achieve a state of *pax deorum* (peace of the gods) instead of *ira deorum* (wrath of the gods): earthquakes, floods, famine, etc. |
| *ira furor brevis est* | wrath (anger) is but a brief madness |  |
| *ita vero* | thus indeed | Useful phrase, as the Romans had no word for "yes", preferring to respond to questions with the affirmative or negative of the question (e.g., "Are you hungry?" was answered by "I am hungry" or "I am not hungry", not "yes" or "no"). |
| *[ite, missa est](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ite,_missa_est)* | go, it is the dismissal | Loosely: "You have been dismissed". Concluding words addressed to the people in the [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_%28liturgy%29) of the [Roman Rite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Rite).[^7646] The term *missa* "Mass" derives from a reanalysis of the phrase to mean "Go, the *missa* is accomplished." |
| *iter legis* | the path of the law | The path a law takes from its conception to its implementation |
| *iucunda memoria est praeteritorum malorum* | pleasant is the memory of past troubles | [Cicero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicero), *[De finibus bonorum et malorum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_finibus_bonorum_et_malorum)* 2, 32, 105 |
| *iugulare mortuos* | to cut the throat of corpses | From Gerhard Gerhards' (1466-1536) (better known as [Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus)) collection of annotated *Adagia* (1508). It can mean attacking the work or personality of deceased person. Alternatively, it can be used to describe criticism of an individual already heavily criticised by others. |
| *iuncta iuvant* | together they strive | also spelled *juncta juvant*; from the legal principle *quae non valeant singula, iuncta iuvant* ("What is without value on its own, helps when joined") |
| *[iura novit curia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iura_novit_curia)* | the court knows the law | Legal principle in civil law countries of the Roman-German tradition that says that lawyers need not argue the law, as that is the office of the court. Sometimes miswritten as *iura novat curia* (the court renews the laws). |
| [*iure matris*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jure_matris) | in right of his mother | Indicates a right exercised by a son on behalf of his mother |
| [*iure uxoris*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jure_uxoris) | in right of his wife | Indicates a right exercised by a husband on behalf of his wife |
| *iuris ignorantia est cum ius nostrum ignoramus* | it is ignorance of the law when we do not know our own rights |  |
| *ius accrescendi* | right of accrual | Commonly referred to as "right of survivorship": a rule in property law that surviving joint tenants have rights in equal shares to a decedent's property |
| *ius ad bellum* | law towards war | Refers to the laws that regulate the reasons for going to war. Typically, this would address issues of self-defense or preemptive strikes. |
| [*ius cogens*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peremptory_norm) | compelling law | A [peremptory norm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peremptory_norm), a fundamental principle of international law considered to have acceptance among the international community of states as a whole and from which no derogation is permitted. |
| *ius est ars boni et aequi* | the law is the art of goodness and equity | Appears on the front of the Sievekingplatz 2, a courthouse of the [Hanseatisches Oberlandesgericht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanseatisches_Oberlandesgericht), in [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany). |
| *ius in bello* | law in war | Refers to the "laws" that regulate the conduct of combatants during a conflict. Typically, this would address issues of who or what is a valid target, how to treat prisoners, and what sorts of weapons can be used. |
| *[ius primae noctis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ius_primae_noctis)* | law of the first night | The *[droit du seigneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Droit_du_seigneur)*, supposed right of a lord to have sexual relations with a newly married female subject |
| [jus sanguinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jus_sanguinis) | right of blood | A legal doctrine granting citizenship based on the nationality of one's parents |
| [jus soli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jus_soli) | right of the soil | A legal doctrine granting birthright citizenship |
| *iustam causam deus non derelinqvet* | god will not abandon the just cause | Appears on [Francis II Rákóczi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_II_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi)'s flag. |
| *iustitia dilata est iustitia negata* | [justice delayed is justice denied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_delayed_is_justice_denied) | [^7647] |
| *iustitia fundamentum regni* | justice is the foundation of a reign | Motto of the Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office of the Czech Republic. |
| *iustitia nemini neganda est* | justice is to be denied to nobody | [^7648] |
| *iustitia non est neganda, non differenda* | justice is not to be denied, not to be delayed | [^7648] |
| *iustitia omnibus* | justice for all | The motto of [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.) |
| *iuventuti nil arduum* | to the young nothing is difficult | Motto of [Canberra Girls Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Girls_Grammar_School) |
| *iuventutis veho fortunas* | I bear the fortunes of youth | Motto of [Dollar Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_Academy) |

In *[Asinaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asinaria)*, act II, scene IV, verse 89 \[495 overall\]. Lupus est homo homini, non homo, quom qualis sit non novit ("a man to a man is a wolf, not a man, when the other doesn't know of what character he is.")[^7653] |  |

| *lux ex tenebris* | light from darkness | Motto of the [67th Network Warfare Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Network_Warfare_Wing) |  |

| *Lux mentis Lux orbis* | Light of the mind, Light of the world | Motto of [Sonoma State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonoma_State_University) |  |

And there was light). Motto of the [University of Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Washington). |  |
